units.tr: When this book had been read, bishops, abbots, monks and the whole crowd of Antichrist's agents conspired and asked the Elector of Brandenburg to have this book and Luther's other books that had been gathered together consumed by the flames of fire. The same Magdeburg priests asked Count of Stolberg, vicar of the absent Cardinal, to do likewise.

units.la: Respondit etiam VVolfgango Fabritio Capitoni, qui saepius Luthero moderationis autor fuerat, & cujus suasu Archi episcopus Moguntinus amicam ad Lutherum epistolam dederat, nescio quid non de se pollicens. Quantum, inquit, litera Cardinalis tui animum meum erexerunt, tantum litera tua dejecerunt, mi Fabriti. Dejecit forte & vultum tuum exordium hoc triste & ingratum. Sed tua culpa, qui & fidem & autoritatem literis Cardinalis tam intempestiva Rhetorica ademeris. Inter multa enim, quae me moverunt, hoc erat unum, quod scribis, eum juvandarum Evangelii partium diversam à nobis iniisse rationem. Hoc enim quid aliud est, quam tuam aut nostram rationem damnabilem esse: cum necesse sit, ministerium spiritus sibi
units.tr: He also replied to Wolfgang Fabricius Capito, who had often been an advocate of moderation to Luther, and at whose persuasion the Archbishop of Mainz had sent a friendly letter to Luther, promising himself I know not what. As much as your Cardinal's letter lifted my spirit, so much has your letter cast it down, my dear Fabritius. Perhaps this sad and unwelcome beginning has also cast down your countenance. But it is your fault, who by such untimely rhetoric have taken away both the trust and the authority of the Cardinal's letter. For among many things that moved me, this was one: that you write that he has taken a different method from ours of helping the parts of the Gospel. For what else is this than to say that your method or ours is damnable, since it is necessary that the ministry of the Spirit

units.la: ANNUS M D X XII.
units.tr: THE YEAR 1522

units.la: sibi ipsi quàm minimè pugnare? Paulus enim ĭsdem vestigiis incedentem Timotheum Corinthiis commendat. Atqʒ ego quidem pro meo in te cando e verbum hoc diversitatis tuæ aliquâ Ƨπιεικεία lenÿssem, nisi tu ipse tuus interpres sic cœgisses intelligendum, Evangelium tunc promoveri, si Principibus conniveatur, parcatur, eorum facta excusentur, &, ut tua verba sonant: ne procaces ad pugnam provocemus. Hac tua ratio est, quæ juxta nostram rationem pulcra adulatio, & veritatis Christiana abnegatio est, & ipsissima ωε○ζωπολψία, quam scriptura sic detestantur ut nihil vehementius. Ego nec inimicis optârim hunc amicum probari, & tantum abest, ut optem hac tuâ ratione juvari Evangelium, ut nihil vehementius deprecer. Et faxit Christus, non ut nihil promoveas, sed ut servet te nobiscum, ne noceas. Maxsuetudinem & benignitatem Christianam exigis, sed quid Christianis & adulatori? Res aperta est, & simplicissima, Christianismus, rem sicut habet, cognoscit, ita fatetur. Malè valere volunt etiam Gentiles eos amicos, qui vitiis amicorum blandiuntur; & veritas Christi vitiis & impietati simul blandiri poterit? Nos autem nostram quoque rationem exponemus, & cum fiducia sub judicium tuum, & totius orbis proponemus, nihil veriti, quod scribis, offendi vulgi judicium mordacitate. Quem autem non offendebat Christus, aut quem non arguebat? Et si spiritus veritatis arguit, non blanditur. Arguit vero non aliquot, sed totum mundum. Igitur nos sic sapi-mus, omnia prorsus esse reprehendenda, arguen-da, confundenda, nihil parcendum, nihil con-nivendum, nihil excusandum, ut medio stet campo libera, & aperta, & pura veritas. Por-ro aliud est, eos, quos corripueris summâ mansue-tudine suscipere, tolerare, juvare. Hoc jam ad charitatis & officii exemplum pertinet, non ad ministerium verbi. Nam & Christus cum acerrimè omnes argueret, tamen optat gallina illis esse, & sub alis illos colligere: Charitas est, quae omnia sustinet, omnia suffert, omnia sperat. Fides verò, seu verbum prorsus nihil sustinet, sed arguit, devorat, seu ut Ieremias dicit, evellit, destruit, & dissipat. Et maledictus, qui facit opus Domini fraudulenter. Aliud est, inquam, mi Fabriti, vitium laudare, vel extenuare: & aliud, benignè & suaviter curare. Primùm enim dicendum est, quid rectum & non rectum erit: deinde, ubi id auditor susceperit, tolerandus, & ut Paulus ait, infirmus fide suscipiendus. Tua verò ratio id efficit, ut nunquam veritas cognoscatur, & tamen interim blanditiâ & fictâ humanitate praesumatur vitium sanari.
units.tr: Can he really contradict himself so little? For Paul commends Timothy to the Corinthians because he walks in the same footsteps. Indeed, for my part I would have softened the word "difference" in your letter with some [ἐπιείκεια, moderation], had you yourself not compelled it to be understood as your own interpreter: that the gospel is then advanced if the princes are indulged, spared, and their deeds excused, and, as your words sound, that we should not provoke them to quarrelsome strife. This is your method, which by our reckoning is a fine flattery and a denial of Christian truth, and the very [προσωπολημψία, respect of persons], which Scripture so detests that nothing is more vehement. I would not wish this friend upon even my enemies, and I am so far from wishing the gospel to be helped by your method that I pray most vehemently against it. May Christ grant that you advance nothing, but that he keep you with us so that you do no harm. You demand Christian gentleness and benignity, but what has a flatterer to do with Christians? The matter is open and very simple: Christianity knows the thing as it is and confesses it as it is. Even the Gentiles hold that those friends are bad who flatter their friends' vices; can the truth of Christ flatter vice and impiety at the same time? We, however, will set out our own method too, and with confidence we will lay it before your judgment and that of the whole world, fearing nothing from the offence that you say the judgment of the crowd will take at our biting words. Yet whom did Christ not offend, or whom did he not rebuke? And if the Spirit of truth rebukes, it does not flatter. It rebukes not some but the whole world. Therefore we hold this view: that everything must be censured, refuted and confounded, nothing spared, nothing connived at, nothing excused, so that truth may stand free, open and pure on the open field. It is one thing, however, to receive, tolerate and help with the greatest gentleness those whom you have rebuked. This belongs now to the example of charity and duty, not to the ministry of the Word. For Christ, though he argued most sharply against them all, nevertheless wishes to be a hen to them and to gather them under his wings. Charity is what bears all things, endures all things, hopes all things. But faith, or the Word, bears nothing at all; it argues, devours, or, as Jeremiah says, plucks up, destroys and scatters. And cursed is he who does the work of the Lord deceitfully. It is one thing, I say, my dear Fabritius, to praise or extenuate a vice, and quite another to cure it kindly and gently. For first it must be said what is right and what is not right; then, once the hearer has accepted this, he must be tolerated and, as Paul says, received as one weak in faith. Your method, however, brings it about that the truth is never known, and yet in the meantime a vice is presumed to be healed by flattery and feigned humanity.

units.la: Ad Boëmos deinde tertio Kalendas Augusti dat literas, quibus gravissimè eos ad constantiam in agnita veritate cohortatur: & nevanâ spe pacis ab Evangelica puritate ad Papam Antichristum rursus deficiant: dehortatur, ne reos se faciant innocentis sansanguinis Joannis Hussi & Hieronymi Pragensis. Quod autem sectæ illis exprobrantur (erant enim in Boëmia Papistæ, Hussitæ, sive Calixtini, & Fratres, falsò nominati Picardi.) respondet, infinito plures sectas esse inter Papistas, & quomodo huic malo rectè consulatur, docet.
units.tr: Then on the 29th of July he sent letters to the Bohemians, in which he most earnestly exhorts them to constancy in the truth they have come to know, and warns them not to fall back from evangelical purity to the Antichrist the Pope on the vain hope of peace. He dissuades them from making themselves guilty of the innocent blood of John Hus and Jerome of Prague. As for the sects with which they are reproached (for in Bohemia there were Papists, Hussites or Utraquists, and the Brethren, falsely called Picards), he replies that there are infinitely more sects among the Papists, and he teaches how this evil may rightly be remedied.

units.la: Mense Julio Lutherus Henrico Regi respondit calamo asperiore: cuius scripti vehementiam non omnes amici Lutheri probârunt. Erasmus ea de re ita: Si Lutherus collaudato pio Regis studio rem solidis argumentis fortiter peregisset, non violatâ regiâ dignitate, rectius opinor consuluisset suæ causæ. Idem. Quid invitabat Lutherum, ut diceret in libello adversus Regem Angliæ: Veniatis, Domine Henrice, ego docebo vos? Certè Regis libellus Latinè loquebatur, nec inerudite.
units.tr: In July Luther answered King Henry with a harsher pen. Not all of Luther's friends approved the vehemence of this writing. Erasmus says of the matter: If Luther had, after first praising the king's pious zeal, carried on the affair with solid arguments and without violating the royal dignity, he would, I think, have served his cause better. The same: What prompted Luther to say in his pamphlet against the King of England: "Come hither, Lord Henry, and I will teach you"? Certainly the king's book was written in Latin, and not without learning.

units.la: Ut autem Lutherus in Saxonia, ita Zwinglius in Helvetia negotium Christi cordatè egit. Ac primùm causam suam ad Senatum Tigurinum contra Episcopi Constantiensis legatos defendit: deinde cum in Eremum divæ Virginis ad festos Visitationis dies ad concionandum cum M. Conrado Schmidio, & M. Leone vocatus fuisset, scripsit ibi amicam ac piam paraenesin ad communem Helvetiorum civitatem: ne Evangelicæ doctrinæ cursum impediant, nec licitis sacerdotum connubiis sese offendi. patiantur. Scripsit ibidem suo & Fratrum nonnullorum nomine supplicationem ad R. D. Hugonem Episcopum Constantiensem: quâ illum rogant: ne se induci patiatur, ut quicquam in praeiudicium Evangelii promulget: neve scortationis scandalum ultrà ferat, sed presbyteris uxores ducere permittat, aut saltem ad eorum nuptias conniveat. Subscripserunt, M. Balthasar Trachselus, Pastor in Ardsuitiae: M. Georgius Calybeus, pastor VVimigensis: M. VVernerus Steiner, Pastor ex Tugio: M. Leo Judae, Pastor Eremi, sed designatus pastor D. Petri Tiguri: M. Erasmus Schmid, Canonicus Tigurinus: Simon Stumpfius, praedicator in Honeck: Jodocus Kilchmeier Canonicus Lucernensis: Huldricus Pistoris, pastor in Ufer: Caspar Megander, Nosocomii Tigurini, Joannes Faber, & Huldrichus Zwinglius, summi templi Tigurini pastores.
units.tr: Just as Luther did his work of Christ in Saxony, so Zwingli did it wisely in Helvetia. First he defended his cause before the Zurich Senate against the legates of the Bishop of Constance. Then, when he had been invited to preach at the Hermitage of the Blessed Virgin for the feast of the Visitation, along with Master Conrad Schmid and Master Leo, he wrote there a friendly and pious exhortation to the common citizens of Helvetia, that they should not hinder the course of evangelical doctrine, nor allow themselves to be offended by the lawful marriages of priests. He also wrote there, in his own name and that of some of the brethren, a supplication to the Reverend Lord Hugh, Bishop of Constance, in which they ask him not to allow himself to be induced to promulgate anything to the prejudice of the gospel, and not to carry any further the scandal of whoredom, but to permit the elders to take wives, or at least to connive at their marriages. It was signed by Master Balthasar Trachsel, minister at Ardsuitia; Master Georg Kalbeus, minister at Wimmis; Master Werner Steiner, minister from Tugium (Zug); Master Leo Jud, minister of the Hermitage, but designated minister of St. Peter's at Zurich; Master Erasmus Schmid, canon of Zurich; Simon Stumpf, preacher at Höngg; Jodocus Kilchmeier, canon of Lucerne; Huldrych Pfister, minister at Uster; Caspar Megander, of the Zurich hospital; Johannes Faber, and Huldrych Zwingli, ministers of the great church of Zurich.

units.la: Idem Zwinglius vicesimâ secundâ Augusti huius anni ad Paraenesin Episcopi Constantiensis ad senatum Praepositurae Tigurinae (Capitulum vocant) missam, respondit Apologetico, quem Archetelem nuncupavit, hoc est, principium & finem, idque ideo, quod speraret initium & finem, hoc est, summam controversiae, inter ipsos hoc moderato scripto compositum iri. Monet eo libro Episcopum, ne aurem accommodet veri-
units.tr: On the twenty-second of August of this year, the same Zwingli answered, by an Apologetic which he called Archetelem, that is, beginning and end, the admonition of the Bishop of Constance sent to the Senate of the Zurich Provostry (which they call the Chapter). He called it that because he hoped that by this moderate writing the beginning and end, that is, the chief point of the controversy, would be settled between them. In this book he warns the bishop not to lend an ear to the enemies of truth,

units.la: Tom. I. Zwinglii oper. pag. 120.
units.tr: Vol. I of Zwingli's works, p. 120.

units.la: Exstat To. I. oper Zwinglii pag. 124. veritatis oppugnatoribus: & respondet ad LXIX. Articulos, in Parenæsi Episcopi comprehensos: deniq; offert se ad uberiorem in colloquio aliquo declarationem.
units.tr: Vol. I of Zwingli's works, p. 124. and he answers the sixty-nine articles contained in the bishop's admonition; finally he offers himself for a fuller explanation in some conference.

units.la: Uratislaviensibus, ut & aliis purioris doctrinæ cultoribus in ipsa Regis Ludovici aula suscitavit Deus patronum, Illustrissimum Principem Georgium, Marchionem Brandeburgicum, magnum aulæ Regiæ magistrum: qui cum jam tum veritatis Evangelicæ gustum haberet, in benigniorem partem interpretatus est, quæ ad Regem Ludovicum deferebantur, querelas.
units.tr: To the people of Breslau, as also to other lovers of purer doctrine, God raised up a patron in the very court of King Louis, the most illustrious Prince George, Margrave of Brandenburg, great master of the royal household. Since he already had a taste of evangelical truth, he interpreted in a kinder light the complaints that were being brought against King Louis.

units.la: Hic igitur annus initium est reformationis Ecclesiarum in Silesia. Nam & Lignicii sub Duce Friderico circa Pentecosten Fabianus Eckelus, Sebastianus item Schubartus Evangelium prædicarunt: & Carolus Dux Munsterbergensis & Ofnensis scriptis ad Lutherum literis, quid de Papa & eius brutis fulminibus, quibus Georgius Podiebracius, ex quo Carolus ortus, percussus fuisset, sentiret non obscurè significavit. Jucundum autem Christiano homini spectaculum est, quasi coram cernere certantem Christum cum Antichristo. Quicquid enim Papa, quicquid Cæsareani molirentur contra Evangelium, id omne Christus in Evangelii commodum convertit. Bulla Papæ, fulmen Cæsaris, non confternârunt, sed animârunt homines ad Evangelium amplexandum.
units.tr: This year therefore marks the beginning of the reformation of the churches in Silesia. For at Liegnitz, under Duke Frederick, Fabian Eckel and likewise Sebastian Schubart preached the gospel about Pentecost. Duke Charles of Münsterberg and Oels also made clear, in letters to Luther, what he thought of the Pope and his brutal thunderbolts, by which George of Podiebrad, from whom Charles was descended, had been struck. It is a delightful spectacle for a Christian to see, as it were before one's eyes, Christ contending with Antichrist. For whatever the Pope or the Caesarean party might contrive against the gospel, Christ turned it all to the advantage of the gospel. The Papal bull and the Caesar's thunderbolt did not dismay people; they rather encouraged them to embrace the gospel.

units.la: E Nobilitate Germanica acerrimi fidei orthodoxæ propugnatores erant, Ulricus Huttenus, Franciscus à Sickingen, Hartmundus à Cronberg. Huttenus multa pro Luthero contra Papam scripsit.
units.tr: Among the German nobility the most zealous defenders of the orthodox faith were Ulrich von Hutten, Franz von Sickingen and Hartmut von Cronberg. Hutten wrote much for Luther against the Pope.

units.la: Franciscus à Sickingen Theodorum ab Hentschuchsheim, socerum suū, erudit literis, quæ publicatæ, de communione sub utraque specie, de Missa, de Monachis, de invocatione sanctorum, de abrogatione imaginum. Joannes Schwebelius præmittit præfationē, quâ ait: Mirum esse rerum conversionem in hoc tempore: olim à sacerdotibus Laicos didicisse legem Domini: nunc sacerdotibus à Laicis discendum esse. Olim Episcopos gladio verbi usos fuisse ad salutem animarum: nunc eosdem uti gladio corporali ad opprimendum Dei verbum.
units.tr: Franz von Sickingen instructed his father-in-law Dietrich von Hentschuchsheim in letters, which were published, concerning communion under both kinds, the Mass, monks, the invocation of saints, and the abolition of images. Johannes Schwebel prefaced it with a preface, in which he says: It is a remarkable reversal of things in this time: formerly the laity learned the law of the Lord from the priests; now the priests must learn from the laity. Formerly the bishops used the sword of the Word for the salvation of souls; now those same men use the bodily sword to suppress the Word of God.

units.la: Hartmundus à Cronberg, ut superiori anno ad Leonem Papam, ita hoc ad cives Cronebergicos, & Monachos Mendicantes, Luthero argumenta suggerente, scribit, gravissimeq; omnes & singulos ab idolomania Pontificia dehortatur.
units.tr: Hartmut von Cronberg, as in the previous year he wrote to Pope Leo, so now he writes to the citizens of Cronberg and to the mendicant monks, Luther supplying the arguments; and he most earnestly dissuades them all and each one from Papal idolatry.

units.la: ARGENTINÆ vir optimus Matthias Zellius extitit, qui Pontificis autoritatem ausus fuit contemnere, & doctrinâ populo Argentinensi explicare Domini nostri Jesu Christi.
units.tr: At Strasbourg there was an excellent man, Matthias Zell, who dared to despise the authority of the Pope and to expound the doctrine of our Lord Jesus Christ to the people of Strasbourg.

units.la: Magnam
units.tr: Great

units.la: Magnā Resp. Argentinensis eo nomine fortitudinis & constantiæ laudem merita est. Nam undique Pontificiis, ut videbatur, Religionis tum hostibus circum circa cincta, ad pericula quæ expavescere debebat, non extimuit, & cū posset intercedere, noluit: & Zelium passa est, propter innocentiæ & simplicitatis existimationem, in eo, quod bene cooperat, perseverare: & de re ipsa cogitans, quanti momenti ipsa esset, periculorum non maximam rationem habuit. Adversabatur enim huic instituto, quantum potuit, VVilhelmus Episcopus, ex familia Hohensteniorum Comitum: unà cum toto Canonicorum Collegio primariæ ædis: cum omnibus totius urbis, Canonicorum, & Abbatissarum & Monachorum collegiis, quorum interpellationibus dimoveri se de statu suo Argentinenses minimè siverunt. Urbes etiam vicinæ, clientes Archiducum Austriæ: ut Haganoa, Schledstadium, VVeissenburgum, cæteraq; in Alsatia, hoc exemplum aversabantur. Marchiones Badenses, vicini, & his proximi Palatini Comites, majorum suorum atq; parentum ceremonias deserendas non esse ducebant. Tota Lotharingia minabatur, rusticana etiam seditio hunc metum augebat. Et tamen perstitit Respublica, & pericula subire maluit, quàm luci veritatis fenestras suas claudere.
units.tr: For this, the Strasbourg republic deserved great praise for its courage and steadfastness. Surrounded on every side by the Papists, who were then the enemies of the religion, it did not shrink from the dangers it ought to have dreaded, and though it could have intervened, it chose not to. It allowed Zell to suffer, because of his reputation for innocence and simplicity, and it let him persevere in what he had done well. Thinking about the matter itself and how important it was, it gave little weight to the dangers. Bishop Wilhelm, of the family of the counts of Hohenstein, opposed this undertaking as strongly as he could, together with the whole college of canons of the cathedral and all the colleges of canons, abbesses and monks in the city. By their entreaties the Strasbourgers did not allow themselves to be moved from their position. The neighbouring towns, which were clients of the Archdukes of Austria, such as Hagenau, Schlettstadt, Weissenburg and the others in Alsace, opposed this example. The margraves of Baden, their neighbours, and the counts palatine nearby held that the ceremonies of their ancestors and parents must not be abandoned. All Lorraine threatened, and a peasant revolt increased this fear. Yet the republic held firm and preferred to undergo dangers rather than close the windows through which the light of truth shone.

units.la: PRimus igitur in concionibus Ecclesiæ erat Matthias Zellius, cui sese non longo intervallo Symphorianus adiunxerat, presbyter ætate grandis, pastor in æde Martini, quæ illo tempore in foro piscario erat, cui tum adhuc firmâ & recenti memoriâ liberior fuerat initio vivendi ratio, in conviviis hilaris, in rebus periculosis omnium primus. Ubi Rhenus erat altissimus, ibi pede sinistro dimidio extra marginem pontis posito, dextro toto præposito, absque ulla vertigine stabat. In æde primarii templi supra primam fornicem cursu in transennam insiliit, & stans atque erectus, subiectas plateas intuebatur, absque ulla non solùm vertigine, sed etiam vertiginis metu. Hic vir ex primis fuit, qui doctrinam Evangelii amplexus, non absque multorum, propter vitæ mutationem, admiratione: ita, ut quibus primis annis fuerat familiaris, ad se plerosque attraxerit: quos huius exemplo motos, pœnitere vitæ anteactæ statim cœperat. Populares hi magis concionatores erant, quàm literati: sed insignis in Matthia probitas: quibus sese paulo post applicabat Antonius Firnius, pastor tum ad D. Thomam: qui primus in urbe ista sacerdos uxorem duxit. Neque longè ab hoc initio aberant Martinus Bucerus, Capito, qui apud Cardinalem Moguntinensem sem intra cancellos Consiliariorum primas tenebat, & Doctor Caspar Hedio, summi templi Moguntini pastor, qui, simul ac Argentinam anno vicesimo tertio venerunt, firmiora coeperant fundamenta poni Evangelicæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Foremost in the sermons of the church was Matthias Zell, and not long after him Symphorian had joined himself to him. Symphorian was an elder, advanced in years, and minister at the church of St Martin, which at that time stood in the fish market. His manner of life, which had been freer in his early years, was still firmly and freshly remembered: cheerful at feasts, and first of all men in dangerous enterprises. Where the Rhine was deepest, he would stand with his left foot half over the edge of the bridge and his right foot entirely beyond it, without any dizziness. In the cathedral, above the first arch, he leapt onto a crossbeam at a run and, standing upright, looked down at the squares below, with no dizziness and not even fear of dizziness. He was among the first men to embrace the doctrine of the Gospel, and his change of life drew wonder from many; so much so that he attracted to himself most of those with whom he had been intimate in his early years. Moved by his example, they at once began to repent of their former lives. These men were more popular preachers than learned ones, but Matthias was distinguished by his integrity. Soon afterwards Antony Firn joined them; he was then minister at St Thomas's, and he was the first priest in this city to take a wife. Not far from the beginning were Martin Bucer and Capito, who held the first place among the counsellors inside the chancery of the Cardinal of Mainz, and Dr Caspar Hedio, minister of the great church of Mainz. As soon as they came to Strasbourg in the year 1523, they began to lay firmer foundations for the evangelical church.

units.la: AUGUSTÆ Vindelicorum Joannes Froschius, Theologiæ Doctor, Carmelita, inter primos fuit, qui Evangelium sincere prædicarent.
units.tr: At Augsburg, John Frosch, Doctor of Theology and a Carmelite, was among the first who preached the Gospel sincerely.

units.la: NORIMBERGA Andreas Osiander primam concionem puriorem habet die Dominico 23. Februarii de semine.
units.tr: At Nuremberg, Andreas Osiander gave the first purer sermon, on the seed, on Sunday 23 February.

units.la: Ibidem GALLUS KORN, Monachus Franciscanus, cum gustum religionis verae haberet, nec id dissimularet in concionibus, in odium Fratrum venit. Aperienti autem forte Cyprianum occurrit dictum Apostoli Denuntiamus vobis, fratres, in nomine Iesu Christi, ut vos subtrahatis ab omni fratre ambulante inordinatè. 2 Thess. 3, 6. Perculsus hoc effato, cum sensum illius ex Ambrosio didicisset, Monasterium deseruit 12. Junii.
units.tr: In the same place, Gallus Korn, a Franciscan monk, having tasted the true religion and not hiding it in his sermons, came into hatred among the brothers. But when he happened to open Cyprian, he came upon the saying of the Apostle: We command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye withdraw yourselves from every brother that walketh disorderly, 2 Thess. 3:6. Struck by this saying, and having learned its meaning from Ambrose, he left the monastery on 12 June.

units.la: FRANCOFURTI ad Moenum, Dominica Invocavit Hartmannus Ibachius, exul Christi, in Coenobio S. Catharinæ, Amâdo ab Holtzhausen, & Joanne Froschen, Patriciis, Scabinis & Senatoribus, dictiq; Coenobii patronis (connivente Senatu) curantibus, Evangelium pure docere coepit.
units.tr: At Frankfurt am Main, on the Sunday Invocavit, Hartmann Ibach, an exile for Christ, began to teach the Gospel purely in the convent of St Catherine. It was done with the care of Amadeus von Holzhausen and John Frosch, patricians, scabins and senators, and patrons of the convent, while the Senate looked the other way.

units.la: VVEISSENBURGI (oppidum est in Alsatiæ & Palatinatûs confinio) Henricus Mothererus Pastor evangelizat, à quo Martinus Bucerus, qui impetratâ à Francisco Sickingensi propter tumultus belli aliquantisper se cedendi veniâ, VVittebergam cogitabat, invitatus, dimidiûq; ibi annum subsistens, ad D. Joannem prædicavit. Sed à Vicario Spirensi uterq; inde pulsus est. Bucerus sub initium anni 1523. Argentinam venit, editâq; summâ eorum, quç VVeissenburgi docuerat, in veritate Evangelica animos civium mirificè confirmavit.
units.tr: At Weissenburg (a town on the border of Alsace and the Palatinate), Henry Motherer, a minister, preached the Gospel. Invited by him, Martin Bucer, who had obtained leave from Francis of Sickingen to withdraw for a while because of the disturbances of war, was planning to go to Wittenberg. He stayed there for half a year and preached at St John's. But both were driven out from there by the vicar of Speyer. Bucer came to Strasbourg at the beginning of the year 1523, and by publishing the substance of what he had taught at Weissenburg in the evangelical truth, he wonderfully strengthened the minds of the citizens.

units.la: HALAM Suevorum de consilio D. Joannis Isenmanni vocatur Joannes Brentius ex Academia Heidelbergensi, ubi in contubernio Realium Matthæum Evangelistam in frequenti auditorio explicârat, hausto sincerioris doctrinæ lacte ex pectore Lutheri anno 1518. Heidelbergæ de Justificatione disputantis. Specimen pro publica concione edit viii. Septembris. Nec quicquam in eo, nisi grandior ætas, desideratum. Natus enim tantum erat annos viginti tres. Etsi igitur iuvenis erat: tamen gravitate, vita sanctimoniâ, morum integritate, quoque officium sibi demandatum, ad quod divinitus erat vocatus, fideliter, & cum autoritate faceret, tantum per Dei gratiam effecit, ne quis propter iuventutem eum contemneret, sed ut omnium non solum
units.tr: At Halle in Swabia, on the advice of Dr John Isenmann, John Brenz was called from the Academy of Heidelberg, where, in the company of the Realists, he had expounded the Gospel of Matthew to a crowded audience, having drunk the milk of purer doctrine from the breast of Luther in the year 1518, when Luther disputed at Heidelberg on justification. He published a specimen for a public sermon on 8 September. Nothing was lacking in him except greater age, for he was only twenty-three years old. Yet although he was young, by his gravity, the holiness of his life and the integrity of his conduct, and by performing faithfully and with authority the office entrusted to him, to which he had been called by God, he achieved so much by the grace of God that no one despised him on account of his youth; but he turned to himself the eyes and ears of all, not only

units.la: Verba Herbrandi. solùm ora & oculos in se converteret, verùm animos etiam verbo Dei inclinaret, quò pristinis erroribus & doctrinis Scribarum & Pharisaorū, quos secum hactenus aluerant, valedicerent, qui & ipsi paulo post partim iniussi, quòd sua execrata sacra in vacuo theatro, ab auditoribus & spectatoribus destituti, facere erubescentes, in alia se contulère loca, partim verò conversi, partim etiam morte sunt abrepti. Magna autem in concionibus popularibus usus est prudentiâ & modestiâ, initio cum haberet adversarios vehementissimos, inter quos præcipui erant Guardianus, Theologia Licentiatus, & Lector Monasterii ordinis Minorum, qui conspirantes saviebant importunis suis clamoribus, & Sophisticâ errores suos defendentes. Quæ cum indesinenter facerent fulminando, & virus suum evomendo, Dominicis & festis diebus, matutinis concionibus in magna populi frequentia: à prandio multò confluebant frequentius, sperantes Ecclesiasten suum eâdem usurum vehementiâ in suorum dogmatum defensione, & par pari relaturum. Verùm ille prudenter dissimulabat ad tempus, & suo more docere pergebat, doctrina Christiana fundamenta iaciendo, meritumque Christi unici redemptoris fide apprehendendum, sedulò & fideliter inculcabat: deinde ubi commoda se offerebat occasio, brevissimè & modestè, perspicuis sacræ scripturæ testimoniis adversariorum dogmata & clamores, hac pugnare cum illis, ostendens,
units.tr: The words of Herbrand. not only the mouths and eyes, but also the minds of all he inclined to the word of God, so that they bid farewell to their former errors and to the doctrines of the scribes and Pharisees which they had until then nourished. These men themselves soon afterwards, some without being ordered to, since they were ashamed to perform their accursed rites in an empty theatre, deprived of hearers and spectators, withdrew to other places; others, however, were converted, and some were carried off by death. Brenz used great prudence and moderation in his sermons to the people, although at first he had very fierce opponents, among whom the chief were the guardian, a licentiate in theology, and the lector of the monastery of the Order of Friars Minor. They conspired and raged with their importunate clamours, and defended their errors with sophistry. While they did this without ceasing, thundering and vomiting out their venom, on Sundays and feast days the crowds at the morning sermons, and even more after dinner, flocked together in large numbers, hoping that their preacher would use the same vehemence in defending their dogmas and would repay like with like. But he prudently dissembled for the time being, and went on teaching in his own way, laying the foundations of Christian doctrine and diligently and faithfully urging that the merit of Christ, the only redeemer, be grasped by faith. Then, when a convenient opportunity presented itself, he briefly and modestly showed, by clear testimonies of Holy Scripture, how the dogmas and clamours of the opponents fight against these things,

units.la: Ita ut tandem plerique Papisticam idolomaniam, dogmata & superstitiones detestarentur. Interea ipse quoque Missam celebrabat, sed non pro defunctis offerebat, verùm tantùm Angelicam, quam sic vocant, legebat Missam.
units.tr: So that at last most people detested Papistical idolatry, dogmas and superstitions. Meanwhile he himself also celebrated Mass, but he did not offer it for the dead; he only read what they call the Angelic Mass.

units.la: In regione <bl>GREICHGÆA</bl>, ad Neccanorum sita, hoc & superiori anno 1521. errores & idola Pontificia primi voce Evangelii taxare & abolere cœperunt, Erhardus Snepffius, qui in oppido Guteberga, sub ditione & patrocinio Theodorici Gemmingen, & postea VVimpinæ, femina verae Evangelii doctrinæ sparsit: M. Bernhardus Grublerus, Gemmingæ: M. Martinus Germanus Furfeldæ: & Joannes Gallus Solisfeldiæ. Hos sequuti sunt VVolffgangus Bufius, Gemmingensis Ecclesiæ Pastor, & collega ipsius, Franciscus Irenicus, qui Germaniam descripsit. Docuerunt eodem tempore in vicinis oppidis M. Joannes Rudolphi, & Matthæus Chytræus, Davidis Pater, Menzingiæ: Nicolaus Trabantius Flehingæ: & postea Joannes Siderocrates, Brettæ: Georgius junior, M. Petrus Erberman, & Thomas Rana, in oppido Eppingen. M. Melchior Hipporius (qui primùm Academiæ Regiomontanæ initia docendo adiuvit) in oppido Bischoffsheim.
units.tr: In the region of Greichgau, which lies along the Neckar, in this year and in the previous year 1521, the first to begin to censure and abolish Papal errors and idols by the voice of the Gospel were: Erhard Schnepf, who spread the true doctrine of the Gospel in the town of Gutenberg under the lordship and patronage of Dietrich von Gemmingen, and afterwards at Wimpfen; Master Bernhard Gröbler at Gemmingen; Master Martin Germanus at Fürfeld; and John Gallus at Sulzfeld. They were followed by Wolfgang Buss, minister of the church of Gemmingen, and his colleague Francis Irenicus, who wrote a description of Germany. At the same time, in the neighbouring towns, Master John Rudolphi and Matthew Chytraeus, father of David, taught at Menzingen; Nicholas Trabant at Flehingen; and afterwards John Siderocrates at Bretten; George the younger, Master Peter Erberman and Thomas Rana in the town of Eppingen; and Master Melchior Hipporius (who had first helped to establish the Academy of Königsberg by teaching) in the town of Bischofsheim.

units.la: BREMENSIS civitas inter cæteras Saxoniæ inferioris urbes, prima mutationem ReliReligionis admisit, ubi hoc anno, rogatu Henrici Efichii Senatoris, Eberhardi Speckhanii, & aliorum Patriciorum, permissu Senatûs, Henricus Sutphaniensis, Monachus Augustinianus, recens Antuerpiâ ex adversariorum manibus elapsus, primùm in sacello prope S. Ansgarium, deinde in templo Ansgarii biennium concionatus est. Conticescebant enim Canonici, quod in loco sacro per tumultum civis quidam vulneratus, eoque templum interdicto Ecclesiastico subiectum esset. Quàmprimum autem Clerus animadvertit, Henricum sibi plausum populi conciliare, rogarique ut maneret, indignari coepit, & primò Magistratum, ne in urbe ferret hæreticum, qui doceret contra Ecclesiam, & cum hoc illi non persuaderet, Archiepiscopum Christophorum, ut se interponeret, precibus fatigare: Archiepiscopus monachum sibi tradi per legatos frustra postulabat, tandemque ut eum condemnaret, Concilium provinciale Buxtehudæ indicebat: Henrico doctrinæ suæ defensionem ex sacris literis offerente, & emendationem pollicente, si erroris convinceretur,
units.tr: The city of Bremen, among the other cities of Lower Saxony, was the first to admit a change of religion. There, this year, at the request of the senator Henry Efich, Eberhard Speckhan and other patricians, and with the permission of the Senate, Henry of Zutphen, an Augustinian monk, who had only just escaped from the hands of his opponents at Antwerp, preached for two years, first in a chapel near St Ansgar's and then in the church of St Ansgar. The canons were silent, because a certain citizen had been wounded in a tumult in a sacred place, and the church was therefore subject to an ecclesiastical interdict. But as soon as the clergy noticed that Henry was winning the applause of the people and that they were asking him to stay, they began to be indignant. First they wearied the magistrate, begging that it should not tolerate in the city a heretic who taught against the Church; and when they could not persuade the magistrate of this, they wearied the archbishop Christopher, asking him to intervene. The archbishop demanded in vain through envoys that the monk be handed over to him; and at last, in order to condemn him, he called a provincial council at Buxtehude. Henry offered to defend his teaching from Holy Scripture, and promised to amend it if he were shown to be in error.

units.la: MAGDEBURGÆ Melchior Miricius, Theologiæ Doctor, Augustinianus, & alii purius docere, & Pontificias invocationes Sanctorum, fiduciam operum humanorum. vota Monachorum, sacrificia Missæ privatæ, purgatorium, taxare hoc anno cœperunt.
units.tr: At Magdeburg, Melchior Miricius, Doctor of Theology and an Augustinian, along with others, began this year to teach more purely and to censure the Papists' invocation of saints, the trust in human works, the vows of monks, the private Masses of the sacrificing priests, and purgatory.

units.la: SERVESTÆ Anhaldinorum Dominicâ Cantate Martinus Lutherus in Augustinianorum Monasterio, (Nosocomium hodie est) primam concionem habet Evangelicam. Ab hoc tempore celebris hæc urbs Papatui valedixit.
units.tr: At Servesta in Anhalt, on the Sunday Cantate, Martin Luther preached his first evangelical sermon in the Augustinian monastery (today it is a hospital). From this time this famous city bade farewell to the papacy.

units.la: MILTEBURGI ad Mœnum sub ditione Moguntina Joannes Draco Carlstadius Theologiæ Doctor, Christi crucem & gloriam volentibus annuntiat, non sine fremitu sacrificulorum missaticorum.
units.tr: At Milteburg on the Main, under the rule of Mainz, Johann Draco Carlstadt, Doctor of Theology, proclaimed the cross and glory of Christ to those willing to hear it, not without the growling of the Mass-priests.

units.la: In POMERANIA cum deserbuisset persequutio Treptoviæ mota, & Princeps Bogislaus, etsi edictum VVormatiense in Pomerania ordinib. promulgaverat, tamen executionem non admodū severè urgeret, dehortantibus eū Valentino Stoicentino, & Jacobo Wobeser, & aliis piis ac eruditis Consiliariis, qui puriorem doctrinam amabant: STETTINENSES omniū primi VVittebergâ Doctores Evangelicos, Paulum à Rheda Quedliburgensem, & M. Nicolaum Curiensem accerciverunt. SUNDII etiam, Christianus Kettelhut, Treptoviâ pulsus, taxare Religionis Pōtificiæ vanitatem & superstitiones coepit. Sic connivente Bogislao, Evangelii femina, paulatim in Pomerania, extremo vitæ illius tempore, spargebantur. Ipse Noribergā ad
units.tr: In Pomerania, when the persecution had broken out at Treptow, and Duke Bogislaus, although he had published the Edict of Worms throughout Pomerania for the estates, did not press its enforcement very harshly, being dissuaded by Valentin Stoicentinus, Jacob Wobeser and other pious and learned counsellors who loved a purer doctrine, the people of Stettin, first of all, summoned from Wittenberg the evangelical teachers Paul von Rheda of Quedlinburg and Master Nicholas of Curia. At Stralsund also, Christian Kettelhut, driven out of Treptow, began to censure the vanity and superstitions of the Papist religion. Thus, with Bogislaus conniving, the seeds of the Gospel were gradually scattered in Pomerania during the last period of his life. He himself, setting out from Nuremberg to the Diet,

units.la: Chytraeus. Ex Actis publicis. ad Comitia profectus, etsi Ferdinandus, Caroli Imperatoris frater & locū tenens, denuò controversiam cū Marchione cognoscebat: tamen re non compositâ rediit, ac in itinere cum Electore Saxoniæ Friderico egit, ut filio suo Barnimo, sororis Friderici & Henrici Luneburgensis filia, Anna, connubio iungeretur. Interea Sundii quidam ex sece vulgi & opificum, invito & repugnante Senatu, imagines ex templis seditiosè eiecerant, & Sacerdotes ac Monachos omnes unà die ex urbe fugârant. Et in Belbugiensi cœnobio Monachi ipsi superstitiones veteres abiecerant. Itaque in patriam reversus, & à sacrificulis incitatus, Abbatem captum postea ex ditione proscripsit (qui prope V Vittebergam deinceps in oppido Belzig pastoris officium gessit.) & cœnobium una cum reditibus omnibus suo præfecto administrandum tradidit. Id primum initium occupandi Monasteria in Pomerania fuit. Sundensibus etiam graviter ob iniuriam, non religioni solum & Ecclesiæ, verùm etiam sibi, patrono illatam, comminatus est. Sed statim in tabem lentam & lethalem incidit, quâ prid. Kalend. Octobr. extinctus est: duobus filiis, Georgio & Barnimo relictis, qui in gubernatione ipsi successerunt.
units.tr: Chytraeus. From the public records. Although Ferdinand, brother of Emperor Charles and his deputy, again examined the dispute with the Margrave, he returned without the matter being settled, and on the journey he urged Elector Frederick of Saxony that his son Barnim be joined in marriage to Anna, the daughter of Frederick's sister and of Henry of Lüneburg. Meanwhile some men of Stralsund, from the common folk and craftsmen, against the will and resistance of the Senate, had seditiously cast the images out of the churches and had driven all the priests and monks out of the city in one day. And in the Belbuck monastery the monks themselves had cast off the old superstitions. So the Duke, returning to his lands and roused by the sacrificing priests, later banished the abbot, who had been seized (he afterwards served as pastor in the town of Belzig near Wittenberg), and handed the monastery over, together with all its revenues, to be administered by his own steward. This was the first beginning of seizing the monasteries in Pomerania. He also threatened the men of Stralsund with serious penalties for the wrong done, not only to religion and the Church but also to himself, their patron. But he soon fell into a slow and deadly wasting sickness, of which he died on 30 September, leaving two sons, Georg and Barnim, who succeeded him in the government.

units.la: Stolpæ vero (quam Eoæ Pomeraniæ metropolin ad fl. eiusdem nominis sitam, bonorum ingeniorum feracem, honestâ gubernatione, civium frequentiâ & commerciis, & Ecclesiâ & schola benè constitutâ, hoc tempore florere cernimus) prima purioris doctrinæ semina sparsit Petrus Suavenius, vir nobilis, in ea urbe natus, & Luthero familiaris & charus, qui in privata ad forum domo, civibus aliquot literatis & scholæ præceptoribus Pauli ad Romanos epistolam interpretatus est. Ab hoc excitati scholæ moderatores, studia sacrarum literarum non modò apud Scholasticos urgebant, verùm etiam concionibus, in schola habendis, plurimos ad purioris doctrinæ studium invitabant.
units.tr: At Stolp, however (which we see flourishing at this time as the metropolis of Eastern Pomerania, situated on the river of the same name, fertile in good minds, with an honest government, a crowd of citizens and trade, and with a well-established Church and school), Peter Suavenius, a noble man born in that town and a friend and dear companion of Luther, first sowed the seeds of a purer doctrine. In his private house by the market he expounded the Epistle to the Romans to several learned citizens and to the teachers of the school. Stirred up by him, the rectors of the school not only urged the study of Holy Scripture upon the scholars, but also, through sermons delivered in the school, invited very many to the study of the purer doctrine.

units.la: LIVONICÆ civitates, Riga, Derbatum & Revalia Pontificiæ religionis ritus mutare cœperunt, autore emendationis Ecclesiæ Rigensis primò Andreâ Cnophio Custrinensi: quem Trepoviæ in Pomerania Joannis Bugenhagii, Scholæ Rectoris collegam, & persecutione Mandweliana inde eiectum, Rigam venisse, & mox administerium Ecclesiæ D. Petri vocatum, modestè initio doctrinam de Justificatione peccatoris gratuita per & propter solum Christum pro nobis passum & resuscitatum, auditoribus inculcasse, & abusibus cum hac doctrina pugnantibus graviter taxatis, ritus tamen ipsos nondum mutasse, paulò antè commemoravimus. Accessit autem postea collega turbulentior, Sylvester Tegetmeierus, qui Rostochio, ubi Ecclesiæ Dei Jacobi minister fuit, nuper effugerat, & adeundæ hereditatis fraternæ causâ Rigam profectus, exeunte hoc anno, in æde Divi Jacobi docere cœpit, & maiore impetu Pontificiorum superstitiones & idola palàm coarguit ac detexit: adeo ut vulgo abominationi esse cœperint, & paulò post statuas omnes è templis eiiceret, & lapides sepulcris impositos removerent: ut solent inprimis mutationum articulis multa inconsideratiùs & turbulentiùs geri. Quare Lutherus ad Rigenses scribens, gravissimè monet, religionem veram & pietatem Christianam, in fide, rectè Deum agnoscente, & propter unicum Servatorem nostrum Jesum Christum, non propter ulla externa opera aut merita propria, sed Deo placere, & æternam salutem consequi statuente: in charitate seu officiis dilectionis erga proximum à Deo mandatis: in spe salutis, non succubente cruce & afflictionibus, fidei confessionem comitatibus: non in externorum rituum humanorum observatione aut abolitione, quæ libera sit extra casum scandali, & ædificatio ni veræ pietatis servire debeat situm esse.
units.tr: In the Livonian cities of Riga, Dorpat and Reval, the rites of the Papist religion began to be changed, with Andreas Knopken of Küstrin as the first author of the reform of the Church of Riga. We have mentioned a little earlier that he, a colleague of Johannes Bugenhagen, Rector of the school at Treptow in Pomerania, was driven from there by the Mandwel persecution and came to Riga. Soon he was called to the ministry of the Church of St Peter, and at first he modestly instilled into his hearers the doctrine of the free justification of the sinner through and on account of Christ alone, who suffered and was raised for us. He sharply censured the abuses that conflicted with this doctrine, but had not yet changed the rites themselves. Later a more turbulent colleague arrived, Sylvester Tegetmeier, who had recently escaped from Rostock, where he had been a minister of the Church of St James, and who came to Riga to claim an inheritance from his brother. At the close of this year he began to preach in the church of St James, and with greater vehemence he openly exposed and laid bare the superstitions and idols of the Papists, so that they began to be generally regarded as an abomination. Soon afterwards he cast all the statues out of the churches, and the stones placed on graves were removed. Such things are commonly done too rashly and turbulently, especially in the early stages of change. Therefore Luther, writing to the men of Riga, earnestly admonished them that true religion and Christian piety consist in faith that rightly acknowledges God, and in the belief that God is pleased, and eternal salvation is obtained, through our one Saviour Jesus Christ and not through any outward works or merits of our own; in love, that is, in the duties of charity towards the neighbour commanded by God; in hope of salvation, not giving way under the cross and afflictions, which accompany the confession of faith; and not in the observance or abolition of outward human rites, which are free outside the case of scandal and ought to serve edification in true piety.

units.la: SCAPHUSII II Sebastianus Hoffmeister, Minorita, D. Theologus, in templo Franciscanorum magno zelo contra abominationes Missę fulminat, &,quod chartæ nuper in Bibliotheca quadam inventæ, manuq; ipsius scriptæ, testantur, auditoribus suis hæc axiomata diligenter inculcavit.
units.tr: At Schaffhausen, Sebastian Hoffmeister, a Minorite and Doctor of Theology, thundered with great zeal in the church of the Franciscans against the abominations of the Mass. As papers recently found in a certain library, written in his own hand, bear witness, he diligently impressed these axioms upon his hearers.

units.la: Christi præsentiam corporalem non esse , nec esse posse secundum scripturam post ascensionem illius in cælos.
units.tr: The bodily presence of Christ is not, nor can it be, according to Scripture, after his ascension into heaven.

units.la: Carnem & sanguinem Christi non percipi corporaliter in pane & vino Sacramenti.
units.tr: The flesh and blood of Christ are not received bodily in the bread and wine of the sacrament.

units.la: Christum nullo loco tanquam corporaliter præsentem, esse adorandum.
units.tr: Christ is not to be adored in any place as if bodily present.

units.la: Carnem & sanguinem Christi spiritualiter fide percipi.
units.tr: The flesh and blood of Christ are received spiritually by faith.

units.la: Docuit de his & aliis magno populi concursu & applausu, & nonnullos ex urbis concionatoribus in sententiam suam perttraxit. Accusatus idcirco à sacrificulis, decreto Senatus mittitur Basileā, doctrinæ suæ consensum à viris doctis petitū: sed male ibi à nonnullis acceptus, re infectâ rediit, habuitq; in animo VVittebergam proficisci; à quo consilio Tigurini & Sangallenses ipsum revocârunt, tum itineris periculum, tum corporis eius imbecillitatem causati. Apologiam igitur doctrinæ suæ, scripturæ dictis munitam, confecit: sed propter infensissimos sibi sacrisiculos apud Senatum parum effecit: nec ad docendi munus amplius est admissus. Fremente mente populo Abbas cœnobii ordinis Benedicti, quod est intra urbis mœnia, ex Bavaria vocat virum doctum & eloquentem, Erasmū Ritterum, qui doctrinam Evangelii oppugnaret, & errores Romanæ Ecclesiæ defenderet. Is ut populum demulceret, Missam vernaculâ linguâ celebravit: sed populus eo non contentus, plenam Cœnæ Dominicæ restitutionem flagitabat.
units.tr: He taught these and other things with a great crowd of people and to great applause, and he drew some of the city's preachers into his opinion. For this reason he was accused by the sacrificing priests, and by decree of the Senate he was sent to Basel to seek the agreement of learned men to his teaching. But he was badly received there by some, and returned with his business undone; he had intended to go on to Wittenberg, but the men of Zurich and St Gall called him back, citing both the danger of the journey and his frail bodily health. So he composed an apology for his teaching, fortified with the sayings of Scripture; but because the sacrificing priests were most hostile to him, it achieved little before the Senate, and he was no longer admitted to the office of teaching. While the people were raging, the abbot of the Benedictine monastery, which lies within the city walls, summoned from Bavaria a learned and eloquent man, Erasmus Ritter, to oppose the doctrine of the Gospel and defend the errors of the Roman Church. To soothe the people, he celebrated Mass in the vernacular tongue; but the people, not content with this, demanded the full restoration of the Lord's Supper.

units.la: In oppido S. Galli Benedictus Burgarerus & Wolffgangus Weterus, concionatores, lectis Lutheri de indulgentiis disputationibus, & aliis libris, illuminati, & Joachimi Vadiani Medici Acta Apostolica in ipsorum gratiam enarrantis, divino zelo, confirmati, reiecto Papa Christum profitentur.
units.tr: In the town of St Gall, the preachers Benedict Burgarer and Wolfgang Wetter, enlightened by reading Luther's disputations on indulgences and other books, and strengthened by divine zeal through the Acts of the Apostles, which Joachim Vadian, a physician, explained for their benefit, professed Christ and rejected the Pope.

units.la: BERNATIBUS Bertholdus Hallerus, Helvetius, Zwinglii discipulus (qui postquam Coloniæ gradum Theologiæ primum adeptus esset, Canonicus simul & concionator Bernæ constitutus est) Christum praedicat, sed timidiuscule. Zwinglius igitur per literas illum confirmat, & modum agendi cum Bernensibus ostendit. Tu, inquit, quod a me requiris, ipse strenuè exsequere: ut ursi sui ferociusculi, audità Christi doctrinâ mansuescere incipiant. Quod negotium summâ lenitate adgrediendum puto. Nec enim apud suos sic agere convenit, ut apud nostros: tuorum enim aures etiamnum teneriores cum sint,
units.tr: At Bern, Berthold Haller, a Helvetian and a disciple of Zwingli (who, after first obtaining the degree of Doctor of Theology at Cologne, was appointed canon and preacher at Bern at the same time), preached Christ, but rather timidly. Zwingli therefore strengthened him by letter and showed him how to deal with the men of Bern. You, he says, should yourself vigorously carry out what you ask of me: that these somewhat fierce bears of yours may begin to grow tame once they have heard the doctrine of Christ. I think this business must be taken in hand with the greatest gentleness. For it is not fitting to act among your own people as among ours; since your people's ears are still more tender,

units.la: Tom. I. operum Zwinglii p. 415. non sunt protinus tam mordaici vero radenda: quod & Christum sensisse puto : cum vetuit margaritas ante porcos dissipari, qui fortasse in te conversi, magna te savitia discerperent, ac in perpetuum Evangelium Christi horrerent. Palpanda igitur sunt ha fera lenius, & ad earum insultum paulisper cedendum, donec patientia nostra, intrepidaque pectoris constantia superate, cicures reddantur. Dedit & Petrus aliquid, cum dixit: Sed nunc scio, fratres, quia ignorantes fecistis: dedit Paulus, dum Galatas lacte, non solido cibo aluit. Cesserant omnes Apostoli savitia, dum non pervicaciter Senatui obstrepuerunt, vibicibus etiam lividi: Sed à praedicatione non cessarunt: sic rogo, fias omnia omnibus, ne tecum Christus explodatur: serva nobis Christum apud tuos, & te nobis, Christoq. Ex Tiguro 4. Kal. Januar.
units.tr: Vol. I of Zwingli's works, p. 415. they must not at once be scraped with such biting truth. I think Christ himself felt this, when he forbade pearls to be scattered before swine, which, perhaps turning on you, might tear you apart with great savagery and make the Gospel of Christ hateful for ever. These beasts must therefore be stroked more gently, and we must yield a little to their attacks, until our patience and the unshaken steadiness of our breast overcome them and they are made tame. Peter too gave ground somewhat when he said: "But now I know, brethren, that you did it in ignorance"; Paul did so when he nourished the Galatians with milk, not solid food. All the Apostles gave way to savagery while they did not stubbornly clamour against the Senate, even though they bore the marks of the lash. But they did not cease from preaching. So I ask you: become all things to all men, lest Christ be cast out with you. Keep Christ for us among your people, and keep yourself for us and for Christ. From Zurich, 29 December.

units.la: DANTISCI Monachus quidam, Alexander dictus, in monasterio, ubi hodie Gymnasium, irradiatus luce Evangelii, à Senatu & civibus in templum Marianum translatus est.
units.tr: Dantiscus: a certain monk, called Alexander, in the monastery where the Gymnasium is today, having been enlightened by the light of the Gospel, was transferred by the Senate and citizens to the church of St Mary.

units.la: ISENNACI in Thuringia duo Monachi, unus Franciscani, alter Carthusiensis ordinis, abusus & errores Pontificios publicè perstringunt, & Missam idololatricam, confessionem auricularem, inutilem, invocationem Sanctorum frivolam esse, docent.
units.tr: At Isennach in Thuringia two monks, one of the Franciscan and the other of the Carthusian order, publicly denounce the abuses and errors of the Papists, and teach that the Mass is idolatrous, auricular confession useless, and the invocation of the saints frivolous.

units.la: VIEN-
units.tr: VIEN-

units.la: ANNUS MD XXII.
units.tr: The Year 1522.

units.la: VIENNE Paulus Speratus, nobilis Suevus, in templo Stephani docet: & abusus Pontificios liberè refutat. Inde pulsus Iglaviam venit, Moraviæ urbem.
units.tr: VIENNA: Paul Speratus, a noble of Swabia, preaches in the church of St Stephen and freely refutes the abuses of the Papists. Expelled from there, he came to Iglau, a town in Moravia.

units.la: MOGUNTIÆ quotidiana Evangelii incrementa audiebantur, quæ per D. Casparū Hedionem, cōcionatorem in primaria æde, per Capitonem, & alios, spiritus operabatur, ac fovebat. Quanquam Oecolampadius modestiam Hedionis tacitè reprehendere videtur: quando sic scribit ad Hedionem. Quam gratiam, vel quem locum apud adversarios inveniant veritas & pietas, tute ipse, non dubito, experiris: cum illorum putida ulcera tangis vel extremo digito, texeris adhuc impendio parcens. Sed tu vide sis, an Evangelici sermonis libertati ad amussim hæc tua respondeat modestia.
units.tr: At MAINZ the daily growth of the Gospel was heard. The Spirit worked and nourished it through Dr Caspar Hedio, preacher in the principal church, through Capito, and others. Yet Oecolampadius seems to rebuke Hedio's moderation in a veiled way, when he writes to him: What favour, or what standing among their opponents truth and godliness find, you yourself, I do not doubt, know by experience, since you touch their rotten ulcers even with the tip of a finger, and still spare them at great cost. But see to it whether this moderation of yours answers exactly to the freedom of the Evangelical word.

units.la: Ad constantiam eundem Hedionem inflammat epistolâ ipso die Parasceues hoc anno exaratâ dignissima, quæ hic apponatur:
units.tr: He also fires the same Hedio to steadfastness with a letter, most worthy of quotation here, written on Good Friday of this year:

units.la: Salve, Hedio Charissime, Declamavimus hodie uterq; , tu ad Ecclesiam gravem, ega ad unum & alterum, quo robore Christus hostibus suis ierit obviam: quod nobis modestia, patientia, ac longanimitatis exemplū retulerit. Verùm quid profuerit, vel ad ravim boare? hoc faciunt & qui ultima regni cœlorum classis sunt. Enitendum nobis, ut infractus sit animus, si quando bella ingruant, & sævire cœperit solutis vinculis Lucifer. Vsque in hunc diem non nisi exilij praludia experti sumus: nempe agrè ferunt quidam homunculi, parva autoritatis, minorisq; Christianismi, libertatem Evangelicam, cui parum assueverunt: nondum ventum ad sentes, flagella, crucem, fel, atq; cætera. Paremus animos, imò oremus, ut quacunque horâ nos vocârit Christus, non cessemus, & nec verbo quidem; certi, felicitatem præcipuam vitæ huius, periclitari nomine Christi. Sat scio, nihil opus apud te eiusmodi inhortatione: sed patere, ut me interim confirmem.
units.tr: Greetings, most dear Hedio. We have both preached today, you to the Church at large, I to one or two people, on the strength with which Christ met his enemies, and how he gave us an example of modesty, patience and long-suffering. But what good is it to bellow in rage? Even those who are the last of the kingdom of heaven's fleet do that. We must strive that the spirit be unbroken, should wars break out and Lucifer begin to rage with his chains loosed. Up to this day we have only experienced the preludes of exile. Certain little men, of small authority and of lesser Christianity, bear badly the Evangelical liberty to which they have scarcely become accustomed. The thorns, the scourges, the cross, gall, and the rest have not yet come. Let us prepare our minds, or rather let us pray, that whatever hour Christ calls us, we may not falter, not even in word, knowing well that the chief happiness of this life is put at risk for the name of Christ. I know well there is no need for such exhortation from you, but allow me in the meantime to strengthen myself.

units.la: ULMÆ Joannes Diebolt Evangelizat, & habitas ibi conciones, unam de Dei verbo, alteram de tribus libris, scripturæ, naturæ, conscientiæ, divulgat: docetque, Christum esse patronum nostrum, & conscientiam hominis quietari per fidem Christi & spem divinæ misericordiæ.
units.tr: At ULM Johannes Diebolt preaches the Gospel. He delivered sermons there, one on the Word of God, another on the three books: Scripture, nature and conscience. He teaches that Christ is our patron, and that a man's conscience is quieted through faith in Christ and hope in divine mercy.

units.la: VVILÆ Imperii oppido Diepoldus quidam hoc anno docebat: Virginem Mariam non esse Mediatricem, nec Cateros Sanctos. Christum esse Mediatorem, Nullum esse purgatorium.
units.tr: At WIL, an imperial town, a certain Diepold taught this year: The Virgin Mary is not a Mediatrix, nor are the other saints. Christ is the Mediator. There is no purgatory.

units.la: Sed monitus Senatus à Regiis moderatoribus è Sturgardiâ, illum removit, ægrè id ferente, & pauca ad altaria offerente, plebe.
units.tr: But the Council, warned by the royal governors from Stuttgart, removed him; the common people took this badly and offered few gifts at the altars.

units.la: Legi epistolam ad Senatum populumque VVilensem à Theobaldo à Bellican die omnium Sanctorum huius anni scriptam, quâ profitetur, se primum fuisse VVilensium Evangelicum
units.tr: I have read a letter to the Council and people of Wil, written by Theobald of Bellikon on All Saints' Day of this year, in which he declares that he was the first evangelist of the people of Wil,

units.la: Crucis. angelistam, eosq; porrò instruit, & ad constantiam hortatur. Est igitur Theobaldus is ipse, quē Crusius cū vulgò Diepoldū vocat.
units.tr: and he further instructs them and exhorts them to steadfastness. Theobald is therefore the same man whom Crusius, following common usage, calls Diepold.

units.la: In oppido Creilsheim Adam VVeis docebat, cuius hæc sunt ad Caspare Hedione de statu Ecclesiæ illius verba: De ministerio verbi sic accipe. Si tam molestus ac ingratus essem populo meo, quàm sum mihi ipsi, non rectè succederet, at Christo autore dici vix potest, quanto ardore, quàm intentis auribus ac animis avidissimè verbum Domini excipiant, quàm volentes ducantur, demiror ipse, ac sequacissimè, huius, ut ut rectè vocas, plebecula, etiam lacrymis excipio piam facilitatem, qua tam imperitum, & ineloquentem me ferunt: spero optima omnia fore: fastidiunt & tam citò veterem concionandi ritum, suspecta & iam hominum traditiones, Christus paulo familiarior eis fit, hactenus ignotus fermè, Paulus Aristotelem è suggesto pepulit. xvi Martii.
units.tr: In the town of Creilsheim, Adam Weiss preached. Of the state of that Church he wrote these words to Caspar Hedio: Understand my ministry of the Word thus. If I were as troublesome and ungrateful to my people as I am to myself, it would not go well; but under Christ as author it can hardly be said with what ardour, with what attentive ears and minds, they most eagerly receive the Word of the Lord, how willingly they are led, and I myself marvel at it. Even with tears I welcome the pious readiness of this little flock, which, as you rightly call it, bears with me so patiently, although I am so unlearned and inarticulate. I hope all will turn out for the best. They already loathe the old manner of preaching so quickly, and men's traditions are now suspect. Christ, almost unknown until now, becomes more familiar to them. Paul has driven Aristotle from the pulpit. March 16.

units.la: Cotbusii Lusatiorum Doctor Joannes Griesman, Minorita, Evangelium docet in Monasterio, & inde sequēti anno VVitebergam profectus, summā doctrinæ Evangelicæ Cotbusianis à se præpositæ, typis divulgat.
units.tr: At Cottbus in Lusatia, Dr Johannes Griesman, a Minorite, preaches the Gospel in the monastery. The following year he went to Wittenberg and published in print a summary of the Evangelical teaching which he had set before the people of Cottbus.

units.la: Arnstatum cum forte venisset Caspar Guethell Augustinianus Islebiensis, rogatus à civib. in foro aliquot cōciones habet, quas in sequenti anno VVittembergæ publicat, Gunthero Comiti Schwartzburgico & Arnstati Domino inscriptas.
units.tr: When Caspar Guethell, an Augustinian of Eisleben, happened to come to Arnstadt, at the request of the citizens he gave several sermons in the market square. In the following year he published them at Wittenberg, dedicated to Count Günther of Schwarzburg and lord of Arnstadt.

units.la: ANNUS MDXXII.
units.tr: The Year 1522.

units.la: DELPHIS Hollandiæ quis fuerit Ecclesiæ status, loquatur epistola Friderici Canirmii, hoc anno ad Casparem Hedionem Moguntiam missa. Sic autem illa: Multa moliuntur adversarii per mandata, epistolas, legationesque etiā, sed infatuat Dominus consilia Ahitophel, & fit, ut mōte parturiente nascatur ridiculus mus, tantum scio, si vel semel liceat in publico concionari, res monachorum (quæ hic infestissima sunt veritati) planè ad nihilum redituras, cum magna ex parte labefactatæ sint pauculis in gymnasio nostro sermonibus à me habitis. Sed expectanda patienter voluntas ac beneplacitum Domini, qui cum videat, usque adeò fervere nos, consultò dissimulat auxilium, ne nostris conatibus aut laboribus quidquam arrogemus, si omnia simpliciter cadant, cum non tam habeat rationem vocandorum, ut ad gratiam perveniant, quàm iam vocatorum, ut in gratia permaneant, sed ubi viderit nos cessare, imò desperare salutem Israel, ac totis animis inde pendere, ut ipse solus operetur iam in medio terra: tum demum ex improviso aderit Ecclesia sua, qui inesperata feret auxilia: ut tantum Deo sit laus & gloria, Amen. Erasmum indies magis frigescere, & quantum ego iudicare possū, retractare latēter, qua videatur olim liberius vel dixisse vel scripsisse, ægerrimè fero, & agnosco puerile metū, qui plus veretur hominum gloriam quam Dei. Cæterum tales Nicodemi apud nos in magno sunt numero, sed qui firmius starent haud dubiè. dubiè si detur publicare gloriam Christi, quo uno fortificantur agrè conscientia.
units.tr: At Delft in Holland, the state of the Church is described in a letter of Frederick Canirmius, sent this year to Caspar Hedio at Mainz. It runs thus: The adversaries are devising many schemes, through mandates, letters and even embassies, but the Lord confounds the counsels of Ahithophel, and so it comes about that the mountain labours and brings forth a ridiculous mouse. I know this much: if I may preach in public even once, the affairs of the monks, which here are most hostile to the truth, will come to nothing, since they have already been largely weakened by the few sermons I have given in our school. But the will and good pleasure of the Lord must be awaited patiently. He sees that we are burning so hotly, and so deliberately holds back his help, lest we claim anything for our own efforts or labours, should everything fall out easily. For he is less concerned with calling those who are to come to grace than with keeping those already called in grace. But when he sees us cease, indeed despair of the salvation of Israel, and depend wholly on him to work alone upon the earth, then at last his Church will be present unexpectedly, and he will bring unhoped-for help, so that all praise and glory may be to God alone, Amen. Erasmus grows colder every day and, as far as I can judge, is secretly retracting what he once seemed to have said or written more freely. I bear this very badly, and I recognise the childish fear that fears the glory of men more than the glory of God. Moreover, there are many such Nicodemites among us, but those who would stand more firmly, undoubtedly, if it were granted to make known the glory of Christ, by which alone the conscience is strengthened with difficulty.

units.la: In aula Franciscì à Sickingen Missam repurgat Oecolampadius: qua de re ipsum-met audire juvat: Quoniam Franciscus à Sickin-gen, Clarissimus Germaniæ Eques, & Imperatorii exercitûs Capitaneus, me accersivit, ut familiam suam in templo Christianè instituerem, imò jam pridem institutam sermonibus spiritualibus pascerem: nihil tam muneris mei putavi, quàm ut illi lex Evangelica, familiaris, cognita, & in promptu esset, unde postea per seipsam ad veram sincerāque Christianismi studia tenderet, nempe pacem, mansuetudinem, modestiam, charitatem, pietatem, & ante omnia egregiam in Deum fiduciam. Et per dies quidem quadragesimæ, quibus aderam, nihil obstabat, quin lectum Latinè Evangelium mox interpretari possem, & familiariter ad pietatis studia inhortarer. At post pascha id minus commodum fuit: non enim familia vacat: ut multam temporis partem in templo transmittat, aliò vocantibus negotiis. Et sunt, quibus, quantumvis parva illic mora, fastidium parit. Plerique, ut fermè ubique mos est, amant quotidiè audire, imò videre sacrum: imò audire non intellecta nostra murmura, & spectare ceremonias, adesse benedictioni, & interim perfunctoriè sese Deo commendare: atque ita se, illo, quo hæc observant, die, satis pios esse putant. Quod sanè exigui fructus est, & credo plerisque interim conducibilius, vel arare, vel texere, vel ligna incidere, vel aliud quiddam opera. Templum enim Christianis totus orbis est: & nusquam non orare, & Deum colere, spiritu & veritate, (ut scilicet coli vult) atque etiam preculis laudibus & laudibus convenit. Templa Christianorum maximè extructa sunt, ut in eis commodius ad audiendum verbum Dei & mysteria celebranda conveniretur: non adeo propter preces & cantilenas. Tametsi nunc nullis non tumultibus (ita enim à Prophetis cantus quorundam dicuntur) verbum Dei cedere, & esse loco postremo cogitur. Itaque de ea re cum Francisco Decurione & patrono egi, ut quotidianâ aliquâ sacrâ lectione in templo sui pascerentur: visum mihi est ipsi (ut acris est judicij) nec non & nobilibus & clarissimis viris, Diethero à Talburg, & Hartmundio à Cronberg: quos tu scis, quâ vere Christiani sint: visum, inquam, est eis, esse in rem rudium & piorum, si invertatur vulgaris ille mos, quo solemus Dominico tantum die verbum Domini annuntiare, & per integram hebdomadam Missas habere: ut potius omnibus diebus annuntietur verbum Domini, & solis Dominicis ac festis diebus fiat sacrum, siquidem utroque potiri non datur. Quae sententia & mihi probabatur. Attentata tamen est via alia per me nempe ut Epistola, Evangeliumque vernaculo nostro idiomate legatur. Posse autem & licere hoc Pauli testimonio docebam: & ita semper affore pabulum verbi Dei, & non defore sacrum, neque plus solito temporis insumi. Non est repugnatum, sed assensum ab omnibus quaquorum intererat. Ebernburgo mense Junio.
units.tr: In the household of Franz von Sickingen, Oecolampadius purges the Mass. It is pleasant to hear the man himself on this matter: Since Franz von Sickingen, the most distinguished knight of Germany and captain of the imperial army, summoned me to instruct his household in a Christian manner in the church, and indeed to feed those already long instructed with spiritual sermons, I thought nothing more fitting to my office than that the Evangelical law should be familiar, known and at hand to him, so that afterwards he might himself press on towards the true and sincere pursuits of Christianity: namely peace, gentleness, modesty, charity, piety and, above all, an outstanding trust in God. And indeed during the days of Lent, while I was there, nothing stood in the way of my being able at once to expound the Gospel read in Latin and to exhort them familiarly to the pursuits of piety. But after Easter this was less convenient, for the household has no leisure to spend much of its time in the church, being called elsewhere by business. And for some, however short the stay there, it breeds boredom. Most people, as is almost everywhere the custom, love to hear, indeed to see, the sacred rite every day; indeed they hear our murmurs without understanding them, look on the ceremonies, attend the blessing, and meanwhile commend themselves to God in a perfunctory way, and so they think themselves sufficiently pious on the day on which they do these things. This is certainly of little profit, and I believe for most people it is meanwhile more useful to plough, or to weave, or to chop wood, or to do some other work. For the whole world is a temple to Christians, and it is fitting to pray and worship God everywhere in spirit and in truth, as he wishes to be worshipped, and also with prayers and praises. Christian churches were built chiefly so that people might more conveniently assemble in them to hear the Word of God and to celebrate the mysteries, not so much for prayers and chants. Although now the Word of God is forced to give way to all kinds of tumults (for so the Prophets call the chanting of some), and to be put in the last place. Therefore I discussed this matter with Franz, the commander and patron, so that they might be fed in the church each day with some sacred reading. It seemed good to him (he has a keen judgement), and also to the noble and most distinguished men, Diether von Talburg and Hartmund von Cronberg, whom you know to be truly Christian: it seemed to them, I say, a good thing for untrained and pious people if that common custom were reversed, by which we are accustomed to proclaim the Word of the Lord only on the Lord's Day, and to hold Masses for the rest of the week; so that rather the Word of the Lord might be proclaimed on all days, and the sacred rite performed only on Sundays and feast days, since both cannot be had at once. This opinion also pleased me. Yet another way was tried by me, namely that the Epistle and Gospel should be read in our own vernacular. I taught that this was both possible and lawful by the testimony of Paul, and that thus there would always be food of the Word of God, and no lack of the sacred rite, nor more time spent than usual. No one opposed it, but all who were present gave their assent. From Ebernburg, in June.

units.la: De hoc suo hospitio Oecolampadius hoc eodem anno ita ad Hedionem: Curarum plenus sum, nec dulcis hic mora, nec abitio decreta. Imo manendum & agnoscenda hospitalitas, quoad evocer, (utinam id brevi fieret) ad conditionem quantulamcunq; honestam, ne tam fugere quàm transfire existimer. Hic enim in petra sementem facio.
units.tr: Oecolampadius wrote about this stay of his to Hedio in the same year, as follows: I am full of cares; neither is my delay here sweet, nor is my departure decided. Indeed I must remain and acknowledge this hospitality until I am called away (would that it might happen soon) to some position, however modest, lest I seem to have fled rather than merely passed through. For here I am sowing seed on rock.

units.la: GEORGIUS Comes VVertheimicus, Ecclesias ditionis suæ reformaturus, petit à Luthero Evangelistam, stipendio annuo centum aureorum, & convictus in mensa sua promissa.
units.tr: George, Count of Wertheim, wishing to reform the churches of his territory, asked Luther for an evangelist at an annual stipend of a hundred gold coins, and board at his table was promised.

units.la: In HUNGARIA sparsa de correctione abusuum, & emendatione doctrinæ Pontificiæ famâ, incredibilem in multis accendit ardorem, non modò ad ipsam veritatem amplexandam, sed etiam ad videndum Lutherum, ex quo cœlestis doctrina felicius hauriri, & studium veritatis purius cognosci posse judicabatur. Itaq; hoc anno, Rectore Academiæ Philippo Melanchthone, primus omnium Martinus Cyriaci de Leutsoria, ad Lutherum VVittebergam se contulit: quem anno 1524. Dionysium Lincium Pannonium, & Balthasarem Glebam Budensem, atq; inde alios atque alios subsequutos fuisse, ex publicis Academiæ matriculis constat,
units.tr: In Hungary, the report of the correction of abuses and the reform of Papist teaching kindled an incredible ardour in many, not only to embrace the truth itself but also to see Luther, from whom the heavenly doctrine was judged to be drawn more happily and the zeal for truth more purely known. Therefore this year, with Philip Melanchthon as Rector of the Academy, Martin Cyriaci of Leutschau was the first of all to betake himself to Luther at Wittenberg. That in 1524 Dionysius Lincius of Pannonia and Balthasar Gleba of Buda, and then others after others followed him, is established from the public matriculation registers of the Academy.

units.la: ANNVS CHRISTI MD XXIII.
units.tr: The Year of Christ 1523

units.la: ANNO vicesimo tertio doctrina Evangelii non solum latius propagata, sed multorum etiam fidelium persequutione, & nonnullorum morte fuit obsignata.
units.tr: In the year 1523 the doctrine of the Gospel was not only spread more widely but was also sealed by the persecution of many faithful people and the death of some.

units.la: Ad latius propagandam doctrinam Evangelii duobus hoc anno mediis Deus usus est: dispersione Fratrum Sickingensium, & mitigatione Edicti VVormatiensis.
units.tr: This year God used two means to spread the doctrine of the Gospel more widely: the dispersal of the Sickingen brothers and the softening of the Edict of Worms.

units.la: Vixerant eodem pene tempore in aula Francisci à Sickingen, Joannes Oecolampadius, Martinus Bucerus, Caspar Aquila patritius Augustanus, Joannes Schwebelius Pfortzhemensis. Francisco vero infelici bello implicato, in quo septimâ Maii periit, ex aula illius, tanquam Academia quadam, Bucerus VVeissenburgum, & inde Argentinam, Oecolampadius Basileam, Aquila Isennacu, Schwebelius Bipontum concesserunt, & veluti novi Apostoli singuli singulas eorum locorum Ecclesias reformârunt.
units.tr: At about the same time, Johannes Oecolampadius, Martin Bucer, Caspar Aquila, a patrician of Augsburg, and Johannes Schwebel of Pforzheim had lived at the court of Franz von Sickingen. When Franz became entangled in an unhappy war, in which he died on 7 May, his court broke up. It had been, as it were, a kind of academy. Bucer withdrew to Weissenburg and then to Strasbourg, Oecolampadius to Basel, Aquila to Isenach, and Schwebel to Zweibrücken. Each of them, like a new apostle, reformed the church of his place.

units.la: In Comitiis porrò Noricis absente Cæsare, sextâ Martii Edicto VVormatiensi, singulari Senatusconsulto fuit derogatum. Legato enim Pontificis Adriani Principes incusanti, quod ex formula decreti Cæsareani non fuerit de Luthero sumpta pœna: postulanti deinde consilium, quomodo malum hoc sanari possit: respondent Principes: de Luthero non sumptam pœnam: quia omnes Ordines gravissimè conquerantur de Curia Romana, & pleriq; Lutheri libris atq; concionibus ita jam sint eruditi: ut, si decretum illud adversus illum valere debeat, plurimi id sic interpretaturi sint, quasi id eò fiat, ut oppressâ veritate, & exstinctâ Evangelii luce, manifesta vitia, quæ tolerari aut dissimulari diutius nequeant, defendantur. Consilium suum hoc esse: ut per liberum Concilium, in Germania primo quoque tempore celebrandum, controversiæ Religionis dirimantur.Interim.
units.tr: At the Diet of Nuremberg, while the Emperor was absent, a special resolution of the estates on 6 March overturned the Edict of Worms. When the Pope's legate accused the princes of having left out of the Emperor's decree any penalty against Luther, and then asked for advice on how this evil could be remedied, the princes replied that no penalty had been imposed on Luther because all the estates complained bitterly of the Roman Curia, and most people had already been so schooled by Luther's books and sermons that, if that decree were to be valid against him, most would interpret it as if it were done so that, with the truth suppressed and the light of the Gospel extinguished, obvious abuses which could no longer be tolerated or concealed might be defended. Their own counsel was this: that the controversies of religion should be settled by a free council, to be held in Germany at the earliest opportunity. Meanwhile:

units.la: Nullos novos libros edendos.
units.tr: No new books are to be published.

units.la: Evangelium purè juxta probatas, & ab Ecclesia receptas interpretationes docendum.
units.tr: The Gospel is to be taught purely, according to approved interpretations received by the Church.
