units.la: Ab Episcopis deligendos homines idoneos, qui concionatores exorbitantes leniter castigent.
units.tr: Bishops are to choose suitable men who will gently rebuke preachers who go too far.

units.la: Sacerdotes, qui uxores ducant, juxta leges Pontificias multandos.
units.tr: Priests who take wives are to be fined according to the papal laws.

units.la: LUTHERUS datis ad Principes literis, invehitur in corruptores mandati. Cæsarei, & decretum Noribergense, quod alii aliter accipiccipiebant, pro se interpretatur. Et primum quidem de novorum librorum prohibitione non se recusare, scribit, modò non intelligatur de libris scripturæ, quorum editio prohiberi nequeat. Per interpretationes ab Ecclesia receptas, non Thomæ aut Scoti, sed Hilarii, Ambrosii, Cypriani, Augustini, à plerisq; intelligi: sed Patribus quoq; longè præferenda Biblica scripta. Deligendos ab Episcopis idoneos concionum censores. Rectè id quidem, sed illos viris doctis carere, sophistis non item. Postremum de multandis sacerdotibus, qui vel uxores ducunt, vel ordinem suum deserunt, nimis durum esse, &, si purè sit docendum Evangelium, omnino mitigandum. Titulus literarum est: Wieder die verkehrer des Kaiserlichen Mandats Martinus Luther.
units.tr: Luther, in a letter to the princes, attacks the corrupters of the Imperial mandate, and interprets for himself the Nuremberg decree, which others understood in different ways. And first, as to the prohibition of new books, he writes that he does not object, provided it is not understood of books of Scripture, whose publication cannot be forbidden. As to interpretations received by the Church, he says that most people understand these to be not those of Thomas or Scotus, but those of Hilary, Ambrose, Cyprian and Augustine; yet even the Fathers must be far surpassed by the biblical writings. As to bishops choosing suitable censors of sermons, he says this is indeed right, but that such men would be lacking among learned men, though not among sophists. Last, as to punishing priests who either take wives or abandon their order, he says this is too harsh and, if the Gospel is to be taught purely, must be altogether softened. The title of the letter is: Against the corrupters of the Imperial mandate, by Martin Luther.

units.la: CÆSAR per literas cum Principibus de facto hoc Decreto iracundius expostulavit, & per legatum prorsus id infringere connisus est.
units.tr: The Emperor, by letter, complained more angrily to the princes about this decree, and through a legate strove to overturn it altogether.

units.la: Sed nec Cæsaris & Pontificis rigor, nec Principum moderatio cursum Evangelii remorari potuerunt. Longè enim aliter in cælo, quàm Norimbergæ de hoc negotio fuisse conclusum, scribit Lutherus ad Fridericum Saxoniæ Electorem. Itaque certatim Principes & civitates Pontificiæ religionis mutationem admiserunt.
units.tr: But neither the severity of the Emperor and the Pope nor the moderation of the princes could halt the course of the Gospel. "For in heaven it has been decided quite differently than it was concluded at Nuremberg about this matter," Luther writes to Frederick, Elector of Saxony. And so the princes and cities eagerly admitted a change of the papal religion.

units.la: FRIDERICUS I. Rex Daniæ ministris Evan-
units.tr: FRIDERICK I, King of Denmark, to the ministers of the Gospel...

units.la: ANNUS MDXXIII.
units.tr: THE YEAR 1523.

units.la: Evangelicis, quos in regno jam tum à Christierno vocatos & defensos reperit, liberam concionandi potestatem facit, & Monachis conjugium secundum Dei verbum permittit. Historia compendiosa Regum Daniae, per Erpoldum Lindenbruch edita, refert haec ad annum 1524. his verbis. Fridericus coronatus doctrinam Ecclesiae, à D. Martino Luthero repurgatam, publicè in templis proponi mandat Anno Christi M D XXIIII.
units.tr: He grants the Evangelicals, whom he found already called and defended in the kingdom by Christiern, the freedom to preach, and permits the monks to marry according to the Word of God. The Compendious History of the Kings of Denmark, published by Erpold Lindenbruch, reports these things under the year 1524 in these words: Frederick, having been crowned, orders the doctrine of the Church, purified by Dr. Martin Luther, to be publicly proclaimed in the churches in the year of Christ 1524.

units.la: CHRISTIERNUS Rex Daniae, regno pulsus, cum Elisabetha conjuge, Caroli V. sorore, exulat V Wittembergae, & Lutherum diu concionantem audit.
units.tr: CHRISTIERN, King of Denmark, driven from his kingdom, is in exile at Wittenberg with his wife Elizabeth, sister of Charles V, and hears Luther preaching for a long time.

units.la: LUDOVICUS Comes Palatinus Rheni Bipontinus, Dux Bavariae, seces fermenti Papistici ex Ecclesiis Palatinatus Bipontini, Joannis Schwebelii ministerio expurgat, Missificos omnes eliminat, nihil moratus vicinorum Episcoporum minas.
units.tr: LUDWIG, Count Palatine of the Rhine of Zweibrücken, Duke of Bavaria, through the ministry of Johann Schwebel, purges the leaven of Papism from the churches of the Palatinate of Zweibrücken, expels all the mass-priests, and, unmoved by the threats of the neighbouring bishops, ...

units.la: ALBERTUS Marchio Brandeburgicus Magister ordinis Marianorum Teutonicorum in Borussia Orientali post Comitiorum Noribergensium exitum, consilia emendandae religionis Pontificiae, & instituendae purioris doctrinae, cuius ab Andrea Osiandro, qui Noribergae tum publicè docere coeperat, semina imbibit, primùm suscepit, & per Georgium à Polentia, Episcopū Sambiensem, ipse ex Borussia absens, pertexuit, Itaq; ex Academia VVittebergensi doctorem pium, gravem, eruditum & moderatum, Ioannem Brismannum, Cotbusii in Lusatia natum, Lutheri familiarem & amicum, evocat, qui exeunte anno Regium montem appulit, & inter varias ac multiplices Commendatorum, sacerdotum, & aliorum, Pontificias persuasiones pertinaciter retinentium, adversationes & insidias magno & constanti animo, & pietate ac prudentiâ singulari, emendationem Ecclesiarū paulatim provexit: donec accedente publicâ Principis auctoritate, & ordinum caeterorum approbatione, forma doctrinae & rituum certa & aequabilis, ubique in illius partis Borussiae Ecclesiis constituta est. Huius laboris socios & collegas fideles & praeclaros habuit Paulum Speratum, qui anno 1524. & Ioannem Polyandrum, qui anno 1525. eò venit. Qui tres οἱ πίστοι seu conditores & lumina Ecclesiae Prutenicae, ab erroribus & idolis Pontificiis repurgatae, praecipua, coniunctis animis & consiliis, summa cum pietatis, constantiae, moderationis, & prudentiae laude annos amplius viginti Ecclesias illas, puritate doctrinae, & disciplinae sanctitate & concordia florentes & tranquillas rexerunt & conservarunt.
units.tr: ALBERT, Margrave of Brandenburg, Grand Master of the Teutonic Order of St Mary in East Prussia, after the close of the Diet of Nuremberg, first undertook plans for amending the Papist religion and establishing a purer doctrine, the seeds of which he had imbibed from Andreas Osiander, who had then begun to teach publicly at Nuremberg. He pursued these plans through Georg von Polenz, Bishop of Samland, while himself absent from Prussia. Accordingly he summoned from the Academy of Wittenberg a pious, serious, learned and moderate teacher, Johann Brismann, born at Cottbus in Lusatia, a close friend and intimate of Luther. Brismann reached Königsberg at the end of the year and, amid the various and manifold oppositions and snares of the commendatory holders of benefices, priests and others who stubbornly kept to Papist persuasions, advanced the reform of the churches step by step with great and steady courage and singular piety and prudence. Then, when the public authority of the prince was added and the approval of the other estates, a form of doctrine and rites, fixed and uniform, was established throughout the churches of that part of Prussia. He had as faithful and distinguished companions and fellow-labourers Paul Speratus, who came there in 1524, and Johann Polyander, who came in 1525. These three, the [οἱ πίστοι] or founders and lights of the Prussian Church, freed from Papist errors and idols, with united hearts and counsels, above all with the highest praise of piety, constancy, moderation and prudence, ruled and preserved those churches for more than twenty years, which flourished and were calm in purity of doctrine, holiness of discipline and concord.

units.la: Joannes Breismannus vigesimâ septimâ SeptemSeptembris Regiomonti in summo templo Kneiphhofii, in veteri autem urbe Dominus Amandus Dominicâ Adventûs concionem Evangelicam primam habuêre.
units.tr: Johann Brismann and Dominus Amandus held the first evangelical sermons at Königsberg: on 27 September in the main church of Kneiphof, and in the old city on Advent Sunday.

units.la: JOHANNES Princeps Anhaldinus favere jàm tum cœpit Luthero: ideoq; per Doctorem Hieronymum, & Franciscanum quendam Lutherum monuit, ut purgaret se ab ignominia, quâ à Ferdinando Austriaco Norimbergæ fuisset notatus, quod novo exemplo docEret, Christum esse semen Abrahæ.
units.tr: JOHANN, Prince of Anhalt, had already begun to favour Luther. Therefore through Dr. Jerome and a certain Franciscan he warned Luther to clear himself of the disgrace with which Ferdinand of Austria had marked him at Nuremberg, because he taught the new doctrine that Christ is the seed of Abraham.

units.la: CAROLUS Sabaudiæ Dux sincerioris religionis studiosissimus esse ferebatur. Quod cum Lutherus ex Annemundo Cocto, Equite aurato Gallo intellexisset, septimâ Septembris huius anni Sabaudum per literas, in quibus fidei suæ confessionem breviter repetit, in pietatis zelo confirmavit. In harum fine, Macte, inquit, Princeps Illustrissime, & heros generosissime, suscita eam, quæ in te cœpit ardere scintillam, & fac ut ignis egrediatur de domo Sabaudiæ, ceu de domo Iosephi, & sit ei tota Gallia quasi stipula, & ardeat sanctum illud incendium Christi, imò flagret, ut verè tandem Francia possit dici ab Evangelio regnum Christianissimum, quod hactenus ab impio in Antichristu, propter effusum sanguinem, officio, impiè dictum est Christianissimum. Anno 1523. 7. Sept.
units.tr: CHARLES, Duke of Savoy, was reported to be most zealous for a purer religion. When Luther learned this from Annemundus Coctus, a Gallic knight, he strengthened the Savoyard in his zeal for piety by a letter of 7 September of this year, in which he briefly repeats his confession of faith. At its end he writes: Well done, most illustrious prince and noblest hero! Rekindle the spark that has begun to glow in you, and make the fire go out from the house of Savoy, as from the house of Joseph, and let all Gaul be to it as stubble, and let that holy fire of Christ blaze, indeed flare up, so that at last France may truly be called, by the Gospel, the most Christian kingdom, which until now the impious Antichrist, on account of the blood shed, has impiously called the Most Christian by the title of his office. 1523, 7 September.

units.la: De Livonia sic Lutherus ad Spalatinum vicesimâ quintâ Januarii: M. Livonia ex me→ petiit per nuntium & per Cancellarium, eruditum virum, ut libellum ad suos populos scriberem de re Christiana, aluntq; ibi verbi praedicatorem, & gaudet se Evangelion habere. Sic à Iudais transfit Christus ad Gentes, & de lapidibus fiunt filij Abrahae quem sui nepotes persequuntur.
units.tr: Luther writes thus to Spalatin about Livonia on 25 January: Livonia has asked me, through a messenger and through the chancellor, a learned man, to write a little book for its people on Christian matters; they maintain a preacher of the Word there and rejoice that they have the Gospel. Thus Christ has passed from the Jews to the Gentiles, and out of stones the children of Abraham are made, whom his own descendants persecute.

units.la: Eosdem Livonos Lutherus epistolâ salutat, quâ gratulatur illis patefactam Evangelii Christi doctrinam, cuius oppressionem plerosq; in Germania Tyrannos pertinaciter moliri queritur, eiusdemq; generis persecutiones atrocissimas ipsis quoq; expectandas praemonet, ad quas sustinendas ut sese praeparent, animumq; obfirmatum habeant, atq; in agnita veritate Evangelica fortiter perseverent, graviter ac piè cohortatur, de fide justificante, & tandem vera ratione bonorum operum, breviter & perspicuè eos erudiens.
units.tr: Luther greets the same Livonians by letter. In it he congratulates them on the Gospel doctrine of Christ having been opened up to them, whose suppression he complains that many tyrants in Germany stubbornly strive to bring about. He warns that persecutions of the same kind, most atrocious, await them too, and earnestly and piously exhorts them to prepare themselves to bear these, to keep their minds firm, and to persevere bravely in the Evangelical truth they have acknowledged. Finally, he briefly and plainly instructs them on justifying faith and, at last, on the true reason for good works.

units.la: VVolfgangus Jonerus Abbas Capellae, qui ex Zwinglii concionibus errores Pontificiae religionis agnoverat, scholam in coenobio instituit, cui praeficit M. Henricum Bullingerum, octodecim annorum juvenem, qui & ipse veritatis Evangelicae gustum, ex scriptorum Lutheri & Melanchthonis lectione Coloniae perceperat.
units.tr: Wolfgang Joner, abbot of Kappel, who had recognized the errors of the Papist religion from Zwingli's sermons, founded a school in the monastery and placed over it Master Heinrich Bullinger, a youth of eighteen. Bullinger himself had tasted the truth of the Gospel at Cologne by reading the writings of Luther and Melanchthon.

units.la: Abbas Hirschfeldensis hoc anno permisit quibuslibet liberum exitum, tam Monachis quàm Monialibus. Pastor Hirschfeldensis defuncta uxore prima, duxit secundam.
units.tr: This year the abbot of Hirschfeld allowed anyone who wished to leave freely, both monks and nuns. The pastor of Hirschfeld, his first wife having died, took a second.

units.la: .In SILESIA plenior Evangelii lux affulsit Uratislavienſibus,& Lignicenſibus.
units.tr: In Silesia a fuller light of the Gospel shone upon the people of Breslau and Liegnitz.

units.la: URATISLAVIÆ Canonicus erat Joannes Hesſius Norimbergensis, Theologiæ Doctor, vitæ inculpatæ, doctrinæ eruditæ, eloquentiæ raræ.
units.tr: At Breslau there was a canon, Johann Hess of Nuremberg, Doctor of Theology, of blameless life, learned doctrine and rare eloquence.

units.la: Cum igitur ab obitu Oswaldi VVimleri paftoratus ad D. Mariam Magdalenam quadriennium vacasset, pro more temporum illorum de obtinendo eo nonnullis coram politico Magistratu contendentibus, senatus morae pertaesus, consentiente populo universo, probante Jacobo à Salza Episcopo, decimo nono Junii Joanni Hesſo, vocatione solenni, Ecclesiae Magdalenanç gubernationem commédat. Is vigesimâ quintâ Octobris Dominicâ XXI. Trinitatis primam ibi concionem habet in maxima populi frequentia.
units.tr: Since the death of Oswald Wimler the pastorate of St. Mary Magdalene had been vacant for four years, and in the manner of those times some contended before the civil magistrate for obtaining it. The senate, weary of the delay, with the whole people consenting and Bishop Jacob von Salza approving, on 19 June committed the government of the Magdalene church to Johann Hess by a solemn call. On 25 October, the twenty-first Sunday after Trinity, he gave his first sermon there before a very large crowd of people.

units.la: Adrianus Papa ægerrimè hoc tulit, & datis ad senatum literis à proposito eum revocare conatus est. Sed frustrà. Senatus enim facti sui causas reddidit gravissimas, editâ Apologiâ, quæ quia vivam habet descriptionem & statûs Ecclesiastici sub Pontifice Romano, & Pontificis in illo, necessariò hîc inserenda & à posteritatis oblivione fuit vindicanda. Sic igitur illa:
units.tr: Pope Adrian took this very badly and, by letters sent to the senate, tried to recall Hess from his purpose. But in vain. For the senate gave very weighty reasons for its action, publishing an Apology. Since this contains a vivid description of the ecclesiastical state under the Roman Pontiff, and of the Pontiff within it, it must necessarily be inserted here and rescued from the oblivion of posterity. It runs thus:

units.la: SENATVS POPVLVSQ. VRATISLAVIENSIS piis lectoribus salutem in Domino. Non ambigi-mus, viri Christiani, qui & corde & ore Christum profitemini, quin vobis (etiam sine ullo nostro en-comio) summè placeat novi pastoris nova electio, cum inprimis vestrae professioni conveniat, niti & exemplo & doctrina Apostolorum, quae sanè & basis & fundamentum verae fidei, eo vobis commenda-tior esse debet, quod à spiritu sancto profecta est, signata sphragismate sanguinis Christi & electorum Dei. Verùm cum multi sint quibus post hujus mundi honores & carnis voluptates nihil quicquam divini aut sancti pensi est, ne illis ansa relinquatur improbandi hoc nostrum adeo laudabile ac frugiferum institutum, breviter eius consilij rationes explicabimus: ne, si forte plerique firmamentum roburque rei non acceperint, aliqui ex eis tyrannide & majestate adversariorum in sensum non verum traducantur: tum etiam, ut inter nos mutua dilectio conservetur, quam alioqui, scissa in diversas partes Ecclesia, labefactari necessum esset. Primùm ergo non immeritò nos, quibus summa Reip. concredita est, vehementer commovit animi, quod aedes Divae Magdalenae tot jam annis sine sponso & parocho consenuit & eviluit, quam adeo pro uno sponso multi appetivere, ut etiam illis ad tribunal saepè de-ventum est, atque ita alij alios mutuo semper eycerent contendentes de animarum nostrarum salute, nihilsecus atque ij, qui tesseris colludunt, porro utrique fortunam sine virtute experiuntur. Quod contendendi studium ab Ecclesia profecto alienissimum esse debet. Oportet enim Episcopum inculpatum esse, tanquam Dei dispensatorem, non præfractum, non iracundum, non vinosum, non percussorem: non turpiter lucro deditum, non ambitiosum, cum ea dignitas non ambitione sed consensu Ecclesia comparetur, & non nummario pretio, sed oneroso honore constet, ijs artibus denique parandum sit verum sacerdotium, quod nisi coactus aliquis ritè capessere non potest, ut in C. de Ep. & Cl. Lc. si quenquam Divus Leo Augustus super acceptando sacerdotio sanctissimè statuit hisce verbis, tanto & Christiano Principe non indignis. Nemo gradum sacerdotii venalitate petitii meretur, quantū quisq; mereatur, non quantum dare sufficit, æstimetur. Prosecto enim quis locus tutus, & quæ causa poterit esse excusata, si veneranda Dei templa pecuniis expugnentur? quem murum integritatis aut vallum fidei providebimus, si auri sacra fames penetralia veneranda proserpit? Denique quid cautum esse poterit, aut securum, si sanctitas incorrupta corrumpitur? Cesset altaribus imminere prophanus ardor avaritiæ: & à sacris adytis repellatur peculare flagitium. Ita castus & humilis nostris temporibus eligatur Episcopus, ut locorum quocunque per venerit omnia propria vitæ integritate purificet, non pretio sed precib. ordinetur. Antistes tantum ab ambitu debet esse seposi-tus, ut quaratur cogendus, rogatus recedat, invitatus effugiat, sola illi suffragetur necessitas excusandi. Profecto enim indignus est Sacerdotio, nisi fuerit ordinatus invitus. Qua de re haud ita longius standum nobis esse duximus illorum disceptationibus, qui tam importunè sacerdotia quærunt, ac passim aliorum injuria sese consecrat, ne scilicet illos expectando interim status nostræ salutis periclitaretur. Proinde aliquot jam annis nō æquè Evangelium hic annuntiatum est: quippe alij pro Christi Evangelio Thomam, Scotum, Aristotelem, Christianis auribus summa cum indignitate instillarunt: alij loculis & marsupio consuluerunt, prædicando non gratuitam fidei, sed pronundinam fiduciam operum: alij item in operculum sua carnis & impietatis sacras literas detorserunt: quo factū est, vt multi nesciant quam viam sequantur, atque ita dubij errent, vt navis in medio mari gubernatore destituta. Quod malum ne indulgentia nimia aut irritando tanquam excetrá illa Lernaa vires acquireret, aut latius serpéret, summa cum diligentia è nostrorum animis tollere, & ad usq; vivam radicem averruncare studuimus: quærendo scilicet nobis & Ecclesia nostra eum pastorem, qui incredibili fiducia & alacritate verbum Domini, & impervestigabiles ab humana prudentia divitias ejus & communionem mysterij, quod erat absconditum à seculo. ideo nobis decantabit secundum spem nostram, quam in illum habemus repositam in Domino, qui omnibus innocentia vita & modestia charus est, qui antea à Reverendissimo D. Episcopo nostro ad Evangelizandi munus, & nunc quoq; à nobis unanimi consensu vocatus & accensus est, ac electus in Domino juxta consuetudinem ab Apostolis vulgatam, & Ecclesia, quae in Christo est, receptam. Siquidem Ecclesia est vocare & eligere pastorem: Episcopi autem, sive presbyteri, manus imponere. Nunc cum ipsa electio canonice & debite celebrata sit, ac secuta judicium & eulogium Reverendissimi nostri Antistitis, qui summa cura nos ad amorem praesentis pastoris invitavit, atque primus illi calculum ac suffragium suum detulit ad annunciandum Evangelion de Christo, non passus, uti sub modio tam bona lucerna perderetur, aut ipse talentum, quod a Domino accepit, intra terra penetralia, seu parum fidelis servus infoderet ac reconderet: verum in verbi ministrum nobis eum constituit: quae Evangelizandi functio inter reliqua Ecclesiae munia prima & maxima est. Proinde cum in maximus nobis datus esset magister, minoribus quoque eum Ecclesiae officiis, quae de jure parochiali dicuntur, praefecimus: rati, par ac debitum esse, minima illi concredere, qui in maximis esset fidelis, cum etiam non liceat alium habere verbi ministrum, alium dispensatorem mysteriorum Dei: ita enim scinderetur & ordo & dignitas sacerdotij. Nam quid magis absurdum esse queat, quam eum habere dispensatorem mysteriorum Dei, qui ita institutus esset, ut verbum ministrare non possit? Quomodo autem aliquis dispensaret mysteria, quorum cognitionem per verbi scientiam non habet? cum nec in mechanicis quidem rudis adhuc opificij admittatur. Ad haec ita constituit Deus, aequitatis legem dispensans: ut in corpore nostro alia sunt membra qua regunt corpus, atque omnibus moribus eius praesident, alia item sunt quae reguntur ac obsequium rectoribus prabent, in Ecclesia quoq; alii gubernarentur ac regerentur, quibus hoc utilissimum est, ut verbo & opere rectorum ad id quod expedit, imbuantur, alios vero pastores dedit & doctores, ad perfectionem Ecclesiae, eos scilicet, qui prae ceteris virtute animi praediti familiarius Deo assistat, & id officii in Ecclesia gerant, quod anima in corpore; ut utraq; pariter compaginata, & sibi invicem mixta, in quo quid deest & in quo abundat, velut in membrorum diversitate consonantia facta, per spiritum perfectum & integrum atq; aptum ad omnia corpus existat & dignum, quod Christum habeat caput. Ergo idem ex scriptura & verbi minister, & dispensator mysteriorum Dei (hoc est, ut Paulus ait, alios dedit pastores & doctores) esse debet, atq; in iis totum sacerdotium comprehenditur potius quam in supercilio Ephod, cidari, tiara, anclabri atq; aliis no eo usq; exigendis ab Ecclesia Christi. Iuste igitur vere piu ac Christianum hominem D. Ioannem Hessum, Theologiae Doctorem in parochum nobis elegimus, ad ministerium verbi ante vocatum ab Episcopo, comisimusq; ei curam & vivorum & mortuorum: ut vivos immarcescibili fructu verbi Domini pascat ac nutriat: defunctos vero in Domino pie sepeliat, no, ut praedecessores parochi, quibus una opera erat inhiare lucro. Nam sive nasceretur, sive moreretur aliquis, omnes erant tributarii & vectigales parocho, ut etiam multa millia gratiarum ac indulgentiarum nomina, remissione peccatorum praesefertia, atq; id genus alia pastorum storum commenta taceamus. Quod verò omnium miserrimum, mortui plus vivis censebantur: ut credibile sit, poëticum illum Charonta in transportandis multis mitiorem fuisse, quàm nostros parochos in sepeliendo. Cum autem sine iis nundinationibus cum suis Diaconis & hypodiaconis verus pastor sese de nudis Ecclesiæ reditibus sustentare non posset, ut sæpè nostris auribus inter concionandum inculcavit sincerirer nobis in Christo dilectus eximius vir, D. Magister Ioachimus, qui aliquot iam annis sive per locationem, sive per aliam rem quampiam dicta parochia præfuit, atq; ita inter concionandum nos admonuit, ut augeremus censum Ecclesiæ, ne cogeretur eam egestate & penuria rerum deserere: consilium quæsivimus, ne ita perpetuùm & vivi & mortui vectigales & in prædam essemus: & ut sine hoc censu pastorem quoq; nostrum honestè ac liberaliter, pro persona & dignitate sacerdotii alere possimus, quo is modò in salutem nostram occupatus sit, non autem turpibus illis rationibus: tot hodiè, tot heri, tot nudius tertius funera, atq; utinam etiam aliquid in crastinum, perendie, & sic deinceps. Quam rem adeo indignam ad sacram & augustam Regiam Maiestatem D. Ludovicum Hungariarum & Bohemiæ Regem, Dominum nostrum Clementissimum, tum per legatos, tum per literas retulimus, & summis laboribus & precibus obtinuimus: uti pro nobis Maximus Rex apud summum Pontificem intercederet, quo is ius eligendi & præsentandi pastorem Ecclesia nostra nobis conferret, quod & ipsum à sua sanctitate, tantâ humilitate, quanta par est, nos expostulavimus. Ad quam postulationem neq; Regiæ Maiestati, neq; nobis quicquam responsi datum est. Cum alioqui nobiscum Summus Pontifex de Lutheranismo (negotio non identidem periculoso) satis copiosè per longum Breve ageret, Ecclesiæ verò nostræ rei ad salutem animarum nostrarum vel maximè necessariæ, prorsum non commemi-nit. Sentientes itaque apud Romanum Pontificem, nec Regiæ Maiestatis, nec nostras preces valuisse, non oscitanter, nec imprudenter ad præsentem electionem accessimus, & pastorem nobis elegimus, quem tanquam obedientes filii, primùm Vicario in spiritualibus generali, deinde Episcopo coràm constitutum, ac iterum Vicario generali præsentavimus, quo eum iuxta morem huius diæceseos, in possessionem Ecclesiæ solenniter investirent. Sed & hic repulsam passi sumus, non quod hunc nobis negarent pastorem, aut de eius integritate dubitarent, quem tantopere, & tot titulis paulò antè commendaverant, & in verbi ministrum prefecerant: sed quod illorum indignationem veriti sunt, qui unà inter se pro ea Ecclesia contendunt & dilitigant. Nos autem nihil minus eundem electum nostrum in possessionem parochiæ instituimus. Ordinata proinde in statum optimum re Ecclesia & pastorali, ne identidem animarum no-strarum strarum cura, atque antehac sape factum est, ulli sub pensione, vel alia Simoniaca conditione locanda veniret, ac subinde multi, in extremis constituti, negligerentur, neve essent nobiscum partita munia sacerdotii, quod utiq; unum & simplex esse par est, perinde eius Christus unus, & auctor & magister est: Vos omnes obtestamur in Domino, ne quis vestrum nobis male vertat, tanta rei tam subitam mutationem, multis etiam non auditam seculus. Neque mirum, si vobis res nova, (licet in Christi Ecclesia semper fuerit usitatissima) videatur, qui nati estis, & coaluistis sub imperio conductitiorum pastorum: quorum artificio in Ecclesia Dei omnia Sacramenta venalia facta sunt, tanquam ab illis ipsis vita aeterna emenda esset, quam quisq; secundum aestimationem suam licitatus est, neque satis es-set eam per fidem dono & plane gratuito accepisse à Christo Iesu, qui fallere nec potest, nec didicit. Horum profecto pastorum imposturas & prætigias inhibistis à teneris, nscientes adhuc lac Apostolicum, & dulcedinem Evangelicam. Si qui autem sunt, qui nobis calumniari non desinent, Spiritu fortitudinis in Domino illorum sycophantias tolerabimus. Nam ab auditione mala non timebit iustus, qui, si homines timeret, Christi servus non esset. Sed quid sollicitamur, ac si hac nostra electio ulli non placeat? cum secundum scripturam & consuetudinem Ecclesia celebrata sit, cuius Ecclesia & caput & sponsus est Iesus pro nobis crucifixus, qui ait: qui mecum non est, contra me est: & qui mecum non colligit, spargit. Nunc si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos. Quis intentabit crimina adversus electos Dei? Deus est qui iustificat, quis ille qui condemnet? Christus est, qui mortuus est, imo qui & suscitatus est, qui etiam est ad dexteram Dei, qui & intercedit pro nobis. Exultate ergo & gaudete nobiscum, qui pro parte Evangelij statis, cum in commune vobis seritur ac metitur, gratias agentes Deo, quod nobis de eo pastore prospexerit, qui & Episcopo nostro, & nobis iuxta charus est, & pie exercitatus in sacris literis, cui satis mercedis erit, excolere vineam Domini, & nos lucrifacere Deo per verbum Iesu Christi. Caeterum abstinebit a spoliandis tum vivus tum mortuis. Nostrum autem, imo totius communitatis erit, & illius curam vicissim agere libere, non coacte, & pro sepultura & aliis ossiciis mittendo in gazophylacium, ut cuiusque pietas & facultates tulerint. Nam qui Evangelio servit, etiam de Evangelio vivat: duplici enim honore dignus est, ut ait Apostolus.
units.tr: THE SENATE AND PEOPLE OF BRESLAU send greetings in the Lord to the pious readers. Christian men, you who profess Christ with both heart and mouth, we do not doubt that the new election of a new minister pleases you greatly, even without any praise from us. It especially suits your profession to rest on the example and teaching of the Apostles, which are the foundation and base of true faith. That teaching should be the more commendable to you because it came from the Holy Spirit and bears the seal of Christ's blood and of God's elect. But since many people care nothing for anything divine or holy once the honours of this world and the pleasures of the flesh are set aside, we will briefly explain the reasons for our decision. We do this so that, if many have not grasped the firmness and strength of the matter, some of them will not be twisted by the tyranny and majesty of our adversaries into a false sense. We also do it so that mutual love may be kept among us, which otherwise would necessarily be weakened, since the Church is torn into different parts. First, we who have been entrusted with the highest government of the commonwealth were deeply troubled that the church of St Magdalen has for so many years grown old and worthless without a patron and parish priest. Many have so eagerly sought this one patronage that they often came even to the court, and so they continually drove one another out, contending over the salvation of our souls. They were no different from those who gamble with dice; both sides tried their luck without any virtue. This zeal for contention ought to be utterly alien to the Church. "A bishop must be blameless, as God's steward: not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not given to wine, not a striker; not shamefully greedy for gain, not ambitious." His dignity is conferred not by ambition but by the consent of the Church. It is secured not by a money price but by a weighty honour. In short, the true priesthood must be obtained by such means that no one can properly take it up unless he is compelled. The Divine Emperor Leo Augustus most holily decreed this concerning accepting the priesthood, in the Code, title De Episcopis et Clericis, law Si quenquam, in words not unworthy of so Christian a prince: "No one earns a step to the priesthood by buying it. Let each man be valued according to what he deserves, not according to what he is able to pay." For what place will be safe, and what cause can be excused, if the venerable temples of God are stormed with money? What wall of integrity or rampart of faith shall we provide if the sacred hunger for gold creeps into the venerable inner sanctuaries? In short, what can be guarded or kept secure if incorrupt holiness is corrupted? Let profane greed cease to hang over the altars, and let the crime of peculation be driven from the holy shrines. Let a chaste and humble bishop be chosen in our times, so that wherever he goes he purifies everything by the integrity of his own life, and is ordained not for a price but by prayers. A prelate ought to be so far removed from ambition that he is sought, must be compelled to accept, withdraws when asked, flees when invited, and only necessity excuses him from taking up the office. For indeed he is unworthy of the priesthood unless he is ordained against his will. On this matter we have judged that we should not spend much longer on the disputes of those who seek priesthoods so importunately, and who on every side consecrate themselves at the expense of others. Otherwise, while we waited for them, the state of our salvation would be endangered. Therefore for some years now the Gospel has not been announced here as it should be. Some have instilled into Christian ears, to their great disgrace, Thomas, Scotus and Aristotle in place of the Gospel of Christ. Others have looked after their purses and money bags, preaching not the free confidence of faith but a marketable confidence in works. Others again have twisted the sacred letters to cover their own flesh and impiety. As a result, many do not know which way to go, and so they wander in doubt, like a ship in mid-sea without a steersman. Lest this evil gain strength through excessive indulgence, or be provoked like that Lernaean hydra, or creep further, we have taken the greatest care to remove it from our people's minds and to root it out down to the living root. We have sought for ourselves and our Church that minister who, with incredible confidence and eagerness, will proclaim the Word of the Lord, the riches of God which human wisdom cannot search out, and the fellowship of the mystery which has been hidden from the ages. He will therefore sing to us according to the hope we have placed in him in the Lord. He is dear to all for the innocence of his life and his modesty. Our most reverend Bishop first called and fired him for the office of preaching the Gospel, and now we too, by unanimous consent, have called, kindled and elected him in the Lord, according to the custom handed down by the Apostles and received in the Church that is in Christ. For it belongs to the Church to call and elect a pastor. It belongs to the bishops, or the elders, to lay on hands. The election itself has now been celebrated canonically and duly, and it was followed by the judgement and commendation of our most reverend Bishop. He with great care invited us to love the present minister and was the first to give him his vote and suffrage for proclaiming the Gospel of Christ. He did not allow such a good lamp to be lost under a bushel, nor did he, like an unfaithful servant, bury the talent he had received from the Lord in the hidden places of the earth. He has appointed him to us as minister of the Word, which function of evangelizing is the first and greatest of the Church's duties. Therefore, since he has been given to us as our greatest teacher, we have also set him over the lesser offices of the Church, which pertain to parochial right. We judged it fitting and right to entrust the least things to him who is faithful in the greatest, since it is not permitted to have one minister of the Word and another dispenser of God's mysteries. Otherwise both the order and the dignity of the priesthood would be torn apart. For what could be more absurd than to have as dispenser of God's mysteries a man so trained that he cannot minister the Word? How would anyone dispense mysteries whose knowledge he lacks through the science of the Word? Not even in the mechanical crafts is a raw beginner admitted. God has so ordained this, dispensing the law of equity. In our body some members rule the body and preside over all its functions, while others are ruled and render obedience to their rulers. So in the Church too some should govern and others be governed, and it is most useful to the latter to be imbued by the word and work of their rulers with what is expedient. God gave pastors and teachers for the perfecting of the Church, namely those who, endowed with a virtue of mind beyond the others, stand closer to God and perform in the Church the office that the soul performs in the body. Thus both, joined together and mixed with one another, supply what is lacking and what abounds, and as in the diversity of members a harmony is made, so through the perfect and whole Spirit the body becomes fit and worthy for all things, having Christ as its head. Therefore the same man should be both minister of the Scripture and the Word and dispenser of God's mysteries (that is, as Paul says, "He gave some pastors and teachers"). In these the whole priesthood is comprehended, rather than in the superhumeral of the Ephod, the mitre, the tiara, the ankle-bands and the other things not required by the Church of Christ. Therefore, rightly, we have chosen as our parish priest the truly pious and Christian man, Dr John Hess, Doctor of Theology, who had earlier been called to the ministry of the Word by the Bishop. We have entrusted to him the care of the living and the dead: that he may feed and nourish the living with the unfading fruit of the Word of the Lord, and bury the dead piously in the Lord. He is not to be like the former parish priests, whose one business was to gape after gain. For whether anyone was born or died, all were tributaries and tax-payers to the parish priest. We pass over the many thousands of graces and indulgences, the names that promise remission of sins, and other such inventions of those shepherds. What was most wretched of all was this: the dead were valued more than the living. So it is credible that the poetic Charon was gentler in ferrying many across than our parish priests were in burying. Since, however, without these dealings the true minister could not support himself, with his deacons and subdeacons, from the bare revenues of the Church, our beloved and eminent brother in Christ, Master Joachim, often insisted to our ears while preaching. He had for some years presided over the said parish, whether by lease or by some other arrangement, and so he admonished us in our sermons to increase the Church's income, lest it be forced to abandon the church through poverty and want. We sought counsel, so that we would not remain forever both living and dead tributaries and prey, and so that we could support our pastor honourably and generously, according to his person and the dignity of the priesthood. Then he could be occupied in our salvation, not in those shameful practices: "So many funerals today, so many yesterday, so many the day before, and would that there were something for tomorrow, the day after, and so on." We reported this matter, so unworthy, through envoys and by letters to the sacred and august Royal Majesty of Lord Louis, King of Hungary and Bohemia, our most gracious lord. With great labours and prayers we obtained that His Most Serene Majesty would intercede for us with the Supreme Pontiff, so that he would grant our Church the right to elect and present its own pastor. We too asked this of His Holiness with all the humility it deserved. To this request no answer was given either to His Royal Majesty or to us. Yet the Supreme Pontiff, in a long Brief, dealt with us quite fully about Lutheranism, a matter by no means dangerous, and he did not mention at all the affair of our Church, which was most necessary for the salvation of our souls. Feeling, therefore, that neither the prayers of His Royal Majesty nor ours had prevailed with the Roman Pontiff, we came to the present election not carelessly nor imprudently. We chose for ourselves a pastor, whom, as obedient sons, we first presented to the Vicar General in spirituals, then before the Bishop in person, and again to the Vicar General, so that according to the custom of this diocese they might solemnly install him in possession of the church. But here too we met with a rebuff. This was not because they denied us this pastor or doubted his integrity, whom they had so highly commended, with so many titles, only a little while before, and set over the ministry of the Word. It was because they feared the indignation of those who contend and quarrel together over that church. Nevertheless, we installed our chosen pastor in possession of the parish. With the Church and its pastoral affairs now set in the best order, the care of our souls will not again be let out to anyone under a pension or any other simoniacal condition, as has often happened before. Many who lie in extremity will not be neglected, and the duties of the priesthood, which ought to be one and simple, will not be divided among us, for Christ alone is its one author and teacher. We beseech you all in the Lord that none of you take it amiss that we have made such a sudden change, something many have not heard of in past ages. Nor is it surprising if the matter seems new to you, though it has always been most usual in the Church of Christ. You were born and grew up under the rule of hired pastors, by whose craft all the sacraments in God's Church have been made venal, as though eternal life could be bought from them, each man bidding for it according to his own estimate. As if it were not enough to have received it by faith from Christ Jesus, a free and entirely gratuitous gift, who can neither deceive nor has learned to. You have indeed been trained from childhood to resist the impostures and juggling tricks of these pastors, not yet knowing the Apostolic milk and the sweetness of the Gospel. If there are some who will not stop calumniating us, we will bear their sycophancy in the spirit of fortitude in the Lord. "The righteous man will not fear evil tidings," for if he feared men he would not be a servant of Christ. But why should we be troubled, as if this election of ours pleased no one? It has been celebrated according to Scripture and custom, in the Church whose head and bridegroom is Jesus, crucified for us, who says: "He that is not with me is against me, and he that gathereth not with me scattereth." "If God is for us, who can be against us? Who shall lay anything to the charge of God's elect? It is God that justifieth; who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us." Rejoice, then, and be glad with us, you who stand for the part of the Gospel, while the seed is sown and reaped for all of you in common. Give thanks to God that He has provided us with such a pastor, who is dear both to our Bishop and to us, and is piously exercised in the sacred letters. It will be reward enough for him to tend the vineyard of the Lord and to win us to God through the word of Jesus Christ. Otherwise he shall refrain from despoiling both the living and the dead. It will be ours, or rather that of the whole community, to look after him in turn, freely and not under compulsion, and to put offerings for burial and other services into the collection box, as each one's piety and means allow. For he who serves the Gospel should also live by the Gospel, since he is worthy of double honour, as the Apostle says.

units.la: LIGNITII iussu Principis Friderici Valentinus Crautwald publice epistolas Paulinas exponit.
units.tr: At LIEGNITZ, by order of Prince Frederick, Valentin Crautwald publicly expounds the Pauline epistles.

units.la: GOLDBERGAE eiusdem Principis cura illustris schola erigitur, professoribus VVittembergâ evocatis Valentino Trocedorffio, & M. Joanne Helmeico.
units.tr: At GOLDBERG, under the care of the same Prince, a distinguished school is founded, with professors summoned from Wittenberg: Valentin Trocedorff and Master Johann Helmeich.

units.la: E BOE-
units.tr: FROM BOE-

units.la: ANNUS MDXXIII.
units.tr: THE YEAR 1523.

units.la: E BOEMIA profecti ad Lutherum legati Fratrum, quos vocant, fidem illi suam de sacramento Eucharistiae expositurunt: de quibus ita ille ad Nicolaum Hausmannum: De Pighardis iam non male sentio, audita eorum, praesentibus ipsis, fide circa Sacramentum Eucharistiae. Bohemos, qui parvulos communicant, non probo, quanquam non in hoc haereticos censeo. Et ad eundem alibi: Pighardi sic de sacramento sentiunt, quod Christus sub pane non sit corporaliter, quomodo aliqui dicunt, se vidisse ibi sanguinem & puerulum, &c. Sed spiritualiter seu sacramentaliter, hoc est, qui panem accipit visibiliter, vere accipit naturaliter eius sanguinem, qui a dextris patris sedet, sed invisibiliter. Ultra hoc non possum eos damnare. Deinde quod non adorant, ad idem referunt, quod non sit ibi visibiliter, ut visiones habent, sed invisibiliter, hoc est ad dexteram patris.
units.tr: Envoys of the Brethren, as they are called, set out from Bohemia to Luther to set forth their faith concerning the sacrament of the Eucharist. He wrote of them thus to Nicolaus Hausmann: I now think not badly of the Picards, having heard their faith concerning the sacrament of the Eucharist, they being present. I do not approve of the Bohemians who give communion to little children, although I do not judge them heretics on this account. And to the same man elsewhere: The Picards hold this view of the sacrament, that Christ is not bodily under the bread, as some say, that they have seen there blood and a little child, etc. But spiritually or sacramentally, that is, he who visibly receives the bread truly receives naturally his blood, which sits at the right hand of the Father, but invisibly. Beyond this I cannot condemn them. As for their not adoring, they refer it to the same point: that Christ is not there visibly, as they have visions, but invisibly, that is, at the right hand of the Father.

units.la: In GALLIA gratia Evangelica annunciabatur hoc anno publice Gratianopoli & Meldis.
units.tr: In France the gospel of grace was publicly proclaimed this year at Grenoble and at Meaux.

units.la: GRATIANOPOLI in Delphinatu Petrus Sebevilla religionem puriorem docet, quem Zwinglius decima tertia Decembris die per epistolam monet: ut in Galliis Christiana armatura munitus in publicum prodeat, sublataque, instar tubae voce, Evangelium Christi, invitis omnibus pappis & Papis praedicet. Christus, inquit, Classi-cum cum cecinit, impressionem in Pharisaos, Scribas & hypocritas facturus. Quis dexteram ad prelium non armabit? Leo rugiet, inquit Propheta, quis non metuet? Christo per ministros suos detonante, quis ex hostibus non pavebit? imo dispeream, si non in totis castris illorum trepidatur: adeo vertuntur, rotantur, ambigunt, ut quid consilii sequuturi sint, nondum exploratum habeant. Nam si Christi gregem mactare per seductos Principes coeperint, verentur, ne sic aperiatur fenestra, ut in se quoq; paulo post irruatur. Si vero scriptura obsistere tentent, conscy sibi violentia, quam ei faciunt, toti frigent ac concidunt. Quid igitur in ignavos non irruimus, uno illoq; satis forti verbi DEI praesidio fulti? Is enim Antichristum interficiet spiritu oris sui. Stat a nobis Christus, quis contra nos? Simus licet Samia vasa, nemo tamen confringere nos poterit, quandiu nobis Dominus adest: aderit autem ex verbi sui certa promissione, qua pollicitus est, se nobiscum mansurum usque ad mundi consummationem: iussitque securos esse, cum ad Reges & Principes illius causa trahamur: daturum enim esse sapientiam & eloquentiam, cui omnes adversarij non poterint resistere. Quid igitur adhuc cunctamur? Victoria in manibus est, an eam decerpere piget? Et paulo post: Non modo cum Antichristo sed cum universo simul orbe certamen tibi subeundum est, si quidem caelestia ambis: ea enim solis eis eveniunt, qui terrena negligunt. Ante omnia igitur opus est, ut te ipsum abneges, ac quotidie moriaris. Id autem tuopte Marte non poteris: ad unam igitur Dei misericordiam confugiendum, & illic flagitandum, ut vias tuas dirigat, mentem illustret, cor excitet, ut illius gratia nihil non tum audeas, tum, quo pacto fieri oporteat, scias. Proderit & illud, Evangelii Christi praedicare molienti, ut reiectis omnibus praesumptis opinionibus & doctrinis, hoc consilio ad literas vere sacras accedat, ut eas praeceptorem habiturus sit, non discipulum.
units.tr: At Grenoble in Dauphiné, Pierre Sebeville taught the purer religion. Zwingli urged him by letter on 13 December to come forward in public in France, armed with the Christian armour, and, lifting his voice like a trumpet, to preach the Gospel of Christ, though all the priests and Popes were opposed. Christ, he says, when he sounded the trumpet call, was about to make an assault on the Pharisees, scribes and hypocrites. Who will not arm his right hand for battle? The lion will roar, says the Prophet; who will not fear? With Christ thundering through his ministers, who among the enemy will not tremble? Indeed, may I perish if there is not trembling through their whole camp. So they turn, whirl and waver, that they do not yet know what plan they will follow. For if they begin to slaughter Christ's flock through deceived princes, they fear that a window will be opened through which they themselves will be attacked shortly after. If they try to resist Scripture, conscious of the violence they do to it, they grow cold and collapse entirely. Why then do we not rush upon these cowards, supported by that one sufficiently strong defence, the Word of God? For he will slay Antichrist with the breath of his mouth. Christ stands with us; who is against us? Though we be Samian vessels, no one will be able to break us as long as the Lord is with us. He will be with us by the sure promise of his word, in which he pledged that he would remain with us until the consummation of the world, and he bade us be unafraid when we are dragged before kings and princes for his cause, for he will give wisdom and eloquence, which all adversaries will be unable to resist. Why then do we still delay? Victory is in our hands; does it grieve you to pluck it? A little later: You must enter the contest not only with Antichrist but with the whole world at once, if indeed you aim at heavenly things, for these fall only to those who neglect earthly things. Above all, therefore, you must deny yourself and die daily. This you cannot do by your own strength, so you must flee to God's mercy alone and there beg that he direct your ways, enlighten your mind and stir your heart, so that by his grace you may dare everything and know how it must be done. It will also help you, who intend to preach the Gospel of Christ, to reject all presumed opinions and doctrines and approach the truly sacred letters with this purpose: that you will have them as your teacher, not as your pupil.

units.la: MELDA, oppidum est in Galliis, decem a Parisiorum Lutetia milliaribus. Eius Episcopus hoc anno fuit Guilielmus Brissonnettus, qui cum doctrinae purioris esset admodum studiosus, idoneos etiam doctores populo praefecit, exclusis Monachis. Lutetiae Jacobum Fabrum, Guilielmum Fatellum, Arnoldum & Gerardum Russum vocavit, qui magna alacritate populum erudiere. Quum autem hoc nomine periculum Episcopo crearent Theologi Sorbonistae, non praestitit constantiam, & ab incepto destitit. Tamen multorum animis religio implantata, & cum doctores pariter & auditores nonnulli inde fugati in alia atque alia Galliae loca se recepissent, mirabili Dei consilio, unius Ecclesiae destructio, multarum fuit aedificatio.
units.tr: Meaux is a town in France, ten miles from Lutetia of the Parisians. Its bishop this year was Guillaume Briçonnet, who, being very keen on purer doctrine, also set suitable teachers over the people, excluding the monks. At Paris he summoned Jacques Lefèvre, Guillaume Farel, Arnold and Gérard Roussel, who with great zeal instructed the people. But when the Sorbonne theologians created danger for the bishop on this account, he did not keep his constancy and desisted from what he had begun. Yet religion was planted in the minds of many, and when the teachers, as well as some hearers, had been driven out from there and had withdrawn to various other places in France, by the wonderful counsel of God the destruction of one church became the building up of many.

units.la: HAMBURGUM M. Stephanus Kempè Franciscanus hoc anno venit, ingenio & facundiâ & magnitudine animi M. Ordonem Stifelium superans, qui à præfectis Cœnobij Mariæ Magdalenæ ad docendi Evangelii munus in eo templo vocatus, inter acerrimos cum Sacrificulis conflictus, magno concursu & applausu civium triennium fere solus æstum & laborem dici sustinuit, donec Joannes Zegenhagius, Magdeburgoad Ecclesiam D. Nicolai, & paulo post Joannes Frizius Lubecâ, ad parochiæ D. Jacobi gubernationem vocati, fideliter in Evangelii propagatione Stephanum adiuverunt.
units.tr: At Hamburg Master Stephan Kempe, a Franciscan, came this year, surpassing Master Ordo Stifelius in talent, eloquence and greatness of spirit. He had been called by the prefects of the monastery of Mary Magdalene to the office of teaching the Gospel in that church. Amid very fierce conflicts with the sacrificing priests, he bore almost alone for about three years the heat and labour of the day, with great crowds and applause from the citizens, until Johannes Zegenhagen, called from Magdeburg to the church of St Nicholas, and a little later Johannes Frisius, called from Lübeck to govern the parish of St James, faithfully helped Stephan in spreading the Gospel.

units.la: HALAM Suevorum Joannes Isenmannus Halensis à Senatu vocatur, ut defuncto pastori succedat. Is non solùm eadem cum Brentio docebat, sed impias Papismi ceremonias abrogare incipiebat. In odium igitur multorum incurrit: præsertim cum Brentius hucusque Missas celebrasset. Ibi tum Brentius publicè se excusavit, rationem sui consilii exponens in hanc sententiam: Optimi auditores, audio quosdam vestrum nostris actionibus offendi: & quidem verum est, ego quoque aliquoties Missam hic apud vos celebravi, sed non per omnia sacrificulorum more, impietate horrenda, sacrificij scilicet pro vivis & defunctis oblatione, omissâ: idque propter vos vos à me factum est. Nam cum primùm huc à vobis essem vocatus, in profundum idololatriæ vos immersos reperi, ideo aliquid erat faciendum: & ad vos in lacum descendi, ut vos educerem, & liberarem paulatim erudiendo, & nonnihil etiam, exemplo Apostoli, ad tempus cedendo & simulando. Iam verò rectius ex verbo Dei à me estis instituti, & horrendam Missæ abominationem, & cænæ Dominicæ prophanationem intelligitis. Ideò abroganda.
units.tr: At Hall in Swabia, Johannes Isenmann of Hall was called by the Senate to succeed the deceased minister. He not only taught the same things as Brenz, but also began to abolish the impious ceremonies of Papism. He therefore incurred the hatred of many, especially since Brenz had until then celebrated Masses. Brenz then excused himself publicly, setting out the reason for his plan in these words: Most excellent hearers, I hear that some of you are offended by our actions. And indeed it is true that I too have celebrated Mass here among you several times, but not in every respect in the manner of the sacrificing priests, omitting the horrible impiety of offering a sacrifice for the living and the dead. And this was done by me on your account. For when I was first called here by you, I found you immersed in the depths of idolatry, so something had to be done. I came down to you into the pit to lead you out and free you gradually by teaching, and somewhat also, after the Apostle's example, by yielding and dissembling for a time. But now you have been instructed more rightly by me from the Word of God, and you understand the horrible abomination of the Mass and the profanation of the Lord's Supper. Therefore it must be abolished.

units.la: Cæterùm Missa anno demum 1527. abrogata est: nisi quod Joannitæ missificârunt usque ad 1534. annum: ad quos multi patritii exiverunt: donec & hæc Missa silere iussa est, templo concluso: ut 1540. omnis Missa in ipsorum ditione extra urbem.
units.tr: But the Mass was not finally abolished until 1527, except that the Johannites kept up the Mass until 1534, and many patricians left for them. Then this Mass too was ordered to be silenced and the church closed, so that by 1540 every Mass in their territory outside the city had been abolished.

units.la: Augustæ Joannes Speiserus Theologiæ Doctor, Parochus Augustanorum coepit verbum Dei concionari sincerius, tanto concursu & fructu, ut meretrices quoq; eius concionibus motæ, ad meliorem frugem redirent, ac prostibulo, quod tùc publicè prope Geggingensem portam tolerabatur, deserto, aut honesta coniugia quærerent, aut aliò inde diffugerent. Sed rediit Speiserus ad Pontificios, & miserè periisse dicitur.
units.tr: At Augsburg Johannes Speiser, Doctor of Theology and parish priest of the Augustinians, began to preach the Word of God more sincerely, with such a crowd and such fruit that prostitutes, moved by his sermons, returned to a better way of life. Abandoning the brothel that was then publicly tolerated near the Geggingen gate, they either sought honourable marriages or went away elsewhere. But Speiser returned to the Papists, and is said to have perished miserably.

units.la: Lutherus ad Augustanos consolatoriam mittit epistolam, quæ exstat Tom. 2. Germ. Jenens.
units.tr: Luther sent a consoling letter to the Augsburgers, which is extant in volume 2 of the German Jena edition.

units.la: Eslingæ Imperii oppido Michaël Stifelius discipulos Christo colligit, quibus cum Parochus Pontificius articulos aliquot opponeret, Lutherus per epistolam Eslingenses docuit, quomodo articulos psychotyranni sui deberent confutare.
units.tr: At Eßlingen, an imperial town, Michael Stifel gathered disciples to Christ. When a Papist parish priest opposed some articles to them, Luther taught the people of Eßlingen by letter how they should refute the articles of their soul-tyrant.

units.la: ARGENTINAM hoc anno veniunt Martinus Bucerus, VVeissenburgo, Caspar Hedio & VVolffgangus Fabritius Capito Moguntiâ: tria non solùm Ecclesiæ Argentinensis, sed orbis Christiani lumina. De his Nicolaus Gerbelius ad Joannem Schwebelium mense huius anni Decembri ita scribit: Evangelio mirificè prodest Hedio. Nam sinceritate vitæ, & gravitate docendi reliquorum sententias corroborat. Neque hactenus atrocioribus odiis res acta, sive quòd accesserit Hedio, sive quòd actum esse de rebus suis timeant, nescio. Bucerus Colossensem epistolam profitetur, Latinè modò, & Germanicè, accurrentibus, ligonibus, cerdonibus, Danistis, omnisq; generis hominibus. Hesternâ die Capito Præpositus noster innumerabili conveniente turbâ Colossensium epistolam enarrare cœpit ad S. Thomam. Interim Papistæ in caligas & calceos &c. Non credis, quantum autoritas Capitonis in populo efficiat. Deus incrementum det; ego optimè spero.
units.tr: In this year Martin Bucer came to Strasbourg from Weissenburg, and Caspar Hedio and Wolfgang Fabricius Capito from Mainz: three lights not only of the Church of Strasbourg but of the Christian world. Concerning them Nicolaus Gerbel writes to Johannes Schwebel in December of this year as follows: Hedio greatly benefits the gospel. For by the sincerity of his life and the seriousness of his teaching he strengthens the opinions of the rest. Nor until now has the affair been carried on with more bitter hatreds, whether because Hedio has come or because they fear for their own affairs, I do not know. Bucer is expounding the Epistle to the Colossians, now in Latin and now in German, with diggers, cobblers, Danzigers and all kinds of people flocking to him. Yesterday Capito, our provost, with an innumerable crowd gathering, began to expound the Epistle to the Colossians at St Thomas's. Meanwhile the Papists are at their wits' end. You do not believe how much authority Capito has with the people. May God give increase; I hope for the best.

units.la: In eadem urbe Kal. Decembribus Senatus mandat concionatoribus omnibus & singulis, ut Evangelium liberè & publicè prædicent: & auditoribus Dei ac proximi amorem imimplantent: mittant autem scommata in alios iacta, & omnia ea, quae vel scandalo esse infirmioribus, vel ad seditionem commovere animos possint.
units.tr: In the same city, on 1 December, the Senate orders all the preachers, each and every one, to preach the Gospel freely and publicly, and to implant in their hearers love of God and of neighbour. They are to refrain from throwing jokes at others, and from anything that could be a scandal to the weaker sort or stir the minds of the people to sedition.

units.la: LANDAVII Imperii oppido Joannes Baderus Pastor Ecclesiae variorum errorum Pontificios coargulr, & reiectis hominum commentis, solius Dei iussa auditoribus suis proponit.
units.tr: At LANDAU, a town of the Empire, John Bader, pastor of the church, refutes the Papists on their various errors, and, rejecting the inventions of men, sets before his hearers the commands of God alone.

units.la: ISENNACI Doctor Jacobus Straus Kal. Januariis cocionari, & non ita multo post idola demoliri, Missam Latinam abolere, & vehementi spiritu contra errores Pontificios detonare coepit. Itaq; a Decano & Capitulo aliquoties ad Joannem Saxoniae Ducem est accusatus. Docuit ibi in tertium annum.
units.tr: At ISENNACH, Doctor James Strauss began on 1 January to preach, and soon afterwards to tear down idols, abolish the Latin Mass, and thunder vehemently against the errors of the Papists. Therefore he was several times accused before John, Duke of Saxony, by the Dean and Chapter. He taught there for a third year.

units.la: VINARIAE disputatio habita fuit de quaestione: An Missa sit Sacrificium? Conclusum quod non.
units.tr: At VINARIA a disputation was held on the question: Is the Mass a sacrifice? It was concluded that it is not.

units.la: VVITTEMBERGAE Lutherus formulam Missae & communionis edit: in qua omnes ritus usitatos, introitum ex Psalmis, Kyrie, collectam, Epistolam, Sequentiam, Evangelium, Symbolon, Concionem, Preces, Praefationem, Sanctos, Precationem Dominicam: Verba coenae: Elevationem: Agnus Dei: Gratiarum actionem retinet. Canonem vero Missae, transformantem coenam Domini in sacrificiu pro vivis & defunctis prorsus omittit. Haec fuit prima reformatio rituum Missae & communionis, etsi Carolostadius tale quid etiam ante hoc tempus ausus fuerat. Revocata item est in usum Confessio auricularis, & privata absolutio, quam Carolostadius aboleverat.
units.tr: At WITTENBERG Luther published a form of the Mass and Communion, in which he retains all the customary rites: the introit from the Psalms, the Kyrie, the collect, the Epistle, the sequence, the Gospel, the Creed, the sermon, the prayers, the preface, the Sanctus, the Lord's Prayer, the words of the supper, the elevation, the Agnus Dei, and the thanksgiving. He entirely omits the canon of the Mass, which turns the Lord's Supper into a sacrifice for the living and the dead. This was the first reform of the rites of the Mass and Communion, although Carlstadt had dared something of the kind even before this time. Likewise auricular confession and private absolution, which Carlstadt had abolished, were restored to use.

units.la: Ad Fridericum Saxoniæ Electorem vir quidam doctus libellum scribit Germanicâ linguâ, quo docet: tres esse capitales errores, quibus in Papatu Christiani fuerint seducti.
units.tr: A certain learned man writes a little book in German to Frederick, Elector of Saxony, in which he teaches that there are three chief errors by which Christians were seduced under the Papacy.

units.la: 1. De libero arbitrio, quod revera sit servum arbitrium.
units.tr: 1. Concerning free will, which is in truth a enslaved will.

units.la: 2. De meritis operum, quæ potius sint fidei.
units.tr: 2. Concerning the merits of works, which are rather the fruits of faith.

units.la: 3. De traditionibus hominum, cum in solo Dei verbo fuerit acquiescendum.
units.tr: 3. Concerning the traditions of men, since one ought to rest in the Word of God alone.

units.la: Nicolaus Ambsdorffius præfationem prefixit libello isti, quâ demonstrat è scripturis: Papam esse Antichristum.
units.tr: Nicolaus Amsdorf prefixed a preface to this little book, in which he demonstrates from the Scriptures that the Pope is Antichrist.

units.la: Hoc eodem anno publicabatur & alius libellus, suppresso autoris nomine, in quo docebatur, quàm horribiliter doctrina Christi, de castissimo Dei cultu, precatione, depravata fuerit in Papatu: dum à vero Deo ad veneratio-nem creaturarum homines sunt avocati.
units.tr: In this same year another little book was published, with the author's name suppressed, in which it was taught how horribly the doctrine of Christ concerning the most pure worship of God and prayer had been corrupted under the Papacy, while men were called away from the true God to the veneration of creatures.

units.la: Huius generis complures alii libelli Germanicâ linguâ prodierunt hoc anno, quibus velut è profundo somno sensim suscitabātur, qui in idolomania Pontificia indormierant.
units.tr: Several other books of this kind appeared in German this year, by which those who had slumbered in Papist idolatry were gradually roused, as if from a deep sleep.

units.la: In HELVETIA Basileæ, Bernę, Tiguri, in oppido San-galli circa religionis negotium hæc facta.
units.tr: In SWITZERLAND, at Basel, Bern, Zurich, and in the town of St Gall, the following was done concerning religious affairs.

units.la: BASILEÆ Senatus Lectores Theologiæ ordina-
units.tr: At BASEL the Senate appoints ordinary lecturers in theology:

units.la: Vita Pelli-canai. dinarios constituit, Joannem Oecolampadium, & Conradum Pellicanum: & quoniam Antonius Zanckerus, Pastor ad S. Martinum, officii sui munia obire tum non potuit, Curatorum Ecclesiae illius rogatu Oecolampadius vices illius supplevit: qui inter alia epistolam Joannis Apostoli Catholicam primam interpretatus est, quam anno 1524. typis descriptam, Christophoro Basilien-sium Episcopo nuncupavit.
units.tr: John Oecolampadius and Conrad Pellican (Life of Pellicanus). And since Anton Zanker, pastor at St Martin's, could not then carry out the duties of his office, at the request of the curates of that church Oecolampadius took over his duties. Among other things he translated the first Catholic Epistle of the Apostle John, which he had printed in 1524 and dedicated to Christoph, Bishop of Basel.

units.la: <bl>Bernae</bl> Magistratus 15. Junii edictum publicat in causa Religionis, cuius summa: Cum discrepantes de fide sententiae audiantur pro concione, & alii in alios fulminent, velle Magistratum, ut concionatores ad unum omnes Evangelium, hoc est, doctrinam à Deo revelatam, & quaecunq; ex scriptis Propheticis & Apostolicis defendi possint, in clara luce suorum auditoriorum enuntient. Quicquid autem scripturis sacris adversatur, sive illud à Luthero, sive ab aliis dictum, scriptumve sit, ne attingant. Seditiosa ne loquantur: Qui secus fecerint, iis poenam iustam decretam.
units.tr: At <bl>BERN</bl> the Magistrate on 15 June publishes an edict in the matter of religion, the substance of which is this: since differing opinions on faith are heard from the pulpit, and some thunder against others, the Magistrate wishes all the preachers, without exception, to set forth the Gospel, that is, the doctrine revealed by God, and whatever can be defended from the prophetic and apostolic writings, in the clear light of their hearers. But whatever is opposed to the Holy Scriptures, whether said or written by Luther or by others, they are not to touch. They are not to speak seditiously. Those who act otherwise are to receive a just penalty, as decreed.

units.la: <bl>Tigurini</bl> cum Zwinglii sui doctrinam passim ut impiam traduci intelligerent: ministris omnibus suae ditionis mandant: ut ad 29. Januarii diem, dissidii religionis causâ Tiguri conveniant: fore enim, ut omnes ibi, quantum satis est, audiatur. Constantiensem quoq; rogant Episcopum per literas amâter ut aut ipse veniat, aut è suis aliquem eò mittat. Quum igitur ad constitutum diem venissent frequentes, adesset etiā Episcopi Vicarius, Joannes Faber, consul verba facit: & quoniam de doctrina sit ortum valdè grave dissidium, idcirco decretum hunc esse conventum, ait, ut si quis omnium sit, qui contra Zwinglii doctrinam aliquid habeat, liberè illud nunc proponat. Zwinglius iam antè certis locis atque thematis doctrinam suam inoluserat, numero ad LXVII. & ut instructi venirent omnes ad eum conventum atque disputationem, evulgârat. Nunc ergo cum finem sermonis consul fecisset, rursus illa proponit, & ad congressum eos invitat. Ibi Faber posteaquam suæ missionis causam explicasset, conatur persuadere, certamen hoc non esse huius loci, verùm ad Concilii notionem pertinere, quod brevi sit futurum. Urgente autem Zwinglio, & postulante, si quid habeat, ut ne dissimulet, ille scripto se refutaturum ipsius dogmata, profitetur. Post multa utrinque commutata verba, cum ex omnibus nemo prodiret amplius in aciem, dimisso convetu Senatus per suos fines edicit: ut traditionibus hominum omissis, Evangelium purè doceatur, è veteris & novi Testamenti libris,
units.tr: When the <bl>Zurich</bl> people understood that the doctrine of their Zwingli was being denounced everywhere as impious, they order all the ministers of their territory to gather at Zurich on 29 January, for the sake of the dispute over religion, for it would come about that everyone there would be heard, as far as is sufficient. They also courteously ask the Bishop of Constance by letter either to come himself or to send someone of his own there. When therefore they had come in numbers on the appointed day, and the Bishop's vicar, John Faber, was present too, the consul spoke: and since a very grave dispute has arisen about doctrine, this meeting, he said, has been decreed so that, if anyone of them has anything against Zwingli's doctrine, he may now set it forth freely. Zwingli had already earlier made his doctrine known in certain places and in theses, numbering 67, and had published them so that everyone might come to that assembly and disputation prepared. Now, when the consul had finished his speech, he again put those forward and invited them to the encounter. There Faber, after explaining the reason for his mission, tries to persuade them that this contest does not belong to this place, but to the notion of a Council, which is soon to be held. But Zwingli pressed, and demanded that if he had anything he should not conceal it, and he declared that he would refute Zwingli's dogmas in writing. After many words had been exchanged on both sides, and when no one from all of them came forward into the battle line any longer, the meeting was dismissed, and the Senate, through its officials, proclaims throughout its territories that, with human traditions set aside, the Gospel be taught purely, from the books of the Old and New Testament,

units.la: Leo Judæ sub initium Februarii præficitur templo Petrino, nuptias celebrat decimâ nonâ Septembris,cum hoc eodem anno primi Sacerdotes uxores duxissent Wilhelmus Rublinus, & Joannes Faber. Jam ergo non in urbe tantum, sed & in agro aunūtiabatur Christus, qui & antea quoq; nō à paucis fuerat prædicatus parochis. Ecclesia aūt ita verbo veritatis imbuta est: ut maxima eius pars iam non tantum contemneret abusus & superstitionem, quæ nondū erat deposita, sed cuperet etiā omnia ea, quæ cerneret præter & contra scripturā verbi Dei in templis Dei vigere usurpariq;, penitus abiicere atq; conculcare. Id cum intelligeret Magistratus, ne quid rursus præpropere & immaturè, parūve religiosè geri videretur, denuo in urbem alteram convocat Synodum. Ad hanc vocati sunt Episcopi, Constantiensis, Curiensis, Basiliensis unà cū schola sive Universitate Basiliensi, vocati sunt confœderati omnes: sed non venerunt omnes, neq; quenquā miserūt Episcopi. Nihilominus posterior hæc priore multò fuit celebrior, Confluebāt enim doĉti & ęlari viri non pauci, confluebāt Ecclesiarū antistites & sacerdotes plus mins DC. Fiebat ē scripturis collatio, & præcipuè disputabatur cōtinuis trib. diebus, de tollendis ex Ecclesia imaginibus, & de abroganda Missa Papistica. Iterūq; vicit veritas, ac exaĉtis aliquot diebus, solūta est Synodus. Utriusq; disputationis asta inveniet lector ad finem Tom. 2. operum Zwinglii.
units.tr: Leo Jud was placed over the church of St Peter at the beginning of February, and celebrated his wedding on 19 September, since in this same year the first priests had taken wives: Wilhelm Röublin and Johann Faber. So now Christ was proclaimed not only in the city but also in the countryside, where he had earlier been preached by not a few rural pastors. The Church was so imbued with the word of truth that the greater part of it now not only despised the abuses and superstition, which had not yet been laid aside, but also desired to cast away completely and trample underfoot all those things which it saw flourishing and being used in the temples of God beyond and against the Scripture of God's word. When the Magistrate understood this, lest anything seem to be done again too hastily and prematurely, or somewhat irreligiously, it convened a second synod in another city. To this were summoned the Bishops of Constance and Chur, and of Basel, together with the school or University of Basel; all the allies were summoned. But not all came, nor did the bishops send anyone. Nevertheless this later meeting was much more crowded than the earlier one, for not a few learned and distinguished men flocked to it, and the leaders of the churches and priests, some 600. A comparison was made from the Scriptures, and chiefly for three continuous days there was debate on removing images from the Church and abolishing the Papist Mass. Again truth prevailed, and after some days had passed the synod was dissolved. The acts of both disputations the reader will find at the end of volume 2 of Zwingli's works.

units.la: MONIALES Psalmorum libros Latinos de manibus deponere, habitum religiosum exuere, & Monasteriis valedicere cœperunt, contractoq; matrimonio, factæ sunt matresfamilias. Leonhartus Köppen, civis Torgensis, feriâ tertiâ Paschatis, 7. Aprilis novem Moniales, genere nobiles, ex Monasterio Nimptschen extractas, VVittebergam adduxit, inter quas fuit Catharina à Boren, postea nupta Luthero.
units.tr: Nuns began to lay down the Latin Psalm books from their hands, to cast off their religious habit, and to bid farewell to the monasteries, and, having contracted marriage, became housewives. Leonhard Köppen, a citizen of Torgau, on the third day of Easter, 7 April, brought nine nuns, of noble birth, taken out of the monastery at Nimbschen, to Wittenberg, among whom was Catherine von Bora, afterwards married to Luther.

units.la: VRATISLAVIÆ primus Hieronymus Rachemeis uxorem duxit, Reginam Nimbisiam.
units.tr: At BRESLAU the first to take a wife was Hieronymus Rachemeis, who married Regina Nimbisia.

units.la: ARGENTINÆ Parochus S. Thomæ idem fecit, qua de re hæc leguntur Nicolai Gerbelii ad Joannem Schwebelium verba:
units.tr: At STRASBOURG the parish priest of St Thomas did the same, concerning which these words of Nicolaus Gerbel to John Schwebel are read:

units.la: Hodie apud nos mira & inaudita res acta, mi Ioannes. Nam quæ Christiana sunt, rara apud nos hactenus fuere. M. Antonius, Parochus olim S. Stephani, nunc S. Thomæ, aliquot annis scortillum apud se habuit, elegans sanè & non vulgari formâ: hanc diebus superioribus uxorem duxit, ductamque à suggestu palam populo vulgavit. Hodie verò 21. Aprilis, cum hæc scribimus, subinde hanc horam, in templi foribus apud D. Laurentium, per M. Matthiam Zellium, habitâ concione adplebe, in matrimonii commendatione, publicè introducitur, ducentib. sponsam duab. honestissimis matribus familias: sequentib. verò omnis generis hominibus, mirificè applaudentibus. Est autem hora diei 8. qua ingens homihominum multitudo ad rem novam, inauditam accurrit: fremunt Papistæ: exultant Christiani. E media plebe acclamat unus: Er hat ihm recht gethan/ Gott geb ihm tausent guter jahr. Tu, crede, multos hunc secuturos esse.
units.tr: Today among us a wonderful and unheard-of thing has happened, my John. For Christian things have hitherto been rare among us. Master Anton, once parish priest of St Stephen's and now of St Thomas', for some years kept a little whore with him, a truly elegant girl of no common appearance. In recent days he has married her, and, leading her up to the pulpit, has openly made it known to the people. Today, however, 21 April, as we write this, at about this hour, at the doors of the church of St Lawrence, through Master Matthias Zell, after a sermon in praise of marriage, the wedding is publicly introduced, the bride being led by two most honourable matrons, and following them men of every kind applauding wonderfully. It is the eighth hour of the day, when a huge crowd of people runs to the new and unheard-of thing. The Papists rage, Christians exult. From the midst of the common people one shouts out: He has done right by him; God give him a thousand good years. Believe me, many will follow him.

units.la: Sic igitur doctrina Evangelii hoc anno fuit propagata. Recognosce nunc mecum, Lector, quomodo fidelium accusationibus, divexationibus, morte denique fuerit confirmata, obsignata.
units.tr: Thus the doctrine of the Gospel was spread abroad this year. Now recall with me, reader, how it was confirmed and sealed by the accusations, persecutions, and finally the deaths of the faithful.

units.la: Accusabantur, Fridericus Elector Saxoniæ, Lutherus, Zwinglius, Pellicanus, civitates, Augusta, Argentina, Norimberga: Concionatores item, Norimbergenses, & Argentoratenses.
units.tr: Accused were Frederick, Elector of Saxony, Luther, Zwingli, Pellicanus, the cities of Augsburg, Strasbourg, and Nuremberg; likewise the preachers of Nuremberg and Strasbourg.

units.la: Fridericum Saxoniæ Electorem Adrianus Papa publico scripto (Bullam vocant) graviter accusat neglecti officii in puniendo vel ejiciendo Luthero: Monet, rogat, obsecrat, ut vel tandem id faciat. Ni pareat, gladium Pontificium & Cæsareum experturus.
units.tr: Pope Adrian, in a public document (they call it a bull), gravely accuses Frederick, Elector of Saxony, of neglecting his duty in punishing or expelling Luther. He warns, asks, and beseeches him to do so at last; if he does not obey, he will feel the Papal and Caesarean sword.

units.la: Lutherum ad conventum Noricum accusabat legatus Pontificius, quod Mahometo esset similimus, siquidem, ut ille per polygamiam, ita hic per dissolutionem votorum castitatis frena laxet cupiditatibus: quod statum Ecclesiæ convellat, & idcirco ne quidem auditus damnandus sit: quod denique, ut nunc in Ecclesiasticos, ita paulo pòst in politicos sit sæviturus. Cui quid responsum, supra retulimus.
units.tr: The Papal legate at the Diet of Nuremberg accused Luther of being very like Muhammad, since, just as the one indulges his desires through polygamy, so the other loosens the reins of lust by dissolving vows of chastity; he overturns the state of the Church, and for this reason he should be condemned without even being heard; and finally, just as he now rages against churchmen, so soon he will rage against the civil authorities. What answer was given to this, we have related above.

units.la: Accusabant eundem ad Electorem duo potentissimi Reges, Henricus VIII. Angliæ, & Ludovicus, Hungariæ & Boëmiæ Rex. Quibus nihil aliud ab Electore responsum, quàm, Lutherum in concilio prius audiendum, quàm damnandum.
units.tr: Two very powerful kings, Henry VIII of England and Louis, king of Hungary and Bohemia, likewise accused him to the Elector. To them the Elector replied only that Luther should be heard in a council before he is condemned.

units.la: Zwinglio in publicis Helvetiorum Comitiis, Bernæ celebratis, crimen hoc intentabatur, quod pro concione dixisset non semel: Helvetios, qui cum exteris iniis-sent fœdus, Christianorum sanguinem vendere, & vesci carnibus humanis.
