Quod ubi ille, legatis Tigurinorum domum revertis, resciv it, ilico per apologiam se purgavit.
units.tr: Zwingli was charged, at the public assembly of the Swiss held at Bern, with the crime that he had more than once said in a sermon that the Swiss, who had made alliances with foreigners, sell Christian blood and feed on human flesh. When he learned this, on returning home from the envoys of Zurich, he at once cleared himself by an apology.

units.la: Cunradus Pellicanus, Joan. Kreis, & Joan. Luthart, ut propter fidem novam monasterio eijciantur, Provincialis Setzgertus à Senatu Basilien si petit. At ille decernit: si hi eijciantur, omnes eiiciendos. Erant autem numero quadraginta.
units.tr: Conrad Pellicanus, Johann Kreis, and Johann Luthart were sought by the provincial Setzger from the senate of Basel, that they be expelled from the monastery on account of the new faith. But the senate decreed: if these are expelled, all must be expelled. There were forty of them.

units.la: Legatis Civitatum Imperii Hispaniam missis, Cæsar liberaliter respondit: sed Pontificem apud se questum ait per literas de Augusta, Argentorato, Norimberga, quasi doctrinæ Lutheri faveant, nec suis & Pontificiis edictis obtemperent. Cui illi, nihil à suis prætermitti diligentiæ, quò ipsius voluntati satisfiat.
units.tr: When envoys of the cities of the Empire were sent to Spain, the Emperor replied graciously; but he said that the Pope had complained to him by letter about Augsburg, Strasbourg, and Nuremberg, as though they favoured the doctrine of Luther and did not obey his own and the Papal edicts. To this they replied that nothing was neglected by their diligence, so that his wishes might be satisfied.

units.la: NORIMBERGENSIS Ecclesiæ Ministros legatus Pontificius in conventu Norico accusaverat, tanquam impia docerent, & ut in vincula conjicerentur, postulabat. Principes autem existimare se dicunt, falsò quædam ad ipsum esse delata: illos etiam in honore esse, ac placere populo: si quid in eos admittatur, fore, ut sic illud omnes accipiant, quasi consultò fiat, veritatis opprimendæ causâ, quæ quidem res motum excitare queat. Se tamen delecturos esse, qui de re tota perquirant inposterum, & quod æquum est, statuant.
units.tr: The Papal legate at the Diet of Nuremberg had accused the ministers of the Nuremberg Church, as though they taught impious things, and demanded that they be cast into chains. The princes, however, said that they thought certain things had been falsely reported to him: those men were also in good repute and pleasing to the people; if anything were done against them, everyone would take it as though it were done deliberately, for the sake of suppressing the truth, which indeed could stir up a commotion. Nevertheless, they would appoint men to inquire into the whole matter in future, and decide what is fair.

units.la: ARGENTINENSES Concionatores, Zellius, Capito, Firnius, non uno modo exagitabantur.
units.tr: The preachers of Strasbourg, Zell, Capito, and Firn, were harassed in more than one way.

units.la: MATTHIAS Cellius à patrono fisci Episcopalis hæreseos accusabatur. Is justo volumine publicato, in quo summam religionis & fidei suæ complexus est, innocentiam suam defendit.
units.tr: Matthias Zell was accused of heresy by the advocate of the episcopal treasury. He published a large volume, in which he summarised the whole of his religion and faith, and defended his innocence.

units.la: CAPITONI Præposito Thomano tria intentabantur crimina: quod adscribi se in civitatem Argentinensium voluerit: quod publicè concionatus sit: quod in oculis urbis totius cum Pontificiis super Religionis negotio disserere unicè cupiverit. Is edita Apologia Germanica, respondet. CIVEUM sel factum, & Præsentatorum multorum exemplo, & salvo jure Episcopi: idque ideo, quod omnis anianima potestati civili subiecta esse debeat, & æquum sit, ut, qui iisdem cum civibus gaudent commodis, onera quoque cum iis portent. Cumq; sibi insidientur nonnulli e clero, jure se ad Magistratus urbici patrocinium confugisse. AD CONCIONANDUM se protractum, tum dissidio civium, quorum alii Matthiæ Cellio, concionatori Evangelico, alii Pontificiis doctoribus adhæserant, tum rogatu multorum, sinistro deniq; plurimorum de se iudicio, quasi Evangelii ipsum suppudeat. Postremo AD DISPVTATIONEM publicam prius non provocasse, quàm Matthias Cellius hæreseos, ipse Capito & hæreseos, & nequitiæ à pastore quodam pagano fuisset damnatus.
units.tr: Three charges were brought against Capito, provost of St Thomas: that he had wished to be enrolled as a citizen of Strasbourg; that he had preached publicly; and that before the whole city he had especially desired to debate the question of religion with the Papists. He, having published a German Apology, replies. As to citizenship, he did it by the example of many citizens and presentators, and without prejudice to the bishop's right; and this because every soul ought to be subject to the civil power, and it is fair that those who share the same benefits as the citizens should also bear the burdens with them. And since some of the clergy were plotting against him, he had rightly fled to the protection of the city magistracy. As to preaching, he was drawn into it by the discord of the citizens, some of whom had attached themselves to Matthias Zell, the Evangelical preacher, others to the Papist teachers; and by the request of many, and finally by the unfavourable judgement of most people about himself, as though he were ashamed of the Gospel. Lastly, as to a public disputation, he had not challenged anyone before Matthias Zell had been condemned for heresy by a certain rural pastor, and Capito himself for heresy and wickedness.

units.la: ANTONIUM FIRNIUM Parochum S. Thomæ, quod uxorem, & quidem primus duxisset, ab officio removet Capitulum Thomanum. Antonius Senatus opem implorat. Idem faciunt cives nonnulli per libellum supplicem, in quo indignissimum esse conquer/ untur: improbari honestum coniugium, scortationes & fœdas libidines probari.
units.tr: The chapter of St Thomas removed Antonius Firn, parish priest of St Thomas, from his office, because he had married a wife, and indeed was the first to do so. Antonius implores the help of the senate. Several citizens do the same by a supplicating pamphlet, in which they complain that it is most unworthy: that an honourable marriage is disapproved of, while fornication and foul lusts are approved.

units.la: DIVEXATI ob professionem Evangelicam fuêre plurimi.
units.tr: Very many were harassed on account of their Evangelical profession.

units.la: MILTENBERGA ditionis Moguntinæ est oppidum ad Mœnum. Audierunt eius incolæ Doctorem Joannem Draconem Karolostadium, sincerae fidei præconem, annum integrum, & quidem magnâ devotione. Fremit & frendet, quicquid est sacrificulorum in oppido: accusatur Joannes ad præfectos Moguntinos: à sacrificulo quodam etiam excommunicatur. Sed sacerdos ille periculum vitæ vix effugit, à Joanne adversus furentem populum defensus. Præfecti Miltenbergensibus mandant, si vitam, si bona salva velint, Pastorem dimittant. Parent illi, Diaconum Evangelicum retinent. Abit Draco, & cum eo, metu plebis, omnes sacrificuli urbem deserunt, securitatem vitæ à Præfectis petentes. Illi oppidum vi armatâ invadunt, Diaconū capiunt, civibus lectionem pomorum sarcastice mandant, lectione Bibliorum interdicunt, & imposito præsidio omnes ad Papisticarum ceremoniarum usum cogunt. Qui ad capiendum Diaconum in viduæ cuiusdam domum missus erat satelles, in eius amplexus irruens Diaconus, salve, inquit, mi frater: frater enimvero meus es: en adsum, transfode me, vel suffoca me. Cui satelles, quasi coelitus immutatus: Domine, à me quidem nihil mali exspectes. Cumq; rustici accurrissent, Diaconum perempturi, illorum quoque impetum satelles ille prohibuit. Milteberga igitur prima inter Germaniæ civitates propter Evangelium vim passa est.
units.tr: Miltenberg is a town of the Mainz territory on the Main. Its inhabitants heard Doctor Johann Draco Karlstadt, a herald of sincere faith, for a whole year, and that with great devotion. All the priestlings in the town rage and gnash their teeth; John is accused before the Mainz prefects, and is even excommunicated by a certain priestling. But that priest barely escaped with his life, having been defended by John against the raging people. The prefects order the people of Miltenberg, if they wish to keep life and goods safe, to dismiss the pastor. They obey, but keep the Evangelical deacon. Draco leaves, and with him, out of fear of the people, all the priestlings desert the town, seeking safety of life from the prefects. Those men invade the town with an armed force, seize the deacon, sarcastically order the citizens to read the pomes, forbid the reading of the Bible, and, by setting a garrison, force everyone to the practice of the Papist ceremonies. A bodyguard who had been sent to seize the deacon at the house of a certain widow was rushing into his embrace when the deacon said, "Hail, my brother: for you are indeed my brother; behold, I am here, pierce me through, or choke me." The bodyguard, as though changed by heaven, said: "Lord, you need expect no harm from me." When the peasants had run up, intending to kill the deacon, that bodyguard also restrained their attack. Thus Miltenberg, first among the cities of Germany, suffered violence on account of the Gospel.

units.la: Lutherus Miltebergenses epistolâ consolatur, argumentatis: quod ferant ista in causa Dei: sa Dei: quòd momentaneæ sint afflictiones, & quidem corporis bonorumq; fortunæ, nō animi: quòd vindicta optima sit Christianorum, gloriari in cruce: quòd etiam in illis adimpletum illud: Ex ore infantium & lactentium fundasti virtutem, ut aboleres inimicum & ultore. Deniq; quod sub pœna capitis & bonorum Miltebergensibus interdictum erat colloquiis de Dei verbo, consulit illis, ut qui fortes spiritu sunt, mandatum illud floccifaciant: qui infirmiores sunt, tacitè in Domino gaudeant, Deumq; rogent: ut animet se quoq; ad publicam veritatis professionem.
units.tr: Luther consoles the people of Miltenberg by letter, with arguments: that they bear these things in the cause of God; that the afflictions are momentary, and of body and goods, not of soul; that vengeance is the best of Christians, to glory in the cross; that also in these things that saying is fulfilled: "Out of the mouth of infants and sucklings thou hast ordained strength, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger." Finally, since it was forbidden to the people of Miltenberg, under penalty of death and loss of goods, to hold conversations about the Word of God, he advises them that those who are strong in spirit should make light of that command, and those who are weaker should rejoice quietly in the Lord and pray God that he might also encourage them to the public profession of the truth.

units.la: Eosdem Miltenbergenses epistolâ plenâ spiritu Erfurto missa solatur D. Joannes Draco Carlstadius, primus illorum Evangelista. Proponit illis consideranda: voluntatem Dei: osculum crucis sponso Christo apud sponsam suam solenne: <bl>συνφόρον</bl> Christu ipsum: crucem perpetuam Evangelii prædicati & crediti sociam: baptismum in conformitatem crucis & gloriæ Christi: persecutionis fructum: fidelitatem Dei, nō onerantis nos supra vires: preces multarum Ecclesiarum pro ipsis.
units.tr: Doctor Johann Draco Karlstadt, the first of their evangelists, consoles the same people of Miltenberg by a letter full of spirit, sent from Erfurt. He sets before them things to consider: the will of God; the kiss of the cross, a solemn thing between the bridegroom Christ and his bride; the fellow-yoked Christ himself; the cross, the perpetual companion of the Gospel preached and believed; baptism, into conformity with the cross and the glory of Christ; the fruit of persecution; the faithfulness of God, who does not burden us beyond our strength; and the prayers of many Churches for them.

units.la: HARTMUNDUS à Cronberg, capto oppido Cronberg à Ludovico Electore Palatino, Richardo Trevirensi, Philippo Hassiæ Landgravio, in exilium pellitur. Solatur autem seipsum Epistolâ ad Argentinenses: quod præviderit hanc Evangelii sortem: quòd Dei volunvoluntate, quòd innocens denique, quippe propter solam Evangelii professionem, hæc talia patiatur. Lutherus feriâ quartâ post Invocavit (verbis ipsius utor) ad Georgium Spalatinum, D. Hartmannus Cronbergius, inquit, jussus Alberto Comiti à Mansfeld, nobiscum est, et utrumque in monasterio prandio excepimus, vir tanta passus, adhuc satis firmus in fide stat.
units.tr: Hartmund von Cronberg, when the town of Cronberg had been taken by Louis, Elector Palatine, Richard of Trier, and Philip, Landgrave of Hesse, was driven into exile. He consoles himself by a letter to the Strasbourgers: that he foresaw this lot of the Gospel; that it is by God's will; and that he, innocent, suffers such things solely on account of the profession of the Gospel. Luther, on the Wednesday after Invocavit (I use his own words), writes to Georg Spalatin: "Doctor Hartmann von Cronberg," he says, "sent by Count Albert of Mansfeld, is with us, and we have entertained both of us at dinner in the monastery; a man who has suffered such things still stands sufficiently firm in the faith."

units.la: JOANNES OECOLAMPADIUS de se, & ULRICO Hutteнo ad Hedionem 21. Januarii hoc scribit: Sunt hic (Basileæ) ex Sacerdotib. & Theologis, qui de me pessimè loqui cupiunt: nec desistunt, ubi clam conveniunt. Tantum machinati, ut Hutteнo non fuerit tutum diutius hic agere: unde & nudiustertius hinc discesserit: quorsum autem, nescio.
units.tr: Johannes Oecolampadius writes this about himself and Ulrich Hutten to Hedio, on 21 January: "There are here (at Basel) some of the priests and theologians, who wish to speak very ill of me, and they do not desist whenever they meet secretly. They have plotted so much that it was not safe for Hutten to stay here any longer; wherefore he also left the day before yesterday; whither, I do not know."

units.la: ARSATIUS Sehoverus iuvenis à Theologis Ingolstadianis squalore carceris & mortis propositæ metu ad canendam septimâ Septembris palinodiam, adactus fuit. Quam rem indignissimè tulit nobilis fœmina, Argula de Grumbach, & per literas super ea cum Bavariæ Duce expostulavit. Arsatius pœnitentiâ ductus, è monasterio, in quod detrusus erat, profugit, Vvittebergam venit, lapsum confessus absolutus, & in Prussiam missus est, ad docendum Evangelium, unde reversus in Ducatu Vvirtembergico 1536. Lembergæ, & postea Vvinedæ ad annum usque 1542. docuit, editâ Postillâ, & fidei suæ consessione. JOAN-
units.tr: Arsatius Sehoverus, a young man, was forced by the theologians of Ingolstadt, through the squalor of his prison and the fear of the death that had been threatened, to sing a palinode on 7 September. The noblewoman Argula von Grumbach took this very badly and protested about it to the Duke of Bavaria in a letter. Moved by repentance, Arsatius fled from the monastery into which he had been thrust, came to Wittenberg, confessed his fall and was absolved, and was sent to Prussia to teach the Gospel. From there he returned and taught in the Duchy of Württemberg: at Lemberg in 1536, and afterwards at Winnenden until 1542. He published a postil and a confession of his faith. JOAN-

units.la: JOANNES VOIGT Monachus Franciscanus Vinariæ in Thuringia propter purioris doctrinæ professionem duriter à fratribus suis tractatur.
units.tr: Johannes Voigt, a Franciscan monk at Weimar in Thuringia, was harshly treated by his brothers because he professed a purer doctrine.

units.la: JOANNES APPEL & FRIDERICUS FISCHER, Canonici & Consiliarii Episcopi VVürtzburgensis, quod uxores duxissent, & Evangelio faverent, incarcerantur, & post trium mensium captivitatem, interveniente Cæsarei regiminis petitione, ægrè ab Episcopo dimittuntur.
units.tr: Johannes Appel and Friedrich Fischer, canons and councillors of the Bishop of Würzburg, were imprisoned because they had taken wives and favoured the Gospel. After three months in captivity, at the request of the imperial government, they were released by the bishop only with difficulty.

units.la: CASPAREM HEDIONEM antequam Argentinam abiret Moguntiæ cum fratribus nonnullis Pontificii acerrimè prosequuntur. Joannes Reiffenstenius Hedionem ad Constantiam hortatur divino hoc epistolio:
units.tr: Before he left for Strasbourg, Caspar Hedio was vigorously pursued at Mainz by the Papists, together with some of his brothers. Johannes Reiffenstein urged Hedio to go to Constance in this divine letter:

units.la: Gratissimum mihi est, quod Sacerdotes Papistici te, Eberbachium, M. Andream, usque adeo persequantur. Eâ enim ratione palàm fit, doctrinam vestram esse Evangelium, atque adeo ipsum Christum, quanquam hæc tantùm præludia sint futura vestræ persequutionis. Vos viros esse decet, tantoq; libentius, quantò promptius innocentissimum illum Christus, cujus Evangelium vos prædicatis, amarissimam mortem, pro omnibus nobis pertulit. Fecit itaq; Dominus, ut filii sui dogmata prædicatorum sanguine stabiliantur. Quid enim aliud vobis exspectandum est, doctrinam Christi profitentibus, nisi crux Christi? Hæc hæc vera est benedictio, quâ benedicit Dominus suis, hanc Martinus sitit,
units.tr: It is most welcome to me that the Papist priests persecute you, Eberbach, and Master Andreas, to such an extent. For by this means it becomes plain that your doctrine is the Gospel, and so Christ himself, although these are only the preludes of your persecution to come. You ought to be men, and so much the more willingly, as the most innocent Christ, whose Gospel you preach, bore the most bitter death for all of us, so much the more readily. Thus the Lord has done, so that the doctrines of his Son are established by the blood of their preachers. For what else is to be expected by you who profess the doctrine of Christ, but the cross of Christ? This, this is the true blessing with which the Lord blesses his own; Martin thirsts for this, nor is there any doubt that he will think so.

units.la: ncc nec dubium, quin sensurus sit. Quod superest, vos admoneo, ut magno & infracto animo in vinea Domini laboretis. Deijcite verbi gladio opera illa Papistica, Missas, indulgentias, caterasque cauponationes Monachorum, sacerdotum Baal. Praedicate fidei justitiam, quae non ex nobis, sed ex Deo est. Erigite magna fiducia signum illud Iona, quo solo omnes justificamur, quoque omnia alia Pharisaorum signa pessundantur. Neque haec tam liberè admonco, quod verear, ne praedicetis Evangelium, sed ut alacrius subinde liberius praedicetis, nec more Erasmico tergiversemini, ac per cuniculos vos volvatis, ut ne intelligentes quidem intelligant. Veritas enim fuco non indiget.
units.tr: Nor is there any doubt that he will think so. As for the rest, I advise you to labour in the vineyard of the Lord with a great and unbroken spirit. Cast down with the sword of the word those Papistical works, the Masses, indulgences, and the other huckstering of the monks, the priests of Baal. Preach the righteousness of faith, which is not of us but of God. Raise up with great confidence that sign of Jonah, by which alone we are all justified, and by which all the other signs of the Pharisees are overthrown. I do not give this advice so freely because I fear you may not preach the Gospel, but so that you may preach it more eagerly and from time to time more freely, and not, in the manner of Erasmus, shift your ground and roll yourselves through burrows, so that even those who understand do not understand. For truth does not need disguise.

units.la: PAULUM SPERATUM, nobilem Suevum, qui Augustae, Herbipoli, Saltzburgae & Viennae constanter & intrepidè Pontificios abusus taxârat, ex Iglavia urbe ad dicendam causam evocatum, Episcopus Olomucensis in tetrum carcerem condit, ex quo divinitus elapsus, V Vittebergam venit, aetatis 40.
units.tr: Paul Speratus, a noble Swabian, who had boldly and fearlessly censured the Papist abuses at Augsburg, Heidenheim, Salzburg and Vienna, was summoned from the town of Iglau to plead his cause. The Bishop of Olomouc threw him into a foul prison, from which, by God's providence, he escaped, and he came to Wittenberg, aged forty.

units.la: Nobiles virgines Misnicae, numero tres, Hanna à Draswitz, Milia ab Olsnitz, & Ursula à Feylitzin ex aula Friburgensi Ducis Saxoniae Henrici ob lectionem librorum Lutheri eijciuntur. Has Lutherus, monitu Nicolai Ambsdorffii, epistolâ solatur.
units.tr: Three noble maidens of Meissen, Hanna von Draswitz, Milia von Olsnitz, and Ursula von Feilitzsch, were expelled from the court at Freiberg of Duke Henry of Saxony because they read the books of Luther. Luther, at the urging of Nicholas von Amsdorf, comforted them with a letter.

units.la: HENRICUS Sutphaniensis, Bremensium Evangelista, ut tanquam Caesaris captivus (Antuerpiâ enim, vim metuens Papicolarum, profugerat) sibi dedatur, Margareta Austriaca à Bremensibus postulat.
units.tr: Henry of Sutphen, the evangelist of the Bremen people, fled from Antwerp for fear of the violence of the Papist partisans. The people of Bremen demanded from Margaret of Austria that he be handed over to them as if he were a prisoner of the Emperor.

units.la: FRANCISCUS LAMBERTUS Monachus familiæ Franciscanæ, qui superiore anno Avinione Tigurũ profectus, cum Zwinglio de invocatione sanctorum contulerat: & vi veritatis victus, cucullum exuerat, VVittembergæ hoc anno exulat, & liberalitate Principis Electoris tantisper sustentatur, dum ductâ ibidem uxore, Argentinam se recepit.
units.tr: Francis Lambert, a monk of the Franciscan order, who the previous year had gone from Avignon to Zurich and there debated with Zwingli about the invocation of saints, and who, overcome by the force of the truth, had cast off his cowl, spent this year in exile at Wittenberg, where he was supported for a time by the generosity of the Elector Prince, until he married there and withdrew to Strasbourg.

units.la: ACCUSATIONES & divexationes audivimus hactenus. Nunc virgas & mortes fidelium intuebimur.
units.tr: So far we have heard of accusations and harassments. Now let us look upon the rods and the deaths of the faithful.

units.la: JOANES Clericus Meldensis, quod schedulam Meldis affixerat valvis summi templi eius urbis contra indulgentias, à Papamisfas, in qua scripserat, eum esse Antichristum, virgis cæditur, & impresså in fronte notâ ignominiosè afficitur. Mater hæc videns, animũ ei addit, exclamatq;: vivat Christus, eiusq; insignia. HENRICUS Voes, & JOANNES Etch, Monachi Augustiniani Antuerpienses, sub inquisitore Jacobo Hogostrato Dominicano, ob Evangelii doctrinam Kal. Julii Bruxellis exusti, primam martyrii gloriam in Germania meruêre. Historiam vir quidam doctus, qui incendii spectator fuit, eleganti complexus est epistolâ, quam, quasi de novo primis Germaniæ Martyribus post annorũ nonaginta quatuordecursum, parentaturi, lectori pio meditandam subijcimus: Sic igitur autor: Exhibitū fuit nobis hijsce diebus spectaculum, miserabile dicerem, si ij quorū misereb it spectatores, miseri sibi, & non beatissimi visi fuissent. Si vacat, & lubitum est audire, accipe paucis rei summam. Ex cœtu illo Augustinensium, qui ex civitate Antuerpia Vilsordiam captivi perduƈti fuerunt, tres numero in hæresi sua perstiterunt, cæteris palinodiam canentibus. Nihil non tentatum est, ut ij eandem, quam fratres ceciner ant, canerent cantionem. Vbi viderunt se, quibus id negotii datum erat, cum omnia agerent nihil agere, decreverunt nimiūm pertinaces extremo tradere supplicio. Transportantur Bruxellam, asservantur in carcere diligenter. Conveniunt eodem M. N. Lovanienses. Fama quia nulla fere diem supplicij præcesserat, paucos alios aliunde huc pertraxit. Pridie Visitationis Deipara Virginis concurritur in forum. Conveniunt ordines Mendicantium tres, neq; enim plures, ut nosti, hic sunt, præeunte vexillo crucis, veluti solent, cum solenni pompa incedunt. Considentibus ordine jam sacræ Theologiæ Professoribus, Abbatibus, mitris & gemmatis pedis conspicuis, qui loco Episcoporum aderant, & aliis nōnullis in pulpito. Nam pulpitum erectum erat peramplum ante Basilicam, quam vulgo Senatoriam domum vocant. Sub horam undecimam ducitur per forum è tribus natu minimus, qui, ut annus ab aliis superabatur, ita doctrinā & facundiā præstabat. Duƈtus intrò, inibiq; paululū moratus, prodiit in pulpitum, induti sacerdotali panoplia. In medio collocata erat mensa, instar altaris ornata & instrata, ante hanc flexis genibus procumbit: ibi omnes, veluti stupentes, oculos defixère in eum. Nullam trepidationis, aut perturbati animi significationem cernere licuit. Atergo consistens concionem incipit Minoritarum Gardianus, ex adverso ceremonias, aperto codice, auspicatur Episcopus. Horam totam, dum hic ceremonias peragit, ille concionatur, eodem corporis habitu, vultuq; eodem juvenis durabat. Ego cum concionatorem praeturba intelligere nequirē, quod & aliis accidebat, totus intendebam in reum. Quod verum esse constat, quorsum dissimulemus? Vultus compositus & placidus, non modò mortis contemptum, verum etiam summam modestiam ac mansuetudinem prae se ferebat. Precationibus & sacris contemplationibus intento assimilis videbatur. Postea jussus nunc hoc, nunc illud facere, mirū quàm promptè, quam non gravatè paruerit. Ferunt dixisse obiter, se fore obedientē usq; ad mortem. Iis peractis ceremoniis, ubi ex sacerdos factus fuisset, quem vulgus laicum, aut secularem vocat, mutato vestitu intrò abit. Post prodeunt duo reliqui, facie horridiores, nimirum barbati: cum juvenis ille, quem memoravi, mento non esset hirsuto, sed formâ mirum in modum decenti & satis venustâ: sed prodeunt vultu eandem constantiam & alacritatem attestante. Quid multis? Et his adimitur sacerdotium, ac Monachatus sacramentum: ex sacris prophani effecti, relinquunt pulpitum. Post paulum educuntur duo, primus ille, & alter ex posterioribus. Itur ad ignem, qui in eodem, ubi haec acta sunt, foro, parabatur.
units.tr: John Clerc of Meaux, because he had posted at Meaux, on the doors of the chief church of that town, a placard against indulgences, in which he had written that the Pope was Antichrist, was beaten with rods and disgracefully branded on the forehead. His mother, seeing this, encouraged him and cried out: Long live Christ and his badges. Henry Voes and John Esch, Augustinian monks of Antwerp, were burnt at Brussels on 1 July, under the inquisitor Jacob Hochstraten, a Dominican, for the doctrine of the Gospel, and earned the first glory of martyrdom in Germany. A learned man who witnessed the burning has set out the story in an elegant letter, which, as if it were newly written for the first German martyrs after the lapse of ninety-four years, we submit to the pious reader for meditation. Thus the author: A spectacle was presented to us these last days, which I would call miserable, if those whom we pitied had not seemed miserable to themselves and not most blessed. If you have leisure and wish to hear it, take the sum of the matter in brief. Out of that group of Augustinians who were brought as captives from the city of Antwerp to Vilvoorde, three remained steadfast in their heresy, while the others sang the palinode. Everything was tried to make them sing the same song the brothers had sung. When those charged with the business saw that, while they did everything, they accomplished nothing, they decided to hand over the most obstinate to the extreme punishment. They were carried to Brussels and kept carefully in prison. The Louvain masters gathered there too. Since there had been almost no rumour before the day of execution, it drew a few others from elsewhere. On the day before the Feast of the Visitation of the Virgin Mary, people ran to the marketplace. The three orders of mendicants came together, for there are no more of them here, as you know, and they advanced with a solemn procession, as they usually do, with the banner of the cross going before. The professors of sacred theology were seated in order, abbots with mitres and jewelled crosiers were conspicuous, who stood in place of the bishops, and some others on the pulpit. For a large pulpit had been erected in front of the church, which the people call the Senate House. At about eleven o'clock the youngest of the three was led through the marketplace; as he was surpassed in years by the others, so he excelled them in learning and eloquence. Led inside, and after lingering there a little, he came out onto the pulpit, clothed in priestly vestments. In the middle a table had been set, adorned and spread like an altar, and before this he knelt down with bent knees; there all of them, as if stunned, fixed their eyes on him. No sign of trembling or of a disturbed mind could be seen. Then, standing behind him, the Guardian of the Minorites began a sermon, while opposite him the bishop began the ceremonies with an open book. For a whole hour, while the one carried out the ceremonies and the other preached, the young man remained in the same posture of body and the same expression of face. I, since I could not understand the preacher on account of the crowd (which was also the case for others), was entirely intent on the accused. And it is certain, why should we pretend otherwise? His face was composed and calm, and showed not only contempt of death but also the greatest modesty and gentleness. He seemed like one intent on prayers and holy contemplation. Afterwards, when he was bidden now to do this, now that, it was wonderful how promptly and how readily he obeyed. They say he remarked in passing that he would be obedient even unto death. When the ceremonies were done, and he had been made from a priest into what the common people call a layman or secular, he went back inside in changed clothing. Afterwards the two others came out, with rougher faces, namely bearded men; for the young man I have mentioned had no bristling beard but a face of remarkably pleasing and rather comely form. Yet they came out with faces attesting the same constancy and cheerfulness. What more? Both were stripped of the priesthood and of the sacrament of the monastic life; made profane from holy, they left the pulpit. After a little while two were led out, the first one and another of the latter ones. They went to the fire, which was being prepared in the same marketplace where these things were done.

units.la: Interea dum ducuntur, dum exuunt sese vestibus, multa audiebantur ex illis, quae argumenta clarissima omnibus fuissent sanarum & piarum mentium, & veluti gestientium cum Christo conjungi soluto corpore, nisi persuasum fuisset, haereseos esse convictos. Subinde testificati sunt, se mori Christianos, se credere in sanctam Catholicam Ecclesiam. Aiebant, hunc esse diem, quem diu exspectassent. Iam vestibus nudati, relicto tantum induso, steterunt diu, magis ipsi palos amplectentes, quam alligati. Ignis lentius succedebatur, id consilio factum sit an casu, equidem affirmare non ausim. Quid? inquis, non languescebant tam diuturna mora vexati? non demittebant animos jam fumo subvolante, mox flamma subsequuturā?
units.tr: Meanwhile, while they were being led and while they were taking off their garments, many things were heard from them which would have been the clearest proofs to all of sound and pious minds, and of men who longed to be joined to Christ once the body was loosed, had it not been persuaded that they were convicted of heresy. Repeatedly they declared that they were dying as Christians, that they believed in the holy Catholic Church. They said that this was the day they had long been waiting for. Now stripped of their clothes, leaving only their undergarments, they stood for a long time, embracing the stakes themselves more than being bound to them. The fire was kindled rather slowly; whether this was done by design or by chance I would not dare to affirm. What? you say, were they not weakened by so long a delay? Did they not lose heart, as the smoke rose and the flame was soon to follow?

units.la: Quod si ex gestibus, fronte, oculis, denique ex toto vultu judicare convenit, quae omnia veluti loquuntur, & non raro certius & meliori fide animum aperiunt quam lingua: fiducia, constantia atque alacritas, quae summa fuerant semper, incrementum sumere videbantur: tum potissimum emicabat, nescio quae hilaritas, adeo ut multis ridere viderentur. Praeter alia recitabant symbolum fidei, & canticum Ecclesiasticum: Te Deum laudamus, idque alternis dicebant. Alter dum ignem succendi sub pedibus aspiceret, ajebat, videri sibi rosas substernī. Tandem exorta flamma vocem utrinque intercepit. Ego semper ab eiusmodi spectaculis natura abhorrui, & lubenter abstinui, neque hic spectator esse potuissem, nisi ipsi, de quorum capite agebatur, mihi, qui otiosus in tuto spectabam scrupulum omnem suâ magnanimitate & vultus hilaritate eiecissent. Tertius productus non fuit, id quare factum sit, compertum non habeo. Quidam hunc resipuisse narrant, verum quando ad populum reductus non fuit, publicè recantaturus, omnibus id persuaderi non potest. Quidam suspicantur, clam necatum. Vtut se res habet, diu latere non potuit. Postridie cum dies esset sacer Diuæ Virgini, Minorita hic in concione populum admonuit: ut, si forte rogaretur ex ipsis, quis fuisset exitus eorum, quos concremari vidissent, dicerent, obïsse in fide erronea Lutheri: accepisse ex quibusdam, dictitâs, se, in extremo momento defecisse eos ab erroribus, quod quidem precibus quorundam, & D. Virginis beneficio, qua miraculum edidisset, factum ajebat. Idem fere asseverabat Lovanij, nam redierat eò Nicolaus Egmondanus, narrans à prandio in concione, se horâ undecima literas accepisse à probo & optimo viro. Francisco ab Hulst, cui provincia à Casare demandata est investigandi & persequendi haereticos, quibus significari ajebat, Augustinianos illos, haereseos damnatos & exustos, redijsse cum jam flamma submoveretur, rejectis erroribus, ad saniorem mentem. Quod quia constanter hoc negant, quotquot proxime ignem astiterunt, tacuisse fortassis praestiterat, nisi si quis id ex abundantia charitatis, qua omnia sperat, factum existimet. Bene valc. Bruxellae sexto Idus Iulij.
units.tr: If one may judge from gestures, brow, eyes, and indeed the whole face, which all speak as it were, and often reveal the mind more truly and more faithfully than the tongue, their confidence, steadfastness and cheerfulness, which had always been great, seemed to grow. Above all a certain cheerfulness shone out, so that many seemed to be laughing. Among other things they recited the creed and the church canticle Te Deum laudamus, and they said it in alternation. One of them, while he watched the fire being kindled beneath his feet, said that he seemed to himself to be walking on roses. At last, when the flames rose, their voices were cut off on every side. I have always shrunk by nature from such spectacles and have gladly kept away from them. I could not have been a spectator here, had they not, whose lives were at stake, removed from me, a idle onlooker standing in safety, every scruple by their own greatness of soul and cheerful faces. A third was not brought out, and I have not learned why this happened. Some report that he recanted, but since he was not brought back to the people to retract publicly, it cannot be made credible to everyone. Some suspect that he was secretly put to death. However the matter stands, it could not stay hidden for long. On the following day, which was a feast of the Blessed Virgin, a Minorite in his sermon warned the people that, if they should be asked what the end was of those whom they had seen burned, they should say that they had died in Luther's erroneous faith. He said that he had heard from some people, as he put it, that at the last moment they had renounced their errors, and that this had happened by the prayers of certain people and by the kindness of the Blessed Virgin, who had worked a miracle. Almost the same was asserted at Louvain, for Nicolaus Egmondanus had returned there, and he told in his sermon after dinner that at the eleventh hour he had received a letter from an upright and excellent man, Francis ab Hulst, to whom the Emperor had assigned the task of seeking out and prosecuting heretics. He said that the letter signified that those Augustinians, condemned and burned for heresy, had returned to a saner mind, rejecting their errors, just when the flame was being moved away. Since all who stood nearest the fire deny this constantly, it would perhaps have been better to be silent, unless someone thinks it was done out of an abundance of charity, which hopes all things. Farewell. Brussels, 8 July.

units.la: LUTHERUS hos Monachos ob confessionis constantiam, cantico, quod in multorū est ore, celebravit, & ut suì temporis primos martyres canonizavit. Et sanè mors istorum fuit vita Ecclesiæ. Bruxella, inquit Erasmus, duo Augustinenses publicitus affecti sunt supplicio. Quaeris exitum? Ea civitas, anteapurissima, cœpit habere Lutheri discipulos, & quidem rō paucos. Savitum & in Hollandia. Quid multis? Ybicunq; fumos excitavit nuntius (Alcandrum intelligit, quem & διπλωματοφόρον nominat, vi bullæ Lutheri libros incendentem.) ubicunque saevitiam exercuit Carmelita, ibi diceres factam haeresèon sementem. Et alibi. Bruxella primùm exusti sunt duo. Tum demùm cœpit civitas favere Luthero.
units.tr: LUTHER celebrated these monks, for the steadfastness of their confession, in a hymn that is on many people's lips, and he counted them as the first martyrs of his time. And indeed the death of these men was the life of the Church. "At Brussels," says Erasmus, "two Augustinians were publicly put to punishment. Do you ask the outcome? That most pure city began to have Luther's disciples, and indeed not a few. The cruelty extended also into Holland. Why say more? Wherever the news of the smoke spread (he means Aleander, whom he also calls the diplomat [διπλωματοφόρον], who burned Luther's books by virtue of the bull), wherever the Carmelite exercised his cruelty, there you would say that a seed of heresy had been sown." And elsewhere: "At Brussels, first two were burned. Only then did the city begin to favour Luther."

units.la: Obiit hoc anno Adrianus Romanus Pontifex, nō sine veneni suspicione, decimâ tertiâ Septembris, & obiit (quemadmodum Guicciardinus loquitur) parvâ sui sive ob temporis, quo regnavit, brevitatem, sive quod rerum esset imperitus, opinione relictâ, & cum totius Curia incredibili voluptate.
units.tr: This year Adrian, the Roman Pontiff, died, not without suspicion of poison, on 13 September. He died (as Guicciardini puts it) with his reputation left either because of the brevity of the time in which he reigned, or because he was inexperienced in affairs, and to the incredible delight of the whole Curia.

units.la: Hic Pontifex dubiū posteris reliquit, simulatène an seriò Romanæ Ecclesiæ reformationè meditatus sit. Qui in benigniorem sententiâ inclinant, ut Vergerius, Pontanus Isacius, & alii, non credunt, hominem Hollandum à Batava simplicitate ita repente deflexisse: credunt autem eius legato in conventu Norico ingenuè Romanæ Curiæ peccata confitenti, emendationem pollicenti, gravaminum,quibus Principes se à Pontificibus Romanis gravari putent, catalogum poscenti.Moventur & eo, quod Papæ Adriani successores tum omnem illam Adriani legationem,tum centum illa gravamina inter hęretica scripta rejecerunt, grave supplicium comminantes omnibus, qui illa legerint, aut domi habuerint. Nec dissimulant, hanc rem fatum accelerasse Adriano, quippe qui suspectâ morte vix secundum Pontificatûs annum ingressus, obierit, & cuius tumulo Romæ in æde quam Teutonum vocant, hæc verba inscripta legantur : O in quæ tempora optimi cuiusque virtus incidit! Qui contrà sentiunt, Sleidanus, Balæus, Lydius, &c. Pontificum hanc ajunt esse techna m, quando Conciliū & notionem causæ tardare volunt, ut liberaliter & prolixè polliceatur, quò spatium intercedat comparandi Regum gratias,& aliatentandi.Nec abludit ab his Erasmus.Huic, ait in epistolâ quadam,(Adriano puta) per certum hominem significavi, me libenter communicaturum quod videretur, modò liceret impunè. Exegit, ut id facerem brevi.Non offensus est, sed tamen non respondit. Vndè facilè divinavi, non idem illi placere, quod mihi videbatur expedire. Mens Adriani quæ fuerit, Deus novit.
units.tr: This Pontiff has left it uncertain to posterity whether he seriously meditated the reformation of the Roman Church or did so only in pretence. Those who lean to the more favourable opinion, such as Vergerius, Pontanus, Isacius and others, do not believe that a Dutchman had so suddenly turned aside from Batavian simplicity; they believe, however, that when his legate at the Diet of Nuremberg frankly confessed the sins of the Roman Curia, promised amendment, and asked for a list of the grievances by which the princes thought they were burdened by the Roman Pontiffs, he was moved to this. They are moved also by the fact that Adrian's successors rejected both that whole legation of Adrian and those hundred grievances, placing them among heretical writings, threatening grave punishment to all who should read them or keep them at home. Nor do they conceal that this affair hastened Adrian's fate, since he, dying by suspicious death, scarcely entered the second year of his pontificate; and on his tomb at Rome, in the church which they call the German church, these words are read as inscribed: "O what times the virtue of every good man has fallen upon!" Those who think otherwise, Sleidan, Balaeus, Lydius, etc., say that this is a trick of the Pontiffs, when they wish to delay a council and the examination of the cause, so that they may promise generously and at length, in order that time may intervene to secure the favour of kings and to try other means. Erasmus does not dissent from these. "To this man," he says in a certain letter (meaning Adrian), "I signified through a certain person that I would gladly share whatever seemed fitting, provided it might be done without danger. He required that I do it quickly. He was not offended, but nevertheless he did not reply. Hence I easily divined that what seemed to me expedient did not please him." What Adrian's mind was, God knows.

units.la: Franciscus à Sickingen Eques Germanus, Lutheranæ hæreseos capitaneus à nonnullis dictus, infelici bello implicitus, quod gesserat anno superiori contra Archiepiscopum Trevirensem, obsidetur à Palatino, Trevirensi, & Hasso in arce Landstall, decussoque ex bombardarum ictu tramite, lædMitur, & septimâ Maii, ætatis anno 42. moritur, salutatus paulò ante quàm animam ageret, à tribus Principibus, hostibus suis. Mira hinc Pontificiorum tripudia, mirææ ovationes subortæ. Videbatur enim Franciscus Brutus quidam esse, qui Germaniam ab Episcoporum tyrannide esset vindicaturus. Sed desertus fuit ab iis, qui se polliciti erant adversus quosvis illi opem laturos esse: nec audiit Lutherum, genus hoc bellorum plane improbantem.
units.tr: Franz von Sickingen, a German knight, called by some the captain of the Lutheran heresy, was involved in an unhappy war which he had waged the year before against the Archbishop of Trier. Besieged in the fortress of Landstuhl by the Palatine, the Trier forces and Hesse, he was wounded when a path was broken by the blow of the cannon, and he died on 7 May in his forty-second year, having been greeted shortly before his death, as he drew his last breath, by three princes, his enemies. Hence came the wonderful exultation of the Papists and the marvellous celebrations that arose. For Franz seemed to be a certain Brutus who would deliver Germany from the tyranny of the bishops. But he was deserted by those who had promised to bring help to him against any enemies; nor did he listen to Luther, who entirely disapproved of this kind of war.

units.la: Ulricus quoque Huttenus, acerrimus Lutheri patronus, Nobilis Francus, mense Augusto in insula lacûs Tigurini, Helvetiis Ufnort dictâ, quæ Eremi Abbatem Dominum agnoscit, apud Joannem Schneckum, felicem σωτῆρος curatorem, moritur ætatis 36.
units.tr: Ulrich von Hutten also, the most zealous patron of Luther, a noble of Franconia, died in August, aged 36, on the island in Lake Zurich called Ufnau by the Swiss, which acknowledges the abbot of Einsiedeln as lord, at the house of Johann Schnecke, his fortunate guardian [σωτῆρος].

units.la: Ulricus Huttenus: Ulrich von Hutten, Nobilis Francus.
units.tr: Ulrich von Hutten, a Franconian nobleman.

units.la: ANNVS CHRISTI MDXXIV.
units.tr: The Year of Christ 1524.

units.la: AD subvertendam Evangelii doctrinam omnes hoc anno machinas adhibebant politici æquè ac Ecclesiastici.
units.tr: To overthrow the doctrine of the Gospel, in this year politicians and churchmen alike employed every kind of machination.

units.la: E Politicis, Cæsar, Imperii Principes in conventu Norico, Ferdinandus, solus, & cum confœderatis, Henricus VIII. Rex Angliæ, Ludovicus Rex Ungariæ & Boëmiæ: Duces, Bavarus & Lotharingus: Metenses, Diethmarsi, Antuerpiani, Duodecim deniq; Pagi Helvetiorum, in opprimendo Evangelio toti fuerunt.
units.tr: Among the politicians, the Emperor, the princes of the Empire at the Nuremberg assembly, Ferdinand alone and with his allies, Henry VIII, King of England, Louis, King of Hungary and Bohemia, the dukes of Bavaria and Lorraine, the people of Metz, of Dithmarschen and of Antwerp, and finally the twelve cantons of the Swiss, were all wholly devoted to suppressing the Gospel.

units.la: CÆSAR per Joannem Haunartum Principibus mandat: ut edictum VVormatiense de exterminandis Lutheranis magno studio servent.
units.tr: The Emperor, through Johann Haunart, orders the princes to observe with great zeal the Edict of Worms concerning the extermination of the Lutherans.

units.la: PRINCIPES Imperii Noribergæ congregati, se, quantum eius præstare possint, facturos pollicentur. Quod ubi Lutherus rescivit, dentato scripto de Germaniæ cæcitate conquestus est, oblatam sibi salutem repudiantis.
units.tr: The princes of the Empire, gathered at Nuremberg, promise that they will do as much as they can to carry this out. When Luther learned of this, he complained in a biting writing about the blindness of Germany, which rejected the salvation offered to it.

units.la: FERDINANDI Austrii permissu Viennæ Caspar Tauberus civis Viennensis, constans Christi confessor, capite truncatur, mense Septembri.
units.tr: With the permission of Ferdinand of Austria, Caspar Tauber, a citizen of Vienna and a steadfast confessor of Christ, is beheaded at Vienna in September.

units.la: Idem Ferdinandus M. Jacobum Otterum ex oppido Kenzingen, quod supra Argentinam trans Rhenum aliquot milliaribus situm, mense Julio pellit: expulsum concionatorem centum & quinquaginta auditorum ad proximum pagum comitatur honoris atq; pietatis causâ, ibiq; per aliquot dies morātur: postea ad uxores liberosq; rediturī, ingressu oppidi prohibentur. Navibus igitur Argentinam descendunt. Interim Friburgo, & Ensishemio advolans manus armata, oppidum occupat, Evangelii reos in vincula quæstionesq; coniicit. Ferunt, inquit Gerbelius, heri. sterno die Archigrammatéum, illic strenuum virū, capitis supplicio punitum: quod contra decretum Ecclesiæ, Bullam Pontificis, & Cæsaris Mandatum, proximis mensibus utramq; partem ἰυχαεῖσίας sumpserit. Quindecim adhuc superesse dicūt, eodē supplicio puniēdos, Argētinæ feriâ 4. post Ulrici.
units.tr: The same Ferdinand, in July, drives Master Jacob Otter out of the town of Kenzingen, which lies a few miles across the Rhine from Strasbourg. The expelled preacher was accompanied by a hundred and fifty of his hearers as far as the next village, out of honour and piety, and there stayed for some days. Afterwards, when they wished to return to their wives and children, they were forbidden entry to the town. They therefore went down to Strasbourg by boat. Meanwhile an armed band flew to Freiburg and to Ensisheim, seized the town, and cast the adherents of the Gospel into chains and into prison for questioning. They report, says Gerbelius, that yesterday (or the day before) a certain brave man, a Greek scholar, was punished by beheading there, because, contrary to the decree of the Church, the Papal bull, and the Emperor's mandate, in recent months he had received both kinds of the Eucharist [εὐχαριστίας]. They say fifteen others are still to be punished with the same penalty. At Strasbourg, Wednesday after the feast of Ulrich.

units.la: Idem FERDINANDUS, Cæsaris frater, Campegius, Salisburgensis, Bavari fratres, Tridentinus, Ratisbonensis Episcopus, itemque Episcoporum, Bambergici, Spirensis, Argentinensis, Augustani, Constantiensis, Basiliensis, Frisingensis, Passaviensis, Brixinensis, legati, à conventu Noribergico Ratisbonæ conveniunt, decernuntque:
units.tr: The same Ferdinand, the Emperor's brother, together with Campeggio, the Bishop of Salzburg, the brothers of Bavaria, the Bishop of Trent, the Bishop of Regensburg, and likewise the legates of the bishops of Bamberg, Speyer, Strasbourg, Augsburg, Constance, Basel, Freising, Passau and Brixen, meet at Regensburg after the Nuremberg assembly, and decree:

units.la: 1. Ex Cæsaris & Leonis X. iudicio, secundum Wormaticensé edictum, Lutheri doctrinā, ut hæreticam, damnandam.
units.tr: 1. By the judgment of the Emperor and of Leo X, according to the Edict of Worms, the doctrine of Luther is to be condemned as heretical.

units.la: 2. Edictum illud per fines suos servandum.
units.tr: 2. That edict is to be observed throughout their territories.

units.la: 3. In Missa nihil mutandum.
units.tr: 3. Nothing is to be changed in the Mass.

units.la: 4. Traditionum Pontificiarum violatores multandos.
units.tr: 4. Violators of the Papal traditions are to be fined.

units.la: 5. Lutheri libros non vendendos.
units.tr: 5. Luther's books are not to be sold.

units.la: 6. Qui VVitteberga discant, domum revocandos.
units.tr: 6. Those who are studying at Wittenberg are to be called home.

units.la: Qui mirantur, inter Germaniæ Principes, solos ferè Bavaros Pontificiæ doctrinæ tam constanter adhæsisse, causam in hunc conventum reiiciant, astutiâ Campegii institutum; ut, quod in generali Principum conventu non potuit, in particulari perficeret.
units.tr: Those who wonder why, among the princes of Germany, almost only the Bavarians have so steadfastly clung to the Papal doctrine, should lay the blame on this assembly, which was arranged by the cunning of Campeggio, so that what he could not achieve in the general assembly of the princes he might accomplish in a smaller one.

units.la: HENRICUS Anglorum Rex Erasmo Roterodamo persuadet, ut stylum stringat adversus Lutherum. Prodit igitur mense Octobri Diatribe de Libero Arbitrio. Invitus in hanc arenam descendit Erasmus. Testatur ipse ad Emserum. Quid mea Diatribâ civilius? Quid profecit tamen, nisi quod Lutheranos excitavit ad maiorem insaniam? Id non ignarus futurum, tamen morem gessi Regi & Cardinali Angliæ (VVolsæo) Pontifici (Clementi) & doctis aliquot amicis: non tacens interim, quid esset sequuturum. Et ad Melanchthonem clarius: Miraberis, inquit, cur emiserim libellum de libero arbitrio. Sustinebam triplex agmen inimicorum. Theologi & bonarum literarum ofores nullum non movebant lapidem, ut perderent Erasmum,
units.tr: Henry, King of the English, persuades Erasmus of Rotterdam to take up his pen against Luther. Accordingly, in October, Erasmus publishes his Diatribe on Free Will. He enters this arena unwillingly. He testifies himself to Emser: What could be more civil than my Diatribe? Yet what has it achieved, except to rouse the Lutherans to greater madness? I was not unaware that this would happen, but I complied with the King and Cardinal of England (Wolsey), the Pope (Clement), and some learned friends, not keeping silent meanwhile about what would follow. And more clearly to Melanchthon: You will be surprised, he says, why I put out the little book on free will. I was bearing up against a threefold army of enemies. The theologians and the enemies of good letters moved every stone to destroy Erasmus,

units.la: Epistolarū libro xviii.
units.tr: Letters, book 18.

units.la: Epistolarū lib. xix. smum, cum, quòd attacti essent libris meis, tum quòd collegium illud florentissimum invexerim Lovanium, eamq; regionem totam infecerim linguis ac bonis literis, sic enim illi loquuntur. Hi Monarchis omnibus persuaserant, me iuratissimum esse Luthero. Itaq; amici, videntes me periclitari, spem prabuere Pontifici & Principibus, fore ut aliquid ederem in Lutherum. Eam spem & ipse pro tempore alui. Et interim isti, non expectato libello, caeperant me libellis lacessere. Nihil igitur restabat, nisi ut ederem, quod scripseram, alioqui & Monarchas habuissem infensos, quibus visus fuissem dedisse verba, & isti tumultuosi clamassent, me metu premere, & atrocius aliquid expectantes impotentius saevissent. Postremò quoniam epistola Lutheri iam est in manibus, quâ pollicetur, se cohibiturum calamum in me, si conquiescam, viderer ex pacto non edere.
units.tr: Letters, book 19. ...especially because they were attacked by my books, and also because I introduced that most flourishing college at Louvain and infected the whole region with languages and good letters, for so they put it. These men had persuaded all the monarchs that I was utterly sworn to Luther. So my friends, seeing me in danger, gave hope to the Pope and the princes that I would publish something against Luther. I myself nourished that hope for the time being. And meanwhile those men, without waiting for the little book, had begun to harass me with pamphlets. Nothing therefore remained but to publish what I had written; otherwise I would have had the monarchs hostile to me, to whom I would have seemed to have deceived them, and those troublemakers would have cried out that I was cowed by fear, and, expecting something more atrocious, would have raged more violently. Finally, since Luther's letter is already in hand, in which he promises that he will restrain his pen against me if I keep quiet, I would seem to be publishing in breach of an agreement.

units.la: Adhuc qui Romae profitentur literas Ethnicas, ipsi Ἐθνικώτεροι, mirè fremunt in me, invidentes, ut apparet, Germanis. Itaq; si nihil edidissem, prabuissem ansam & Theologis & Monachis, & illis Romanensibus sigulis, quorum Alpha, ni fallor, est N, ut facilius persuaderent Pontificibus ac Monarchis, quod persuadere conabantur. Postremò hos furiosos Evangelicos habuissem iniquiores. Nam ipse rem tractavi modestissimè: & tamen quod scribo, non scribo adversus animi sententiam, quanquam ab hac quoq; libenter discessurus, ubi persuadebitur, quod rectius est.
units.tr: Still, those who teach Ethnic letters at Rome, themselves more Pagan than the Pagans, rage wonderfully against me, envying, as it appears, the Germans. So if I had published nothing, I would have given an occasion both to the theologians and to the monks, and to those Roman individuals, whose Alpha, unless I am mistaken, is N, to persuade the Pontiffs and the monarchs more easily of what they were trying to persuade them. Finally, I would have made these furious Evangelicals more unfair to me. For I have handled the matter most modestly; and yet what I write, I do not write against my own opinion, although I would gladly depart from this too, when it is shown to me what is more right.

units.la: In hac Διατριβῇ sive collatione praemonet Erasmus: non expedire ad pietatem, materiâ hanc altius scrutari, & quaerere de praescientia Dei contingenti: An purè passivè se voluntas hominis in spiritualibus habeat, nec ne? An omnia merâ necessitate faciamus; Deinde tacitè confert veterum Patrum, qui liberum arbitrium agnoverunt, multitudinem, cum novorum Doctorum, qui servum arbitrium praedicat, paucitate, laudatâq; veterum pietate, eruditione, miraculis, novorum autoritatem non sine sarcasmis minuit. Tum postquam definivit liberum arbitrium, quod sit vis humana voluntatis, quâ se potest homo applicare ad ea, quae perducunt ad aeternam salutem, aut ab iisdem avertere, recenset loca sacrae scripturae, quae ipsi visa sunt liberum arbitrium statuere: diluit ea, quae ex adverso stare videntur: incommoda & absurda enumerat, quae consequantur, si semel funditus tollatur liberum arbitrium: placere sibi ait, sententiam illorum, qui nonnihil tribuunt libero arbitrio, gratiae plurimum: docet, hac sententiâ receptâ, nihil perire eorum, quae Lutherus piè quidem & Christianè disseruit, de summa charitate in Deum, de abiicienda fiducia meritorum, operum & virium nostrarum, de tota fiducia transferenda in Deum & illius promissa.
units.tr: In this Diatribe [Διατριβῇ], or discussion, Erasmus first warns that it is not expedient for piety to probe this matter too deeply, and to inquire about God's contingent foreknowledge: whether the human will is purely passive in spiritual matters or not; whether we do everything by sheer necessity. Then he quietly sets the multitude of the Fathers, who acknowledged free will, against the paucity of the new teachers who preach the enslaved will, and, praising the piety, learning and miracles of the old, he diminishes the authority of the new not without sarcasm. Then, after defining free will as the human power of the will by which a man can apply himself to those things which lead to eternal salvation, or turn away from them, he lists the passages of Holy Scripture which seemed to him to establish free will, and he dilutes those which seem to stand on the other side. He enumerates the inconveniences and absurdities which would follow if free will were once utterly abolished. He says that he is pleased with the opinion of those who attribute something to free will, and very much to grace. He teaches that, with this opinion accepted, nothing is lost of what Luther has argued, indeed piously and Christianly, concerning the supreme love of God, the renunciation of trust in our merits, works and powers, and the transfer of all trust to God and his promises.

units.la: Lutherus quid de libello hoc senserit, ex epistola ipsius ad Spalatinum videre est. Sic autem ibi: Incredibile est, quàm fastidiam libellum de libero arbitrio : nec dum ultra duos quaterniones eius legi. Molestum est tam erudito libro respondere, tam eruditi viri. Feriâ tertiâ omnium Sanctorum.
units.tr: What Luther thought of this little book can be seen from his letter to Spalatin. It reads thus: It is incredible how much I loathe the little book on free will; I have not yet read beyond two quires of it. It is irksome to answer a book so learned, by a man so learned. Tuesday after All Saints.

units.la: LUDOVICI Ungariæ & Boëmiæ Regis, juvenis bonitate abutebantur Pragenses in Boëmia, & Budenses in Ungaria. Pragenses decretis, carceribus & exiliis in Lutheranos, & Fratres, (quos Picardos vocant) hoc anno saeviebant. Et persuasus ab illis Rex Ludovicus Carolo Duci Münsterbergensi, Georgii Podiebracii nepoti, Boëmiæ gubernatori mandabat: ut omnes Lutheranos & Picardos in exilium proiiceret. Budenses in Ungaria Georgium quendam, Bibliopolam, unà cum libris Evangelicis exulserunt.
units.tr: The goodness of the young King Louis of Hungary and Bohemia was abused: the people of Prague in Bohemia, and of Buda in Hungary. This year the people of Prague raged against the Lutherans and the Brethren (whom they call Picards) with decrees, prisons and exiles. Persuaded by them, King Louis ordered Charles, Duke of Münsterberg, grandson of George of Poděbrady and governor of Bohemia, to cast all the Lutherans and Picards into exile. At Buda in Hungary they expelled a certain George, a bookseller, together with Evangelical books.

units.la: DUCIS BAVARIÆ tyrannidis meminit Lutherus epistolâ ad Lamberrũ Thorn. Et alibi: in Bavaria, inquit multùm regnat crux & persequutio verbi, etiā nō palàm seminati.
units.tr: Luther mentions the tyranny of the Duke of Bavaria in a letter to Lambert Thorn. And elsewhere: In Bavaria, he says, the cross and the persecution of the Word reign greatly, even where the Word is not openly sown.

units.la: DUX LOTHARINGIÆ Antonius facto decreto, quoniam doctrina Lutheri damnata sit à Pontifice Romano, & à Cæsare, & à celeberrimis Academiis, mandat suis, ne quis pro concione aliquid eius generis doceat. Item, qui libros habent ullos à Luthero scriptos, intra certũ diem exhibeant: meliùs audiri posset, ascendit, & Evangelium de quinq; panibus & duobus piscibus piè explicavit. Postero autem die sacco indutus propter metum populi, subitò in profluentem coniectus est.
units.tr: Antony, Duke of Lorraine, having made a decree, since the doctrine of Luther has been condemned by the Roman Pontiff, by the Emperor, and by the most famous universities, orders his people that no one is to teach anything of that kind from the pulpit. Likewise, whoever has any books written by Luther is to hand them over within a set day. A preacher, who was being heard more fittingly, mounted the pulpit and piously expounded the Gospel of the five loaves and two fishes. But on the next day, clothed in sackcloth because of the people's fear, he was suddenly thrown into a flowing river.

units.la: HELVETIORUM Pagi duodecim xxvi. Januarii in conventu suo Lucernensi decernunt: Pontificiam religionem retinendam: reliquias Sanctorum à nemine ridendas: qui contra fecerint, Magistratui esse deferendos.
units.tr: The twelve cantons of the Swiss, on 26 January, at their assembly at Lucerne, decree that the Papist religion is to be retained; that the relics of the Saints are not to be mocked by anyone; and that whoever acts contrary to this is to be reported to the magistrate.

units.la: Vigesimâ primâ Martii Tigurum veniunt eorundem Helvetiorum legati, articulos bene multos Tigurinis proponentes, rogantesque, ut missâ reformatione Ecclesiarum suarum, in maiorum decretis persistant. Qui iidem, si Tigurinis grave sit iugum Pontificum, Episcoporum, Abbatum &c. operam se daturos promittunt, ut gravamina ista tollantur. Quibus humaniter & benignè dimissis, Tigurini scriptum ad Helvetios mittunt, in quo protestantur, multa de quib. accusentur (ut de contumeliis Virginis Mariæ, & similia) in ipsorum ditione non fieri: quæ autem mutata sint in melius, ea reprehensionem non merereri, quia talis reformatio cum verbo Dei minimè pugnet: neq; se ab Episcopis, ad quorum iurisdictionem Ecclesiasticâ Helvetii pertineant, neq; ab Academia Basiliensi, ullius erroris esse convictos. Respondét etiam speciatim ad singula accusationis capita: Et se per conscientiam suam non posse aliter agere, nisi error demonstretur: idq; ut fiat ab ipsis, ab Episcopis & ab Academia Basilien si, ante finem mensis Maii, vehementer orare: cum enim terminum sese expectaturos.
units.tr: On 21 March the envoys of the same Helvetii come to Zurich, putting forward quite a number of articles to the Zurich people and asking that, the reformation of their churches being set aside, they persist in the decrees of their ancestors. These same men promise that, if the yoke of the Pontiffs, bishops, abbots, etc. is burdensome to the Zurich people, they will take care to have these grievances removed. The Zurich people dismissed them kindly and courteously, and sent a written reply to the Helvetii in which they protest that many of the things they are accused of (such as insults to the Virgin Mary and the like) do not happen in their territory; that the things that have been changed for the better do not deserve reproof, since such a reformation does not conflict at all with the Word of God; and that they have not been convicted of any error either by the bishops, to whose ecclesiastical jurisdiction the Helvetii belong, or by the Academy of Basel. They also answer each head of the accusation separately, and state that in conscience they cannot act otherwise unless an error is demonstrated; they earnestly beg that this be done by them, by the bishops and by the Academy of Basel before the end of May, for they will wait for that deadline.

units.la: HÆc Politicorum in Evangelicos hoc anno fuit sævitia. Non minore in eosdem adhibuerunt Ecclesiastici, Papa, Cardinalis Lotharingus: Archiepiscopi, Moguntinus, & Rigensis: Episcopi Danici, Spirensis & Argentinensis, Provincialis item Augustinianorum, Conradus Trögerus.
units.tr: This was the cruelty of the civil authorities against the Evangelicals this year. No less was shown against the same people by the churchmen: the Pope, Cardinal of Lorraine; the Archbishops of Mainz and Riga; the bishops of Denmark, Speyer and Strasbourg; likewise the provincial of the Augustinians, Konrad Tröger.

units.la: PAPA Clemens VII. ad Comitia Noribergensia, hoc anno continuata, Cardinalem Campegium mittit: qui absentem Fridericū Saxoniæ Electorem Papæ & suis literis, amanter admodū scriptis, hortatur: ut populi licentiam & sacrarū legum atq; ceremoniarū mutationem graviter & masculè ulciscatur. Deinde Principes ipsos in Comitiis rogat, ne ullam in Religione innovationem fieri patiantur, dissimulans, sibi de responso Principum superiori anno legato Adriani Pontificis dato, quicquam constare, nisi quod privatim ad se scriptum, sub titulo Principum delatum sit, quod ille existimet, odio privato à quibusdam adversus Romanam Rempublicam confectum.
units.tr: Pope Clement VII sends Cardinal Campeggio to the Diet of Nuremberg, which was continued this year, and he urges the absent Frederick, Elector of Saxony, by letters from the Pope and his own, written in a very friendly manner, to punish severely and vigorously the license of the people and the change of the sacred laws and ceremonies. Then he asks the princes themselves at the Diet not to allow any innovation to be made in religion, pretending that he knows nothing of the princes' reply given the previous year to the legate of Pope Adrian, except that a letter written privately to him, under the title of the princes, has been produced, which he thinks was composed by certain men out of private hatred against the Roman commonwealth.

units.la: ANNUS MDXXIV.
units.tr: The Year 1524

units.la: CARDINALIS LOTHARINGI iun-ior su Joannes Castellanus Thornacensis, Doctor Theologus, (qui in Campania, in regione Partensi, in Urbe Vicensi, Episcopi Metensis sede, tandemque Metis magno zelo Evangelium docuerat) in itinere interceptus quartâ Maii carceri mancipatur, in quo crudeliter novem menses habitus, duodecimâ die Januarii anni sequentis ab ordine sacerdotali degradatus, ab urbis Vicensis magistratu vivus crematus est.
units.tr: John Castellanus of Tournai, the younger, a doctor of theology, who had taught the Gospel with great zeal in Champagne, in the Partois region, in the town of Vic, a seat of the bishop of Metz, and finally at Metz, was seized while travelling on 4 May and thrown into prison. He was cruelly held there for nine months. On 12 January of the following year he was stripped of his priestly orders and burned alive by the magistrates of the town of Vic.

units.la: ALBERTUS Archiepiscopus Moguntinus ut superioribus annis Halberstadii & Miltenbergi, ita hoc anno Halæ Saxonum in cives Evangelicos sæviit.
units.tr: As in earlier years at Halberstadt and Miltenberg, so this year at Halle in Saxony, Albert, archbishop of Mainz, raged against the Evangelical citizens.

units.la: JOANNES Blanckefeld Berlinensis, Archiepiscopus Rigensis, Jurisconsultus celebris, & Revaliensis ac Derbatensis in Livonia Episcopus, Casparo defuncto succedit, & à civitate Rigensi missis in urbem internunciis, & confirmatione privilegiorum generali, iuramentū subiectionis debitū exigit. Cùm autem religionis emendatæ, qualē civitas expetebat, mentionem nullā in specie faceret, ac insuper duo templa & πτωχίας civitatis sibi suisque reddi flagitaret, re insecta illi dimissi sunt. Paulò post Kakenhusiâ Archiepiscopus Rigensis arcem & oppidum ingressus, contra fidem civibus datam pastorem Bernhardum Bruggemannum, & collegam illius Paulum Bloshagium, & schola moderatorem Gilebertum Schofferum, idola Pontificia improbantes, oppido pellit, & non ditione modo sua, sed & urbe Rigâ, nondum ei subiecta, iis interdicit. Lemfalæ postea ministro Ecclesiæ pio, ac erudito, eiecto, nobilitatem dicecesis omnem iuramento sibi astringit. Hinc ad Rigensem civitatem legatos, iuramentum fidelitatis ac subiectionis debitum flagitantes, denuo mittit. Quæ simpliciter respondet, nisi de religione & doctrina Evangelii instaurata, quam privilegium & ornamentum civitatis præcipuum ac summum censeant, & de templis omnibus recte sibi cautum sit, non posse se iusiurandum, quod flagitet, dare. Cùm enim videant, Archiepiscopum omnes ingenii ac potentiæ suæ nervos, ad extirpandam funditus puriorem religionem, quam ipsi vel cum vitæ periculo retinendam ducant, intendere, parum se de Archiepiscopi gratia, amore & fide sibi posse polliceri aut concordiam sperare. Quod si in fidem eius concesserint, perpetuas animorum distractiones, inimicitias, bella & clades, atque adeo interitum animæ & corporis, bonorum & fortunarum omnium suarum, totiusq; urbis exitium sequuturum se prævidere: cui occasionem præbere incô-lidefideratâ iuramenti præstatione non decreverint. Sic gravius etiam exacerbato Archiepiscopo civitas Rigensis, à Magistro ordinis, V Valtero Plettenbergio auxilium & defensionem contra Archiepiscopũ petit, cumque solum Dominum se agnituram esse prositetur:(antea enim Rigenses Archiepiscopo & Magistro ordinis ex æquo iuramentum fidelitatis præstare, & provocationes à sententiis Senatus ad utrumq; pariter fieri solebant) Is receptis in tutelam Rigensibus initio sequentis anni, urbem illustri & solenni pompâ de novo ingreditur. Quâ occasione primùm reformatæ religionis liberè in tota urbe exercendæ privilegium ab hoc Livoniæ Magistro, illiusque deinceps successoribus, impetrârunt. Canonici verò Rigenses benevolentiam & fidem suam erga civitatem Rigensem multis verbis prædicantes, cum partem urbis quam tenebant, se suo sumptu munire velle, & omnia summa polliciti essent: paulatim præmissis omnibus suis fortunis, ex urbe discedunt, & machinas ac tormenta ex turribus ac mœnibus detracta clam subducere conantur. Quâ eorum perfidiâ animadversâ, Senatus omnes eorum domos, molendina, agros, & fundos urbi vicinos occupat, & suis civibus colendos distribuit, & partem illam urbis aggeribus & valtis cinctâ firmissimè munit, cōcessa tamē
units.tr: John Blanckefeld of Berlin, archbishop of Riga, a celebrated jurist and bishop of Reval and Dorpat in Livonia, succeeded Caspar, who had died. He sent messengers to the city of Riga and demanded the customary oath of submission, in return for a general confirmation of privileges. But since he made no specific mention of the reform of religion, which the city was seeking, and further demanded that the city's two churches and its almshouse be handed over to him and his people, the envoys were dismissed without result. Shortly afterwards the archbishop entered the castle and town of Kokenhusen and, contrary to the pledge given to the citizens, drove out the minister Bernhard Bruggemann, his colleague Paul Bloshagius, and the schoolmaster Gilbert Schoffer, who were condemning Papist idols, and forbade them to live not only in his own territory but also in the city of Riga, which was not yet subject to him. Later, at Lemsal, he expelled the godly and learned minister of the Church and bound all the nobility of the diocese to himself by oath. From there he again sent envoys to the city of Riga, demanding the due oath of fealty and submission. The citizens replied plainly that they could not give the oath he demanded unless the reformed religion and the teaching of the Gospel, which they regarded as the chief and greatest privilege and ornament of the city, were restored, and unless all the churches were secured to them. For they saw that the archbishop was directing all the strength of his talent and power to rooting out utterly the purer religion, which they judged must be kept even at risk of life; so they could promise themselves little of the archbishop's favour, love and good faith, or hope for harmony. If they should entrust themselves to his good faith, they foresaw that perpetual division of minds, enmity, wars and disasters would follow, and indeed the ruin of soul and body, of all their goods and fortunes, and the destruction of the whole city; and they would not give him the opportunity for this by taking the oath he demanded. Thus, with the archbishop made still more bitter, the city of Riga sought help and protection against the archbishop from the Master of the Order, Walter von Plettenberg. Since the city declared that it would recognise him alone as lord (for the Rigans had previously sworn fealty equally to the archbishop and the Master of the Order, and appeals from the decisions of the Senate were customarily made to both alike), he received the Rigans under his protection and at the beginning of the following year entered the city again with a splendid and solemn procession. On this occasion the citizens first obtained from this Master of Livonia, and afterwards from his successors, the privilege of freely exercising the reformed religion throughout the whole city. The canons of Riga, extolling in many words their goodwill and loyalty towards the city of Riga, promised that they would fortify at their own expense the part of the city which they held, and offered all sorts of assurances. Gradually, however, they abandoned all their property and left the city, and tried secretly to carry off the engines and artillery removed from the towers and walls. When this treachery was noticed, the Senate seized all their houses, mills, fields and estates near the city, distributed them to its own citizens to cultivate, and strongly fortified that part of the city with embankments and ramparts, while allowing the canons free entry to the city, the right to lodge with citizens, and the liberty to carry on trade with them.

units.la: {} Canonicis liberâ urbem ingrediendi, & hospitio civium utendi, cùmque illis commercia exercendi facultate. Gravissimè autem exacerbatus his Rigensium actionibus Archiepiscopus, & cum Magistro ordinis, cuius patrocinio illi nitebantur, simultates & odium immane exercens, cum Moschis consilia communicare adversus Livoniæ Magistrum, in vulgo spargebatur. Itaque universâ nobilitate, collegiis & populo adversus eum inflammato: publica Livoniæ Comitia VVolmariæ instituta sunt, in quibus suam innocentiam omnibus ordinibus Archiepiscopus demonstrare conabatur. Sed tandem communi consensu res eò deducta est, ut deinceps Archiepiscopus cum omnib. suis suffraganeis Episcopis, collegiis, iuribus, sessione, &c. Magistro ordinis eiusque successoribus se perpetuò subiiceret: ac deinceps nihil vel iure vel armis, inscio Magistro, contra Rigenses se moliturum promitteret. Ut enim ob communicata cum Moscho adversus Livoniam consilia, præsentissimum vitæ & famæ periculum declinaret: conditiones omnes, ab ordinibus propositas, se, accepisse apud suos ostendit.
units.tr: The archbishop, gravely angered by these actions of the Rigans, and exercising enmity and immense hatred against the Master of the Order, under whose protection they stood, was reported in common talk to be sharing plans with the Muscovites against the Master of Livonia. And so, with the whole nobility, the colleges and the people inflamed against him, the public Diet of Livonia was convened at Wolmar, where the archbishop tried to demonstrate his innocence to all the estates. But at last, by common consent, the matter was brought to this point: that thereafter the archbishop, with all his suffragan bishops, colleges, rights, seat and so on, would submit himself permanently to the Master of the Order and his successors, and would promise that he would henceforth attempt nothing against the Rigans, either by right or by arms, without the Master's knowledge. For, to avert the very present danger to his life and reputation arising from the plans he had shared with Moscow against Livonia, he showed that he had accepted among his own people all the conditions proposed by the estates.

units.la: DANICI EPISCOPI, qui in senatu regni præcipuum & summum locum obtinebant, cursum Evangelii in Dania ad aliquot annos intercluserunt. Etsi enim Fridericus ticus Rex ut exemplo multos in regno isto ad pietatem invitavit, ita autoritate regiâ eos defendit, qui puriora religionis semina primi ibi iecerunt: tamen per Episcoporum refragantium sibi potentiam Ecclesias reformare, & idola, Antichristi insignia, abolere non potuit.
units.tr: The bishops of Denmark, who held the chief and highest place in the Senate of the kingdom, blocked the course of the Gospel in Denmark for some years. For although King Frederick, by his example, invited many in that kingdom to piety, and by royal authority defended those who first sowed the purer seeds of religion there, nevertheless he could not reform the churches and abolish the idols, the badges of Antichrist, because of the power of the bishops who opposed him.

units.la: SPIRENSIS Episcopus Joannem Baderum, Concionatorem Landavien-sem per Vicarium suum excommunicat, quod auricularem Confessionem, purgatorium, Missas pro vivis & mortuis, invocationem Mariæ, vota monastica, discrimen dierum & ciborum, &c. ex scripturis ausus fuerit impugnare. Literæ excommunicationis Dominicâ Cantate Spiræ valvis summi templi sunt affixæ. Baderus per Notarium publicum confecto scripto ab excommunicatione ista illegitima, atque ideo nulla, appellat ad Concilium, quod brevi celebrandum esse in Germania Principes Imperii nuper in conventu Norimbergensi decreverant.
units.tr: The bishop of Speyer excommunicated John Bader, preacher at Landau, through his vicar, because he had dared to attack from the Scriptures auricular confession, purgatory, masses for the living and the dead, the invocation of Mary, monastic vows, the distinction of days and foods, and so on. The letters of excommunication were posted on the doors of the great church at Speyer on the Sunday Cantate. Bader, by a written instrument drawn up by a public notary, appealed from this unlawful and therefore void excommunication to the Council, which the princes of the Empire had recently decided at the diet of Nuremberg would shortly be held in Germany.

units.la: ARGENTINENSIS Episcopus quàm subdolè prædicationi Evangelicè in urbe Argentina insidiatus sit, ex Capitone libet audire: Episcopus Argentinensis supremæ autoritatis est, quam tuetur dexteritate quâdam in rebus agendis, ut in Ecclesiastico rarâ & singulari. Adhæc sibi aliquis esse videtur, & nihil iniquius fert, quàm se negligi. Iam vero crescente Christo sua putat æstimationi fieri detrimentum, quòd hinc cadit inanis formido de Episcopali stomacho, terribili quodammodo, dum stultitia & error vul-gum possideret. Is negotium fecit maritis Sacerdotibus, quos pro tèplis palàm devovit diris, idq; tum, cum omnia tuta sperassemus. De industria enim quiddam placiditatis pra se tulerat, ut sic incautos, & quod aiunt, in utramq; aurem dormientes opprimeret. Summa consilii fuit, inter se cives committere, dum pars fulmen istud Episcopale horrerent, pars magnificè contemnerent. Sub idem tempus à Senatu per dolos Canonici ad D. Petrum impetrârunt, ut à Parochia illorum providendâ me abstinere iuberent. Præterea via instituta fuit, quâ maritos fratres ex urbe deturbandos omnes putassent, inprimis autem Bucerum. Subornatus est Comes de Lynigen senior, qui mihi præsenti tô[?] ties manus inferre tentaret, dictis priùs in os multis contumeliis atrocissimis, idque intra urbem, intra ædes Papistici Prælati. At nos omnibus ex his periculis Christus eripuit. Nam ubi Episcopus excommunicatione publicassFet, nos intra eandem noctem appellationem fratrum nomine effinximus. Postridie appellatum est præsente Notario, mox excusa omnia prodierunt.
