Quo remedio, populus ne quid super excommunicatione disceptaret, cavimus: expectârat enim nostra in se vicissim sententia Episcopus, quâ se cum complicibus damnaremus, quares ad manifestam desiisset seditionem. Talia sunt ingeingenia, ha artes Episcoporum, tranquillos inter se committere. Quarta die ejus hebdemada mihi per Senatum Parochia renunciatur, qui mihi videbar Senatus autoritate pridem ingressus. Statim fit rumor, eijciendos verbi pracones concurritur, quiritatur, incusantur vulgo sacerdotes, jaciuntur convitia etiam in senatum, sed ab extrema tantum plebe. Proceres aliqui a minis agre temperabant, quin sacerdotibus pessima quaeq; si nos excludi contingeret, denunciarent. Tot ribus simul conclusis tamen adnitor omnia expedire, do negotium ijs quos gratos populo noram, verbis tranquillis plebem ab inquietudine contineant, me esse curaturum apud Senatum, ne quid Evangelio decedat, necrem tam esse deploratam, ut imperitis videri possit: rescindi sapius levi momento sententias aquiores, & perspicuum satis, Curtisanos tanti non haberi, ut in illorum gratiam Senatores velint posthabere suos cives in causa tam pia, atque alia id genus. Quibus peractis studia paulisper continuimus, quoad super certioribus consiliis dispiceremus. A Consilio igitur agendi apud Senatum facultatem impetro. Statuitur dies sabbathi. Interea ecce nova tragedia, Capitulo meo S. Thoma datur spes, ut ferebat, a Senatu, Bucerum non fore tutum apud templum Aurelia, quod maritus. Ibi cura nostri opus fuit, ne quid binc incommodi. Porro Comes de Lynigen crudelia magis commovit, sed aliunde, ut videtur, incitatus. Nam ut eram causa conficienda componendaq; litis ad illum admandatur, die Iovis ejus septimanæ, placidè, satis re-spondit, & rem perduxit in diem posterum. Iterum me sistæ intra curiam Domini ab Henneberg. Tum ille mox iracundâ multa, Domino edium cum nepo-te & tota familia inspectante, infandis contumeliis, petitu & clamoribus furiosis audiendo defatigatum interficere admolitus est, nemine omnium prohibente, quoad me Deus tandem eriperet. Periculum, mihi crede, fuit anceps. Sed praeter animi formidinem vultum non mutavi, ipsdem fortiter vestigiis inhæsi, recordatus in eodem articulo, omnes capitis mei capillos numeratos, casurum aut evasurum, ut patri visum esset: qui filio nihil incommodi velit, neque quàm velit, illi posse quicquam incommodius accidere.
units.tr: ARGENTINENSIS, the bishop of Strasbourg, how craftily he laid traps for the evangelical preaching in the city of Strasbourg, may be learned from Capito: The bishop of Strasbourg holds supreme authority, which he maintains with a certain dexterity in conducting affairs, rare and singular in an ecclesiastic. Besides, he seems to be someone of importance, and bears nothing more unjustly than being neglected. Now, as Christ grows, he thinks his esteem will suffer harm, because from this a vain dread arises of the episcopal temper, which is in a way terrible, while folly and error possess the common people. He caused trouble for the married priests, whom he openly cursed with dire curses from the pulpits, and this when we had hoped that everything was safe. For he had deliberately displayed a certain calm, so that he might crush the unwary, who, as they say, were sleeping on both ears. The sum of his plan was to set the citizens against one another: while one part shrank from that episcopal thunderbolt, another part scorned it grandly. About the same time, through the trickery of the canons, they obtained from the Senate, at St. Peter's, an order that I should abstain from providing for their parish. Besides, a plan was devised by which they thought all the married brothers should be driven out of the city, and above all Bucer. The elder Count of Lininger was suborned, who repeatedly tried to lay hands on me in person, first hurling at my face many most atrocious insults, and this within the city, within the house of a Papist prelate. But Christ snatched us from all these dangers. For when the bishop had published the excommunication, we drew up on the very same night an appeal in the name of the brothers. On the following day the appeal was made in the presence of a notary, and soon all these things came out into the open. By this remedy we took care that the people should not dispute anything about the excommunication: for the bishop was expecting our sentence in return against him and his accomplices, by which we would condemn him, since he had ceased from open sedition. Such are the cleverness and arts of bishops, to set peaceful men against one another. On the fourth day of that week the parish was announced to me by the Senate, which I thought I had recently entered by the Senate's authority. Immediately a rumour arose that the preachers of the word were to be thrown out; there was complaining, the priests were accused in the common talk, and insults were hurled even at the Senate, but only from the lowest of the people. Some of the nobles could scarcely restrain themselves from threats, so that they would denounce every kind of evil against the priests if we should happen to be excluded. With so many things closing in at once, I nevertheless strove to settle everything. I entrusted the business to those whom I knew to be pleasing to the people, to keep the common folk in check with calm words; I would take care with the Senate that nothing be lost to the Gospel, nor the cause be so desperate as to seem so to the inexperienced: that more equitable decisions had often been rescinded on a slight pretext, and it was plain enough that the courtiers were not held in such esteem that the senators would want to put their own citizens after them, in a cause so pious, and other things of that kind. When these things were done, we held back our efforts for a little while, until we could see more clearly what to do. So I obtained from the Council the opportunity of acting before the Senate. The day of the Sabbath was fixed. Meanwhile, behold, a new tragedy: my chapter of St. Thomas was given, as it reported, hope by the Senate that Bucer would not be safe at the church of Aurelia, where the married man was. Care for us was needed there, lest any harm should come from it. Further, the Count of Lininger stirred up cruel things more than before, but, as it seems, was incited from elsewhere. For when the matter of my case, the settling and composing of the dispute, was referred to him on the Thursday of that week, he answered calmly and quite reasonably, and put the business off until the next day. Again I was summoned within the court of the Lord of Henneberg. Then he, straightway, with much angry shouting, with the lord of the house and his nephew and the whole household looking on, set about killing me, wearied with listening to unspeakable insults, demands and furious cries, and no one among them all forbade it, until God at last snatched me away. The danger, believe me, was great. But beyond my fear of mind I did not change my expression; I stood firm on the very same footing, remembering that in the same extremity all the hairs of my head were numbered, and that either I would fall or escape, as it seemed good to the Father, who wishes no harm to come to his son, and to whom nothing more harmful can happen than what he wishes.

units.la: Appetebat sabbathum, magnâ libertate ago cum Senatu, rejectis adversariorum argumentis, quæ conjicere oportuit. Magnum erat omnium silentium, ut fit, dum quisque sibi deplorata causa cavet. Deliberârunt itaque in horam propè quintam, neque sine Deo deliberârunt. Nam qui nudius quartus Parochiâ me abdicârant, illi ipsi iterum addicunt, ad natalem usque Iohannis Baptistæ: nam aliter mihi addicta non erat. Fraterea convenerat cum Parochiis omnibus Christianè providendis. Nec tamen interim, dum parochys potiti sumus, eluctati sumus, ut liberè ab adversariis Christum liceat asserere. Mira mutatio: Curthisanis, qui missis undique literis nos pridie expulsos gloriati sunt, vultus mærore concidit. Pûs ex dispensatione mens erecta. Civium & Senatûs concordia facta, quæ tamen revera nec dum dissuta suta fuerat. Propter excommunicationem Episcopi nemo sacrificulus, nulla mulier commota est : tam commodè cecidit appellatio. Senatus agit causâ mei cum Comite, neque aliud captamus, quàm utcunq; diluerim objecta crimina: omnia mihi salva, sed inquieta satis etiam post fatalem illam septimanâ, in quam tanta negotia simul inciderunt. Iam expectamus interdictum novum Imperij, vaticinium Caesareum, vim Cacodaemonis universam, quae spero inania concident, & in nervum erumpent. Nam propius, si perget, cum Episcopo agemus, siquidem ultima experturus videtur, & nos ceu cum devoto hoste decernemus.
units.tr: He was heading for the Sabbath, and I dealt with the Senate with great frankness, setting aside the arguments of our opponents, which I had to anticipate. There was great silence among them all, as usual, while each man took care of his own interests once his cause seemed lost. They deliberated until nearly five o'clock, and they did not deliberate without God. For the men who four days earlier had removed me from the parish now restored it to me, until the feast of the Nativity of John the Baptist; otherwise the parish would not have been awarded to me. Moreover, a meeting was held with all the parishes concerning how they should be Christianly provided for. Yet in the meantime, while we have held the parishes, we have not yet struggled free enough to be able to assert Christ openly against our opponents. A remarkable change: the Curthisani, who by letters sent everywhere had boasted the day before that we had been expelled, have had their faces fall in grief. From the arrangement, the mind is lifted up. A harmony between the citizens and the Senate has been reached, though in truth it had not yet been properly stitched together. Because of the Bishop's excommunication, no priest has been stirred up and no woman has been moved; the appeal has fallen so conveniently. The Senate is conducting my case with the Count, and we seek nothing else than that I might somehow clear myself of the charges laid against me. All my affairs are safe, but still rather unsettled, even after that fateful week in which so many matters fell upon us at once. Now we await a new interdict of the Empire, Caesar's prophecy, and the whole power of the evil demon, which, I hope, will collapse into nothingness and break its sinews. For if he persists, we shall deal more closely with the Bishop, since he seems about to make his final attempt, and we shall make our decision as against a sworn enemy.

units.la: CUNRADUS TRAEGER Provincialis Augustinianorum, ut Ecclesias Helveticas & Argentinensem turbaret, centum paradoxa Argentinae edidit, & Friburgi Uchtlandiae disputanda propositi pro Traditionibus hominum contra Traditiones Dei : tacitè, ut multi opinabantur, opposita disputationi Zwinglii de verbi Dei auctoritate.
units.tr: CUNRADUS TRAEGER, provincial of the Augustinians, in order to disturb the Helvetic churches and that of Strasbourg, published at Strasbourg one hundred paradoxes, and proposed for disputation at Freiburg in Uechtland theses in defence of the traditions of men against the traditions of God. Many believed that this was tacitly set against Zwingli's disputation on the authority of God's Word.

units.la: INTER has tot & tantas doctrinae puritoris persequutiones mirabilis negotii Evangelici successus est conspectus.
units.tr: AMID these so many and so great persecutions of purer doctrine, the successful progress of the Evangelical work was seen to be remarkable.

units.la: FRIDERICI Daniae Regis laudatissimis conatinatibus etsi, ut supra dictum, Episcoporum potentia obstabat, ita tamen favit Deus, ut non solum praecipuae civitates, Haffnia, Malmoia, Ripae, & alii non paucae, verum etiam tota fere dioecesis Vibergensis, freta Regis patrocinio, abiecto
units.tr: Although, as was said above, the power of the bishops stood in the way of the most praiseworthy endeavours of King Frederick of Denmark, God so favoured them that not only the chief cities, Copenhagen, Malmö, Ribe and not a few others, but also almost the whole diocese of Viborg, relying on the King's patronage and having cast off

units.la: Papismo Evangelismum amplexarentur. Hemmingius celebrat etiam Magnum Gbie Dominum de Krenkerup, qui, secundum Regem primus in regno Danico revocatæ doctrinæ autor fuerit, per literas à Luthero rectè instructus, & patrocinio suo primos Evangelii præcones contra vim aliorum defenderit.
units.tr: Papism, embraced the Evangelical religion. Hemmingius also praises the great lord Gbie of Krenkerup, who, second only to the King, was the first author of the restored doctrine in the Danish kingdom, rightly instructed by letters from Luther, and who by his patronage defended the first heralds of the Gospel against the violence of others.

units.la: In LIVONIA Evangelion, inquit Lutherus, oritur, & procedit, præsertim apud Rigenses feliciter quorum literas ac legatum nuper suscepi, sic mirabilis est Christus. Sed & Episcopus tandem unus Christo nomen dedit & Evangelizat in PRVSSIA, nempe Sambiensis, quem fovet ac erudit Joannes Brismannus, quem illuc misimus abjecto cuculló: ut & Prussia regno Satanæ valedicere incipiat. Episcopus iste fuit GEORGIUS de Polentia, cui Lutherus commentarium suum in Genesin inscripsit, quiq; hoc ipso anno civibus Braunsbergicis petentibus cōcionatorem Evāgelicum misit Christophorum quendam, eumq; per Illustrem D. Petrum Burggravium & Baronem à Dhona, Capitaneum Braunsbergensem, populo præsentavit, additâ hac clausulâ, in sua ad Capitaneum epistolâ: Wir verschē vns/ es soll/ ob Gott wil/ Christliche liebe vnd alles guts darauß entstehen. Dienstag nach Jubilate.
units.tr: In LIVONIA, says Luther, the Gospel arises and advances, especially among the people of Riga, whose letters and envoy I lately received; so wonderful is Christ. But also a bishop has at last given his name to Christ and is preaching the Gospel in Prussia, namely the bishop of Samland, whom John Brismann fosters and instructs, and whom we sent there, having cast off the cowl, so that Prussia too may begin to bid farewell to Satan's kingdom. That bishop was Georg von Polenz, to whom Luther dedicated his commentary on Genesis. In this same year, at the request of the citizens of Braunsberg, he sent them a certain Christopher as Evangelical preacher, and presented him to the people through the Illustrious Lord Peter Burggrave and Baron von Dohna, captain of Braunsberg, adding this clause in his letter to the captain: "We promise you that, God willing, Christian love and every good thing will arise from it. Tuesday after Jubilate."

units.la: REGIOMONTI in Borussia, feriâ tertiâ post Invocavit, statuæ in templo cathedrali per pueros pureos & senes deiectæ, & tabulæ altariorum ablatæ sunt, idque de consilio Pauli Sperati.
units.tr: At KÖNIGSBERG in Prussia, on the Tuesday after Invocavit, statues in the cathedral church were thrown down by youths and old men, and the altarpieces were removed; this was done on the advice of Paul Speratus.

units.la: MEGAPOLITANUS Ducatus gubernabatur hoc tempore ab Henrico & Alberto fratribus, Magni Ducis Megapolitani filiis. Uterque hoc anno à Luthero petunt Evangelistas, alter per Joannem Loser, alter per Priorem Sternbergensem. Etsi autem Albertus Papisticam religionem in sua Ducatus parte retinuit: tamen Henricus cum filio Magno Principe literatissimo in sua ditione Ecclesias reformârunt, operâ M. Gerhardi Oemekenii, & aliorum usi. Mortuo autem Alberto Henricus suos ex fratre nepotes Joannem Albertum & Ulricum piè instituti voluit, qui defuncto patruo Henrico, totum Ducatum à reliquiis fermenti Papistici repurgarunt. Floret hodie Joannis Alberti ex filio Joanne Nepos, JOANNES ALBERTUS, orthodoxæ doctrinæ strenuus propugnator.
units.tr: The Duchy of Mecklenburg was at this time governed by the brothers Henry and Albert, sons of the Grand Duke Magnus of Mecklenburg. Both of them this year asked Luther for evangelists: one through Johann Loser, the other through the Prior of Sternberg. Although Albert kept the Papist religion in his part of the duchy, Henry, together with his son Magnus, a most learned prince, reformed the churches in his territory, using the services of Master Gerhard Oemeke and others. When Albert died, Henry wished his nephews Johann Albert and Ulrich, who had been piously brought up, to succeed him; and when their uncle Henry died, they purged the whole duchy of the remnants of Papist leaven. Today the grandson of Johann Albert, through his son Johann, flourishes: JOHANN ALBERT, a vigorous champion of orthodox doctrine.

units.la: VVISMARIÆ in Ducatu Megapolensi primus taxare, abusus Pontificios & regnum Antichristi revelare cœpit Henricus Mollensius, quem Albertus Dux Megapolitanus Magni filius, maritus novus, celebratis paulò ante Berlini cum Joachimi I. Electoris Brandeburgici filia Anna nuptiis, aulicum Ecclesiasten secum adduxerat, eumque toto Qua-
units.tr: At WISMAR in the Duchy of Mecklenburg, Henry Mollensius first began to censure the Papist abuses and to reveal the kingdom of Antichrist. Duke Albert, son of Magnus and a newly married husband, had brought him with him to court as preacher, having shortly before celebrated at Berlin his wedding with Anna, daughter of Joachim I, Elector of Brandenburg, and he allowed him to preach in the church of St George, and to expose and refute the hypocrisy of priests and monks, throughout the whole

units.la: Quadragesimæ tempore, & in feriis Paschæ concionari in templo Georgii, & Sacerdotū ac Monachorum hypocrisin retegere ac redarguere sinebat. Huic consona, sed maiori cum libertate & facundiâ, in Franciscanorum cœnobio, Henricus Neuerus custos seu inspector vicinorum in tota provincia eiusdem ordinis cœnobiorum, paulò ante electus, in feriis Paschæ magno hominum concursu & admiratione, ac Principe ipso, cum recens ducta coniuge conciones illius frequentantę, prædicare incipiebat, ac quò acerbioribus odiis suorum Monachorum & patrum ordinis expositus erat, eò ardentiore zelo ac constantiâ cursum prædicationis semel susceptæ urgebat, præsertim cum aulæ & civium plurimorum, ac senatorum etiam aliquot patrocinio tectus esset.
units.tr: season of Lent and on the days of Easter. Similar to this, but with greater freedom and eloquence, in the Franciscan monastery Henry Neuer, custodian or overseer of the neighbouring monasteries of the same order throughout the province, recently elected, began to preach on the days of Easter, to great crowds and admiration, and with the Prince himself attending his sermons with his newly wed wife. The more bitter the hatred of his own monks and the fathers of his order to which he was exposed, the more ardent his zeal and constancy in pursuing the course of preaching once undertaken, especially since he was sheltered by the patronage of the court, of many citizens, and of several senators as well.

units.la: MAGDEBURGÆ Melior Mericius, Eberhardus VVidenseeDoctor, & Johannes Fritzhans, edunt publicè themata octodecim adversus traditiones Pontificias, vota monastica, sacrificium Missæ, primatum Papæ, purgatorium, vigilias, iustificationem operū, &c: eaq; ad disputandum proponunt. Sed nemo Pontificiorum disputationis aleam subire voluit.
units.tr: At MAGDEBURG, Melchior Mericius, Eberhard Widensee, Doctor, and Johann Fritzhans publicly issued eighteen theses against Papist traditions, monastic vows, the sacrifice of the Mass, the primacy of the Pope, purgatory, vigils, justification by works, and so on, and proposed them for disputation. But none of the Papists was willing to risk the hazard of a disputation.

units.la: Consul igitur Nicolaus Sturm, & plurimi cives sincerioris doctrinæ cupidi, Lutherum VVirtenbergâ evocant. Is, cū Augustinianorū templū angustius videretur, ad D. Joannē docuit: & paucos dies ibi moratus, cum consiliū de emendatione Religionis suū Consuli& delectis civiū exposuisset: Nicolaum Ambsdorf‐fium se ipsis missurum pastorem ostendit, cui non secus ac sibi ipsi omnib. in rebus cōfidere possent. Ambsdorffius igitur de sententia Lutheri Magdeburgenses Ecclesias pie & praeclare à se institutas, cum quidem collega fidū Doctorem Eberhardum V Vydenseiū aliquā‐ diu haberet, doctrinæ suæ voce & consiliis sa‐ lutaribus, totos octodecim annos rexit, donec Naoburgensis Ecclesiæ Episcopus crearetur.
units.tr: Therefore the Consul Nicolaus Sturm and many citizens eager for purer doctrine summoned Luther from Wittenberg. Since the Augustinian church seemed too cramped, he taught at St John's. After staying there a few days, and having set out his plan for reforming religion to the Consul and the chosen citizens, he showed that he would send them Nicolas Amsdorf as pastor, in whom they could trust in all things no less than in himself. Amsdorf, therefore, at Luther's wish, having for some time the faithful colleague Doctor Eberhard Widensee, governed the Magdeburg churches, which he had piously and splendidly set up, for eighteen years, with the voice of his teaching and his wholesome counsels, until he was made bishop of the church of Naumburg.

units.la: BREMAM autore Henrico Sutphaniensi, qui bienniū jam ibi docuerat, Jacobus Præpo‐situs Theologiæ Licentiatus, Augustinianus Antuerpiensis, qui ex Belgico se ad Lutherū contulerat, vocatus in templo Mariano, & paulo post Joannes Timannus Amsterdamus, vir eloquens, in æde Martini pastor constitu‐ tus est: qui anno 1525. demū Pontificias Mis‐sas, in omnibus parochiarum & monasterio‐ rū templis, solo cathedrali excepto, aboleverūt.
units.tr: At BREMEN, on the initiative of Henry of Zutphen, who had already taught there for two years, Jacob, provost and licentiate in theology, an Augustinian of Antwerp who had come to Luther from the Low Countries, was called to the church of St Mary, and shortly afterwards John Timann of Amsterdam, an eloquent man, was appointed pastor in the church of St Martin. In 1525 at last they abolished the Papist Masses in all the churches of the parishes and the monastery, the cathedral alone excepted.

units.la: BRUNSWIGAE nō sine magnis motibus, qui triennio ipsum durârunt, doctrina Papæ abje‐sta, doctrina Christi fuit admissa. Minoritis hoc anno Concilium ibi celebrantibus, & pro‐positis publicis propositionibus, invocationem sanctorū, & sacrificium Missæ tueri conanti‐ bus, non solùm viri docti, sed cives etiam ali‐ quot se acriter opposuere. Monachi eorum nomina deferunt ad Unionem (sic enim vocabatur consistorium Ecclesiasticorum Prælatorum, in quo erant decem Prælati, ut Abbas Ægidianus, duo Decani, ad S. Blasium, & ad S. Cyriacum in suburbio, & deinde septem pastores, Unio ad Senatum urbis. Is plerosq;, qui accusati, eiicit, lectione librorū Lutheri omnibus interdicit, in libros novi Testamenti à Luthero versi, ostiatim inquirit. Tamen hoc ipso anno Joannes Copmannus Sacellanus ad D. Virginem, & Conradus Trutenbellius graviter pro cōcione contra Pontificios disputant, civibusq; amorem Evangelii instillant. Novæ igitur turbæ. Præsides Unionis volunt Sacellanos remotos: cives volunt retentos. Senatus nolens reluctari Unioni, discedit ex urbe. Cives illum revocant, obedientiam promittunt in omnibus: modò Evangelii libera prædicatio concedatur. Redit Senatus : Dominicanos & Minoritas, disputationem cum concionatoribus detrectantes, eiicit: Præsidibus Unionis, dimissionem concionatorum petentibus, respondet: culpam huius rei ipsis præstandam, quod otiosi ventres substituerint sibi, quos modò accusent Sacellanos. Si nunc illos amotos velint, perdituros eos & se, & urbem, & Senatum.
units.tr: At BRUNSWICK, not without great disturbances, which lasted three years, the doctrine of the Pope was rejected and the doctrine of Christ admitted. When the Minorites held a council there this year and put forward public propositions defending the invocation of the saints and the sacrifice of the Mass, not only learned men but several citizens too opposed them sharply. The monks reported their names to the Union (for so was called the consistory of ecclesiastical prelates, in which there were ten prelates, such as the Abbot of St Egidius, two deans, of St Blasius and of St Cyriacus in the suburb, and then seven pastors), and the Union reported them to the Senate of the city. The Senate expelled most of those accused, forbade everyone to read Luther's books, and searched house by house for the books of the New Testament translated by Luther. Yet this same year John Copmann, chaplain at St Mary's, and Konrad Trutenbell vigorously disputed against the Papists in their sermons and instilled love of the Gospel into the citizens. Thus new troubles arose. The presidents of the Union wanted the chaplains removed; the citizens wanted them kept. The Senate, unwilling to resist the Union, left the city. The citizens recalled it, promising obedience in all things, provided that free preaching of the Gospel be allowed. The Senate returned, and expelled the Dominicans and Minorites, who refused disputation with the preachers. To the presidents of the Union, who asked for the dismissal of the preachers, it replied that the blame for this must rest with them, since they had installed idle bellies, whom they now accused as chaplains. If they now wished those men removed, they would bring ruin on themselves, on the city, and on the Senate.

units.la: EIMBECCA urbs est Ducum Brunsvicensiū in Grubenhagen. Hanc benigno oculo adspexit hoc anno Deus, ministerio M. Ernesti Burmeisteri, & D. Godeschalci Croppii, aliorumq;, & indulgentiarum Papalium vanitatem, & gratiæ Jesu Christi efficacitatem populo commonstrans.
units.tr: Eimbeck is a town of the Dukes of Brunswick, in Grubenhagen. This year God looked on it with a kindly eye, through the ministry of M. Ernst Burmeister, Godeschalk Kropp, and others, showing the people the emptiness of papal indulgences and the efficacy of the grace of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Incidit in hunc annum & COMITATUS HOYENSIS Ecclesiarum reformatio, quam Jodocus Comes inchoavit, & quatuor filij ipsius Albertus, Ericus, Otto, & Fridericus, ultimi istius stemmatis Comites, continuârunt. Legerat Jodocus Comes in summo mærore suo submissos sibi àsocero Comite V Wolfgango de Gleichen, Lutheri & Melanchthonis libros, contuleratq; de iis cum aulico concionatore, sacrifico & confessore suo Corado Drudekeno, quem instigatus ab Ernesto Duce Luneburgensi V Vittebergâ misit, accersitu virum aliquê eruditum, qui monachos Terminarios, & alios missificos copescere posset. Luthe rus misit Adrianum Boxschotium Antuerpiensem, qui Antuerpiæ cucullum exuerat & V Vittebergam profectus fuerat, virum in Latina lingua facundum, & in Belgico sermone suavem, qui de voluntate Comitis templum ingressus Neoburgi (quod est amplissimi Comitatus primarium oppidum) Monachum in Lutherum ex suggestu fulminantem, ita adortus est: Ego ad hoc vocatus sum ab inclyto Comite Hoyensi, Domino Jodoco, ut te & tuos mendacii arguerem: ideo dic tu perverse monache, idq; palam coram tota Ecclesia hac, ubi, quando, & quibus in locis erravit Lutherus? Obmutuit Monachus, & clam de suggestu descendens alió profugit, nunquam in Comitatum istum reversus. Adrianus proximâ concione suggestum conscendit, disputatione publicâ se Pontificios errores confutaturum, Lutheri dogmata probaturum, edicit. Sed Monachis disputationē refugientibus Comes Jodocus per hunc Adrianū Missas, Vigilias, Invocationes sanctorū, & totum abominationum Pontificiarū chaos abolet, Adriano Ecclesiæ in oppido Hoya pastore declarato, Cyriaco Hesso ab Alberto Mansfeldico Comite ad se missō aulici concionatoris, M. Jodoco Crammio à Duce Luneburgico missō, urbici pastoris Neoburgii, officio demandato.
units.tr: The reformation of the churches of the County of Hoya also falls in this year. Count Jodocus began it, and his four sons, Albert, Eric, Otto and Frederick, the last Counts of that line, carried it on. In his deep sorrow Count Jodocus had read the books of Luther and Melanchthon, which his father-in-law, Count Wolfgang of Gleichen, had sent him, and he discussed them with his court preacher, chaplain and confessor, Konrad Drudeken, whom Duke Ernst of Lüneburg had sent from Wittenberg at his instigation. They asked for a learned man who could check the Terminarian friars and other mendicants. Luther sent Adrian Boxschoten of Antwerp, who had cast off his cowl at Antwerp and gone to Wittenberg, a man eloquent in Latin and pleasant in the Flemish tongue. With the Count's consent he entered the church at Neuenburg, the chief town of the very large county, and attacked a monk who was thundering against Luther from the pulpit: "I have been called by the illustrious Count of Hoya, Lord Jodocus, to prove you and your followers liars. So tell me, you perverse monk, before this whole congregation, where, when, and in what places Luther has erred." The monk fell silent, and slipped down from the pulpit and fled elsewhere, never returning to that county. At the next sermon Adrian mounted the pulpit and declared that he would publicly refute the Papist errors and prove Luther's doctrines in a public disputation. But when the monks refused the debate, Count Jodocus, through this Adrian, abolished the Masses, the vigils, the invocation of saints, and the whole chaos of papal abominations. Adrian was appointed minister of the church in the town of Hoya; Konrad Hess, court preacher sent by Count Albert of Mansfeld, and M. Jodocus Cramer, sent by the Duke of Lüneburg, were given the office of town minister of Neuenburg.

units.la: CELLAE in aula Ernesti Ducis Luneburgensis Evangelium hoc anno docebat Gotsaligus quidam, cui Lutherus epistolâ quâdâ gratulatur de conditione istâ, ac monet, ut pusillanimitatem conjugis Ernesti Margarethæ, sororis Electoris Friderici Saxonis ferat, dum illa verbum ferat & non persequatur.
units.tr: At Celle, in the court of Duke Ernst of Lüneburg, a certain Gottschalk taught the Gospel this year. Luther congratulates him in a letter on this post, and advises him to bear with the timidity of Ernst's wife Margaret, sister of the Elector Frederick of Saxony, while she bears the Word and does not persecute it.

units.la: MELTZAE (duobus ab Antuerpia milliaribus) quidam parochus fuit, qui sæpiús in patentibus locis & campis propter audientium multitudinem concionabatur, cumque illi sermo de Missa esset, nos quidem, inquit, sacrificuli, Iuda proditore summi deteriores. Is enim ChriChristum Dominum vendidit & tradidit. Nos vero eum vobis vendimus & non tradimus. Erat & Antuerpiæ & in finitimis locis hoc tempore magnus numerus hominum omnis generis, qui tum primùm aliquem verbi Dei gustum capiebant.
units.tr: At Meltz, two miles from Antwerp, there was a certain parish priest who often preached in open places and fields because of the crowds of hearers. When his sermon turned to the Mass, he said: "We little sacrificers are far worse than Judas the traitor. For he sold and handed over Christ the Lord. But we sell him to you and do not hand him over." At this time there was in Antwerp and the neighbouring places a great number of people of every kind, who were then for the first time tasting something of the Word of God.

units.la: In ditionem Iheverensem sincerioris doctrinæ facem intulit hoc anno primus, Henricus Cramerus Esensis, pastor in urbe Iheverana, multũ adiutus auctoritate Romeri Zedichii, Quæstoris & Cõsiliarii Iheverensis.
units.tr: In the lordship of Jever, the torch of purer doctrine was first kindled this year by Henry Cramer of Esens, pastor in the town of Jever, greatly aided by the authority of Romerus Zedichius, questor and councillor of Jever.

units.la: Annaebergae in Misnia Fridericus Myconius die Palmarum docere cœpit Evangelium. Die igitur passionis Domini ibidem excommunicatur, in monasterio Franciscanorum, Myconius publico scripto ad Rempublicam & cives Annæmontanos edito, Deo gratias egit, quod ex Ægyptiaca servitute liberatus sit: lætaturq;, quod Dominicâ Palmarum Christũ Hierosolymam ingredientem sit comitatus: hortatur deniq; Annæmontanos: ne metuant Papistas, & si Magistratus eos persequatur, quid facto opus sit, indicat.
units.tr: At Annaberg in Meissen, Friedrich Myconius began to teach the Gospel on Palm Sunday. On the day of the Lord's passion he was therefore excommunicated there, in the Franciscan monastery. Myconius, in a public writing addressed to the government and citizens of Annaberg, gave thanks to God that he had been freed from Egyptian servitude. He rejoiced that on Palm Sunday he had accompanied Christ entering Jerusalem. Finally he exhorts the people of Annaberg not to fear the Papists, and indicates what must be done if the magistrate persecutes them.

units.la: Cygnaeae in Misnia cœpit hoc anno ex audiri cœlestis tuba renascentis Evangelii, ex qua urbe ἐξ[illegible, ~3 letters] Fridericus Myconius ad Annæmontanos ea scripsit quorum modo mentio facta.
units.tr: At Zwickau in Meissen, this year the heavenly trumpet of the reborn Gospel began to be heard. From this town [ἐξ, illegible, about three letters] Friedrich Myconius wrote those things to the people of Annaberg which have just been mentioned.

units.la: Gotham vocatus Myconius, Cygnaeâ pulsus, ad gubernandas Ecclesias Thuringiacas annos 22. ibi docet.
units.tr: Called to Gotha, and driven out of Zwickau, Myconius teaches there for twenty-two years, governing the churches of Thuringia.

units.la: URATISLAVIÆ Doctor Joannes Heffus vigesimo die Aprilis theses ad disputandum propositi, quibus comprobaturum se promisit: Soli Deo esse inharendum. Missam non esse sacrificium, sed solum meritum Christi. Blasphemos esse in Deum, qui conjugio interdicant Sacerdotibus.
units.tr: At Breslau, Dr. Johann Hess, on the twentieth day of April, put forward theses for disputation, by which he promised to prove: "One must cling to God alone. The Mass is not a sacrifice but only the merit of Christ. Those who forbid priests to marry are blasphemers against God."

units.la: Disputavit in templo S.Dorotheæ ipsum octiduum, & interrogantibus quibusvis respondit.
units.tr: He disputed in the church of St. Dorothy for eight days in a row, and answered whatever anyone asked.

units.la: Lutherus ad Spalatinum: Vratislavia disputatio Joannis Hessi processit feliciter, frustra resistentibus tot legatis Regum & technis Episcopi.
units.tr: Luther to Spalatin: "The disputation of John Hess at Breslau has proceeded happily, although so many legates of kings and the tricks of the bishop have resisted in vain."

units.la: LIGNICII Silesiorum in templo S.Joannis coena Domini sub utraque specie exhibetur. Idem fit in altero urbis templo primario. Joannes VVerner aulæ concionator designatur.
units.tr: At Liegnitz, in the Silesian territory, the Lord's Supper is administered in both kinds in the church of St. John. The same is done in the other principal church of the town. Johann Werner is appointed court preacher.

units.la: NORIBERGÆ, cum Georgius Pesler ad S. Sebaldum, & Hector Pömer ad S.Laurentium Præpositi biennium & amplius Evangelium docuissent, & de abusibus Papisticis populum erudiissent, hoc anno abrogarunt Abusus missaticos. Missam pro defunctis. Cantum, Salve Regina &c. Salem & aquam consecratam.
units.tr: At Nuremberg, after Georg Pesler at St. Sebald's and Hector Pömer at St. Lawrence's, as provosts, had taught the Gospel for two years and more and instructed the people about Papist abuses, this year they abolished the abuses of the Mass: the Mass for the dead, the song "Salve Regina" and the like, and consecrated salt and water.

units.la: Matutinas & Completorias cantiones.
units.tr: The morning and evening (Matins and Compline) chants.

units.la: Et facti sui rationem ex sacra scriptura publico scripto divulgarunt 21. Octobris. Titulus scripti est: <bl>Grund vnd vrsach auß der heiligen schrift/wie vnd warumb</bl> <bl>beyder Pfarrkirchen zu Nürnberg Pröbste die mißbreuche bey der heiligen Meß/Jahrtag/geweihet saltz vnd wasser/same etlichen andern ceremonien abgestelt/ vnterlassen vnd geändert haben.</bl>
units.tr: And they made known the reasons for their action from Holy Scripture in a public writing, on 21 October. The title of the writing is: "The grounds and reasons from Holy Scripture, how and why the provosts of both parish churches of Nuremberg have abolished and altered the abuses at the holy Mass, the anniversary masses, the consecrated salt and water, and certain other ceremonies, and have left them off."

units.la: NOERDLINGAE, quae Imperii civitas est, Evangelium hoc anno purius annunciatur, verbi praecone Theobaldo Billicano.
units.tr: At Nördlingen, which is an imperial city, the Gospel is this year proclaimed more purely, the herald of the Word being Theobald Billican.

units.la: ARGENTINAE Magistratus ubi satis diu omnia spectasset, omnia considerasset: ubi animadvertit hominum, qui concionatores sequebantur, copiam, & in concionibus, frequentiam: cum sentiret mores civium emendari, & magis quam antea mitescere: cum pars etiam Senatus non minima doctrinam hanc amplecteretur: libertatem in omnibus suis templis Evangelii concessit: locum scholis apud Dominicanos dedit: stipendia decrevit: qui coenobia deserebant Monachi, iis jus civitatis dedit: uxores ducere concessit: qui in coenobiis reliqui erant, iis pecuniam annuam, dum viverent, constituit: facultates Ecclesiasticas coenobiorum Quaestoribus comisit: quae adhuc integrae conservatae, aut pauperibus, aut ministris Ecclesiae, pro multitudine& proportione,& functionib.distribuuntur.
units.tr: At Strasbourg the magistrate, after he had watched and considered everything for quite a long time, noticed the great number of people who followed the preachers, and the crowds at the sermons. Since he perceived that the morals of the citizens were being improved and were becoming milder than before, and since a not inconsiderable part of the Senate also embraced this doctrine, he granted freedom of the Gospel in all its churches. He gave a place for schools at the Dominicans' house, and decreed salaries. The monks who abandoned their monasteries were granted civic rights, and he allowed them to take wives. For those who remained in the monasteries he set an annual sum of money for as long as they lived. He entrusted the church property of the monasteries to the questors. What has been kept intact so far is distributed, according to number and proportion and duties, either to the poor or to the ministers of the Church.

units.la: Theologi Argentinenses fundamenta & causas suscepte à se mutationis rituum Missæ, seu cœnæ Domini,Baptismi,dierum festorū, imagnum, cantionum in publicis Ecclesiæ cōgressibus,ex sacris literis edito libro, quem Friderico Palatino dicârunt, exeunte anno 1524. expoluerunt: cui subscribunt VVolfgangus Capito,Caspar Hedio,Matthias Zellius,Symphorianus Pollio, Theobaldus Niger,Joannes Latomus, Antonius Firn,Martinus Hag, Martinus Bucerus. Iidem communi nomine commonent Pagos Helvetios: quàm impia sint paradoxa à Conrado Trægero ad disputandum proposita: in quibus Ecclesia scripturæ, hominum commenta verbo Dei præferantur.
units.tr: The Strasbourg theologians, in a book drawn from the sacred writings, which they dedicated to Frederick the Palatine, and which was published at the end of the year 1524, set out the grounds and causes of the changes they had undertaken in the rites of the Mass, or the Lord's Supper, of baptism, of feast days, of images, and of songs in the public assemblies of the Church. It is signed by Wolfgang Capito, Caspar Hedio, Matthias Zell, Symphorian Pollio, Theobald Niger, Johann Latomus, Anton Firn, Martin Hag, and Martin Bucer. The same men, in their common name, warn the Swiss villages how impious are the paradoxes which Konrad Treger has put forward for disputation, in which the teaching of the Church is preferred to Scripture and human inventions to the Word of God.

units.la: CASPAR HEDIO contrarias aliquot Theses Cunrado opponit: Bucerus ad paradoxa prolixè respondet. Capito virulentam commonitionem Cunradi ad Helvetios, superiori oppositam confutat. Omnes Cunradum ad disputandum in urbe Argentina provocant. Senatus contra vim omnem atq; pericula ipsi cavet. Sed Trægerus varia causatus,tandem,quod cupidè velit, id sibi facere per Episcopum non esse integrum, ait.
units.tr: Caspar Hedio sets several contrary theses against Konrad; Bucer answers the paradoxes at length; Capito refutes Konrad's virulent admonition to the Swiss, which was opposed to the earlier one. All of them challenge Konrad to a disputation in the city of Strasbourg. The Senate takes every precaution against violence and danger to him. But Treger, alleging various excuses, at last says that it is not within the bishop's power to grant him what he eagerly wants.

units.la: Tanta autem statim fama erat Theologorum,Argentinensium, Capitonis inprimis & Bucerij:ut Jacobus Faber Stapulensis & Gerardus Rufus clam è Gallia profecti,Capitonem & Bucerum audirent, & de omnibus doctrinæ præcipuis locis cum his dissererent, missi à Margaretha Francisci Regis sorore, Navarræ Reginâ. Atq; ita Evangelica vitis in Gallicis Ecclesiis aliquid etiam germinis ex urbe Argentina accepit. Cæterum multos cives Argentinenses in fide vera hoc anno confirmavit Doctoris Sebastiani Meieri Revocatio. Fuerat is ante hoc tempus Concionator ad Franciscanos Argentinæ, & Papista Papistice docuerat. Illuminatus autem spiritu, hoc anno ad inclytam Argentinensium Rempub. libellum typis descriptum mittit, quo retractatæ quæ docuerat.
units.tr: Such was at once the fame of the Strasbourg theologians, especially Capito and Bucer, that Jacques Lefèvre d'Étaples and Gérard Roussel, having secretly left France, went to hear Capito and Bucer and discussed all the chief points of doctrine with them. They were sent by Margaret, sister of King Francis and queen of Navarre. And so the Evangelical vine in the churches of France received something of a shoot from the city of Strasbourg. Moreover, the recantation of Dr. Sebastian Meyer confirmed many citizens of Strasbourg in the true faith this year. Before this time he had been a preacher to the Franciscans at Strasbourg and had taught in the Papist manner. But, enlightened by the Spirit, this year he sent to the renowned government of Strasbourg a printed booklet in which he retracted what he had taught.

units.la: 1. de Missa quod esset sacrificium, quo nos Deo aliquid offerimus. 2. de pœnitentia, quod tres eius partes, contritio, confessio, satisfactio. 3. De Papa: quod sit caput Ecclesiæ; interpretari scripturam ex suo ingenio possit: reservare sibi peccata possit quæ velit &c. &c. 4. De indulgentiis: quod septem, & plurium annorum pœnas in purgatorio sustinedas tollat. 5. De purgatorio, ad quod stabiliendum abusus sit scriptura dictis Matth. 5. & 18. & 12. & 1 Cor. 3. 6. De sanctis, quod invocandi: quod illorum intercessione à peccatis abstineamus; à morbis liberemur.
units.tr: 1. On the Mass, that it is a sacrifice in which we offer something to God. 2. On repentance, that its three parts are contrition, confession and satisfaction. 3. On the Pope, that he is the head of the Church; that he can interpret Scripture according to his own wit; that he can reserve to himself whatever sins he wishes, etc., etc. 4. On indulgences, that they remove the penalties of seven years and of many more years to be endured in purgatory. 5. On purgatory, for establishing which Scripture has been abused by the passages Matthew 5, 18 and 12, and 1 Corinthians 3. 6. On the saints, that they are to be invoked; that by their intercession we abstain from sins and are freed from diseases.

units.la: 7. De libero arbitrio, quod in hominis potestate sit, bona vel mala operari.
units.tr: 7. On free will, that it lies within man's power to do good or evil works.

units.la: 8. De bonis operibus, quòd sint meritoria vitæ æternæ, & quòd sit meritum congrui, digni, & condigni, ex lacunis scholasticorum.
units.tr: 8. On good works, that they are meritorious of eternal life, and that there is a merit of congruity, of worthiness and of condignity, drawn from the trifles of the schoolmen.

units.la: 9. De votis monasticis, quòd sint alter Baptismus, in quo de novo regeneretur homo, unde & nova nomina, velut in baptismo fieri solet, monachis & monialibus imponantur.
units.tr: 9. On monastic vows, that they are a second baptism, in which a man is born again anew, whence also new names, as is customary in baptism, are imposed on monks and nuns.

units.la: 10. De Ecclesiasticis: quòd jure divino non teneantur tributum & vectigalia solvere: nec à Magistratu politico possint capi, aut carceribus includi.
units.tr: 10. On ecclesiastics: that by divine right they are not bound to pay tribute and taxes, nor can they be seized by the civil magistrate or shut up in prisons.

units.la: Hæc omnia retractat, & ex verbo Dei convellit, nihil veritus voculas malevolorum & calumniatorum. Præfatio scripta est Bernæ Helvetiorum vr. Septembris huius anni.
units.tr: He retracts all these things and overturns them from the Word of God, caring nothing for the petty words of the malevolent and the calumniators. The preface was written at Bern in Helvetia on the fifth of September of this year.

units.la: BASILEAE Joannes Oecolampadius magno zelo, nec minore fructu in propagando Christi regno laborat, quem frustra Joannes Cochlæus, missis Stutgardiâ literis, amplissimis promissis à veritate agnita avocare conatur. Adiungunt se Oecolampadio M. V Volfgāgus V Veissenburgius, Marcus Bersius, Frater Joannes Luthardus, Frater Thomas Geiers falck, primi reformatæ doctrinæ apud Basilienses præcones. Hoc ægerrimè ferebant sacrificuli, ideoque detonabant in ipsos diris & maledictis, hæreticorum pessimorum pœnas eos commeritos esse clamitantes. Senatus igitur Basiliensis omnibus ditionis suæ concionatoribus mandat: ut loquia Dei, nō homihominum populo proponant, à convitiis & maledictis abstinent, edicti violatoribus severas poenas minatur.
units.tr: At Basel, John Oecolampadius labours with great zeal, and no less fruit, in propagating the kingdom of Christ. John Cochlaeus, by letters sent from Stuttgart, tries in vain to call him away from the truth he has recognised, with the most generous promises. Joining Oecolampadius are Master Wolfgang Weissenburgius, Marcus Bersius, Brother John Luthardus and Brother Thomas Geiersfalck, the first heralds of the reformed doctrine among the people of Basel. The little priests took this very badly, and so they thundered curses and maledictions against them, crying that they deserved the punishments of the worst heretics. Therefore the Senate of Basel commands all the preachers within its jurisdiction that they set before the people the Word of God, not the words of men, that they abstain from insults and curses, and it threatens severe penalties on violators of the edict.

units.la: Februario mense venit eò Guilielmus Farellus, ex Gallia profugus. Is contra traditiones humanas publicè disputaturus, à Vicario Episcopi, & Rectore Academiae impeditur. Senatus verò urbicus Farello, quod themata eius Evangelio viderentur conformia, liberam disputandi, aliis liberam opponendi facit potestatem: editum à Vicario & Rectore Academiae mandatum, quo & auscultatione & oppositione interdicebatur, in auctoritatis suae imminutionem accipit, contra decretum suum peccaturis usu molendinorum, furnorum, & mercatûs interdicit.
units.tr: In February Guillaume Farel came there, a fugitive from France. He was about to dispute publicly against human traditions, but was prevented by the Vicar of the Bishop and the Rector of the Academy. But the city Senate, because his theses seemed to conform to the Gospel, granted Farel free disputation and granted others the freedom to oppose him. The mandate issued by the Vicar and the Rector of the Academy, by which both listening and opposing were forbidden, it took as a diminution of its own authority, and it forbade those who would transgress its decree the use of mills, ovens and the market.

units.la: Erant autem articuli à Farello ad disputandum propositi, tredecim, quorum summa ista:
units.tr: The articles that Farel proposed for disputation were thirteen, of which the substance is this:

units.la: 1. A Christo perfectam vivendi regulam nobis prescriptam.
units.tr: 1. That a perfect rule of living has been prescribed to us by Christ.

units.la: 2. Matrimonium incontinentibus esse licitum.
units.tr: 2. That marriage is lawful for those who cannot contain.

units.la: 3. Discrimen ciborum, vestitûs, cremoniarum, esse Iudaicum.
units.tr: 3. That the distinction of foods, of clothing, and of tonsures is Jewish.

units.la: 4. Periculosas esse preces multorum verborum.
units.tr: 4. That prayers of many words are dangerous.

units.la: 5. Sacerdotum esse praedicare verbum Dei.
units.tr: 5. That it is the task of priests to preach the Word of God.

units.la: 6. Mandata Dei non esse in consilia convertenda,
units.tr: 6. That the commandments of God are not to be turned into counsels.

units.la: 7. Qui non liberè Evangelium docet, illum Christi pudere.
units.tr: 7. That he who does not teach the Gospel freely is ashamed of Christ.

units.la: 8. Qui non fide iustificari se credit, illum se-ipsum Deum facere.
units.tr: 8. He who believes that he is not justified by faith makes himself a god.

units.la: 9. Sacrificandum soli Deo.
units.tr: 9. Sacrifice is to be offered to God alone.

units.la: 10. Laborandum manu bene valentibus.
units.tr: 10. Those who are strong in body must labour with their hands.

units.la: 11. Ieiunia hypocritica & idola fugienda.
units.tr: 11. Hypocritical fasts and idols are to be shunned.

units.la: 12. Iudaicis ceremoniis renunciandum.
units.tr: 12. The Jewish ceremonies are to be renounced.

units.la: 13. Videndum, ut Christus nobis alluceat, sic omnia fore pacata.
units.tr: 13. Let it be seen that Christ shines upon us; thus all things will be settled in peace.

units.la: Disputatæ sunt hæ Theses in magna hominem frequentia 15. Februarii. Sed non multò post Vicarius Episcopi & Academiæ Rector vi & factione suâ Farellum Basileâ exegerunt.
units.tr: These theses were disputed on the fifteenth of February before a great crowd of people. But not long afterwards the Vicar of the Bishop and the Rector of the Academy, by force and by their faction, drove Farel out of Basel.

units.la: Hos Evangelicorum persequutores perstringit Oecolampadius epistolâ, quâ mense Junio huius anni Christophoro Episcopo Basiliensi inscriptam, suis in primam epistolam Johannis Demegoriis præfixit. Vindicat ibi Evangelicos à crimine seditionis, novitatis, contemptûs Patrum, & tandem nostrā, inquit, doctrinam innoxiā esse opinor, bonā partem plebis, quæ audit, testificaturam. Tantùm lupinos odere, qui inclamari timent, quò Christi oves vobis concreditas, impunè deglubant. Esto autem, quod illorum autoritatem confirment superciliosi quidā à Senatu Universitatis Basiliensis, qui publicis edictis, aliisq; machinationib. nobis in reb. piis negotium fecerunt impiè: eandem tamen quam illi, merentur fidem. Verus est enim syncretismus. Traducitur quippe & illorum inscitia tota orbe, quod Evan-
units.tr: Oecolampadius criticises these persecutors of the evangelicals in a letter, dated June of this year, addressed to Christopher, Bishop of Basel, which he prefixed to his own commentary on the First Epistle of John. There he vindicates the evangelicals from the charges of sedition, novelty and contempt for the Fathers, and at last: "I think our doctrine is harmless, and the better part of the common people who hear it will bear witness to this. Only the wolves hate it, who fear to be called out, lest they strip with impunity the sheep of Christ entrusted to you. Yet suppose that some supercilious men of the Senate of the University of Basel, who have done wickedly in pious matters by public edicts and other machinations against us, confirm their authority: they deserve the same credit as those men. For it is a true syncretism. Indeed their ignorance is spread throughout the whole world, that the Evan-

units.la: Oecolamp. lib. 4 epistolarum. Evangelium ne à limine quidem rectè salutârint, & feliciter neq; docuerint, neq; docere potuerint: cūq; de clave glorientur scientia, ipsi in regnũ scriptura nec intrêt, nec alios intrare sinât. Iam nemo est, qui non improbet in eis, quod ad reddendâ ratione fidei publicè semper terga verterint provocati. Nemo dignam Theologis crediderit excusationem, quâ Romana Sedis obedientiam pratexuerunt, contemptâ fratrum & plebis exspectatione.
units.tr: Oecolampadius, Letters, book 4. "They have not even greeted the Gospel properly from the threshold, nor have they taught it happily, nor could they teach it; and while they boast of the key of knowledge, they themselves do not enter into the kingdom of Scripture, nor do they allow others to enter. Now there is no one who does not disapprove of them, that when summoned they have always turned their backs on giving a public account of the faith. No one would think there was an excuse worthy of theologians, by which they pretended obedience to the Roman See, while despising the expectation of the brethren and the common people."

units.la: Consimilem, imò illustriorem Evangelicorum Apologiam idem Oecolampadius commentariis suis in Danielem præposuit.
units.tr: Oecolampadius prefixed a similar, indeed a more illustrious, apology for the evangelicals to his commentaries on Daniel.

units.la: LICHSTAL oppidum est ditionis Basiliensium. Evangelizabat in eo M. Stephanus Stoer, quem ob ductam uxorem alii ridebant, alii convitiis proscindebant.
units.tr: Liestal is a town in the jurisdiction of Basel. In it Master Stephen Stoer preached the Gospel; some laughed at him because he had taken a wife, others tore him apart with insults.

units.la: Auditores id ægrè ferentes, petunt à Senatu Basiliensi, pastori suo potestatem faciat, factum suum publicè in urbe Basiliensi ex Scripturis defendendi. Senatus annuit. M. Stephanus omnibus templis & monasteriis affigit hæc themata:
units.tr: The hearers, taking this badly, asked the Senate of Basel to give their minister the power to defend publicly, in the city of Basel and from the Scriptures, what he had done. The Senate agreed. Master Stephen posted these theses on all the churches and monasteries:

units.la: 1. Coniugium nulli hominum ordini in scriptura prohibitum est.
units.tr: 1. Marriage is prohibited to no order of men in Scripture.

units.la: 2. Adulterium & scortationem omnes leges omnium ordinum hominibus prohibent.
units.tr: 2. Adultery and fornication are forbidden to men of every order by all the laws of all orders.

units.la: 3. Vitanda libidinis & scortationis causâ extra matrimonium, coniugium omnibus hominibus mandatum est.
units.tr: 3. Marriage is commanded to all men, to be avoided for the sake of lust and fornication outside marriage.

units.la: 4. Scortatio nullum hominum ordinem minùs decet quàm Ecclesiasticum, idq; propter scandala.
units.tr: 4. Fornication becomes no order of men less than the ecclesiastical order, and that because of scandals.

units.la: 5. Publicus scortator secundum legem Dei verè est excommunicatus, & idcirco non idoneus ad munus sacerdotale.
units.tr: 5. A public fornicator is truly excommunicate according to the law of God, and therefore is not fit for the priestly office.

units.la: Dies disputationi dicta decimâ sextâ Februarii: confluit maxima hominum turba: surgit Stephanus, rationem reddit, cur uxorem duxerit: themata sua scripturæ dictis firmat: postremò, si quis vel ab Episcopo, vel à Capitulo, vel ab Academia, ad opponendum missus sit, obsecrat, ut se erroris ex scriptura convincat. Altum ibi silentium. Compellat igitur sacrificulos præsentes. His quoque tacentibus Oecolampadium rogat, suum super thematibus istis iudicium exponat. Is, se idem hactenus docuisse, affirmat. Idem se sentire Conradus Pellicanus, Professor Theologus, Hartmundus à Cronberg, Nobilis exul, M. Wolfgangus Weissenburgius, M. Bonifacius Wolffhartus, aliique profitentur. M. Stephanus, dissolutis erudite argumentis contra matrimonium Sacerdotum à M. Bonifacio ex mente Pontificiorum præpositis, magno cum honore ad Ecclesiam & uxorem suam rediit.
units.tr: The day appointed for the disputation was the sixteenth of February. A very great crowd of people gathered. Stephen rose, gave his reason why he had taken a wife, and confirmed his theses by the words of Scripture. Finally, he begged that if anyone, whether sent by the Bishop, the Chapter or the Academy, was there to oppose him, that person would convince him of error from Scripture. There was deep silence. He therefore addressed the little priests who were present. When they too kept silent, he asked Oecolampadius to set out his judgement on these theses. He affirmed that he had taught the same until now. Conrad Pellicanus, professor of theology, Hartmund von Cronberg, a noble exile, Master Wolfgang Weissenburgius, Master Boniface Wolfhart and others professed that they thought the same. Master Stephen, having dissolved with learned arguments the arguments against the marriage of priests, which Master Boniface had put forward in the manner of the Papists, returned with great honour to the Church and to his wife.

units.la: OECOLAMPADIUS qui hactenus vicariam operam Ecclesiæ Basilicnsi præstiterat, creaƈreatur Pastor, ad S. Martinum. Jubet igitur Diaconum infantes linguâ vernaculâ baptizare: Cœnam sacram utrâq; specie, assensu Senatûs, distribuit missaticum sacrificium: purgatorium, & id genus alias Pontificias traditiones pro concione ex scripturis sanctis refellit. Unde sensim Missa, circumcisiones exteraeq;. Papisticæ ceremoniæ corruerunt.
units.tr: Oecolampadius, who until now had performed the vicarious service for the Church of Basel, was made pastor at St. Martin's. He therefore ordered the deacon to baptise infants in the vernacular tongue. With the assent of the Senate he distributed the Lord's Supper in both kinds, and in sermons he refuted from the holy Scriptures the Mass, the sacrifice, purgatory and other such Papist traditions. Whence gradually the Mass, circumcisions and other Papist ceremonies collapsed.

units.la: Etsi igitur Capito & alii nonnulla purioris doctrinæ semina audientium animis aliquot annos ante iniecerant, Oecolampadius tamen iure primus Basiliensium Apostolus nominatur: cui in Ecclesiæ illius gubernatione ordine successerunt, Oswaldus Myconius, anno 1532. Simon Sulcerus, anno 1552. Joannes Jacobus Grynæus λόγῳ καὶ πράγματι Theologus, anno 1586. quem nos mense Maio proximo, ætatis annum septuagesimum septimum agentem, cupidè invisimus, cupidius vidimus, cupidissimè de variis iisq; ἀξιολόγοις rebus loquentem audivimus.
units.tr: Although Capito and others had some years earlier sown some seeds of purer doctrine in the minds of the hearers, Oecolampadius is rightly named the first apostle of the Basel people. In the governance of that Church he was succeeded in order by Oswald Myconius, in 1532; Simon Sulcer, in 1552; and John James Grynaeus, a theologian in word and deed [λόγῳ καὶ πράγματι], in 1586. In May of the coming year, when he was in his seventy-seventh year, we eagerly visited him, more eagerly saw him, and most eagerly heard him speaking of various notable [ἀξιολόγοις] matters.

units.la: TIGURINI cum quinquennii à Zwinglio fuissent informati, visum est Magistratui reformationem aggredi. Hoc igitur anno mense Junio processiones inhibitæ, è præcipuis urbis templis tumbæ Martyrum sublatæ: idola in urbe, & quàm latè patet ditio ipsorum, ablata, & flammis abolita. Catharina de Cimmern Abbatissa, tradito dito
units.tr: The Zurich citizens, having been instructed by Zwingli for five years, decided that the magistrates should take up reform. So this year, in June, processions were forbidden, the tombs of the martyrs were removed from the principal churches of the city, and the idols were taken away from the city and from every part of their territory as far as it extends, and burned.

units.la: Strumpfius lib. 6. dito cœnobio in manus Consulis, viro nupsit, honestis reditibus annuis à Magistratu dotata. In hoc cœnobio aluntur nūc & instituuntur à fido præceptore aliquot adolescētes:
units.tr: Strumpfius, book 6. Catharina von Cimmern, the abbess, handed the convent over into the hands of the burgomaster and married a man, endowed by the magistrate with an honourable annual income. In this convent some young men are now supported and taught by a faithful tutor.

units.la: Vicesimâ Decembris Præpositura quoque reformatur, è cuius bonis Pastores, Professores, Ludimagistri modò aluntur.
units.tr: On 20 December the provostry was also reformed, and from its revenues ministers, professors and schoolmasters are now supported.

units.la: Zwinglius secundâ Aprilis huius anniu-xorem duxit: Annam Reinhartam, viduam nobilis viri, Joannis Maieri.
units.tr: Zwingli married on 2 April of this year: Anna Reinhart, widow of a nobleman, Johann Meyer.

units.la: CONSTANTIÆ ad locum Bodamicum Joannes Zwiccius evangelizat. Ambrosius Blaurerus parænesin Germanicam ad Senatū urbicum scribit. Hunc ad concionandum VVolffgangus Capito hortatur: Parænesin, inquit, tuam mirabundus legi. Quod si ad verbū dicendū te demitteres, quid præstares, obsecro? Neque est quod iures, seu parum suffecturus causeris. Sub tali provincia nemo vocatus deficiet, cū divinitus adiuvetur. Gaudeo deniq; ausuros vos innovare foris, qua verbo in cordibus piorū instaurata nostis. Nā evanescit Spiritus, si, qua asseverat, cessas re præstare, etiamsi cunctatione tuâ magnū argumentū præbes incomparabilis tuæ prudētiæ. Nobis tamen hîc multa præter spem, præter consilia acciderunt: profuit, inquam, à Matthia Zellio præsertim totā sententiā abominationis Pontificiæ motam, me invscio. Nam posteaquā rescire exploratus auditorū animis, facilè animadverti, eò loci nos redactos, ut necesse esset, aut progredi fortiter, quāvis exitum
units.tr: At Constance, on the Lake of Constance, Johannes Zwick preaches the Gospel. Ambrosius Blaurer writes a German exhortation to the city council. Wolfgang Capito urges him to preach: "I read your exhortation with wonder. But if you were to put yourself forward to preach the word, what would you achieve, I beg you? Nor is there any reason for you to swear that you would be unequal to it. In such a charge no one who is called will fail, since he is helped by God. I rejoice, finally, that you will dare to renew outwardly what you know has been restored by the word in the hearts of the pious. For the Spirit evaporates if you delay in doing what you assert; even though by your hesitation you give a great proof of your incomparable prudence. Yet here many things have happened beyond hope and beyond plans for us: it helped, I say, that the matter was stirred up, against my will, especially by Matthias Zell, who was wholly moved by the detestation of Papist abomination. For afterwards, when I had learned from the explorers of the hearers' minds, I easily perceived that we had been brought to such a point that we must either advance boldly, though we could not foresee the outcome, or else draw back, not without discouraging the pious, who grow cold and are being killed, once they have sensed that their leaders are faltering. Go on, then, with good omens and with Christ as your guide. For without God present, nothing you attempt will succeed."

units.la: {a} Witeb. exitum prævidere non potuimus, aut referre gradum non sine deiectione piorum, qui frigent, qui enecantur, ubi nos duces languere senserint. Perge igitur bonis avibus & auspice Christo. Sine Deo enim præsente nihil moliri continget.
units.tr: {a} Witeb. We could not foresee the outcome, or else draw back without discouraging the pious, who grow cold and are being killed, once they have sensed that their leaders are faltering. Go on, then, with good omens and with Christ as your guide. For without God present, nothing you attempt will succeed.

units.la: SCAPHUSIANI qui anno superiori disputationi Tigurinæ interfuerant, cum domum reversi Abbati & reliquis Canonicis indicassent, ex omnibus præsentibus neminem unum fuisse, qui sacræ scripturæ locis, & idoneis argumentis, themata Zwinglii refellere posset: & Abbatem & Erasmum Ritterum ad oppugnandum Evangelium è Bavaria vocatum, ita immutârunt, ut, quod antea oderant Evangelium, amarent, & de Ecclesiæ reformatione serio deliberarent. Oecolampadius de reformationis modo consulitur: Senatus, ut auctoritatem suam interponat, rogatur: Abbas & reliqui monachi monasterio egrediuntur, abiiciunt cucullos, ducunt uxores, privatas instituunt familias, decimas, & omnes Ecclesiæ reditus Magistratûs potestati & administrationi committunt hac conditione, ut vitæ necessaria ad vitæ dies suppeditentur. Idem fecit Abbatissa cum torotibus suis, ordinem relinquunt, Magistratui omnia tradunt, ducunt viros, fiunt verè matres, quæ ante sic dicebātur. Inter has fuit nobilis virgo, postea mater optimi & doctissimi viri Joannis Conradi Cochii qui hodieque Scaphusianos pane vitæ cœlestis cibat. Erasmus, qui prius Evangelii doctrinam oppugnaverat, Evangelium nunc magno zelo propugnat, cui collegæ adiunguntur doctissimi viri VVolffgangus Biderman Rotvilanus, M. Beatus Gerinus Tigurinus, Benedictus Burgoverus Sangallensis. Imagines, picturæ, ornatus Papisticus, altaria ad tempus fuêre relicta. Consultius enim visum ista prius ex animis, quàm oculis hominum tollere.
units.tr: The Schaffhausen men who had attended the Zurich disputation the year before, when they returned home and reported to the abbot and the other canons that among all those present there was not a single man able to refute Zwingli's theses from passages of Holy Scripture and with suitable arguments, so changed the abbot and Erasmus Ritter (who had been summoned from Bavaria to attack the Gospel) that they began to love the Gospel, which before they had hated, and to deliberate seriously about the reform of the Church. Oecolampadius was consulted about the manner of reform; the Council was asked to add its authority. The abbot and the other monks left the monastery, cast off their cowls, took wives, set up private households, and committed the tithes and all the revenues of the Church to the power and administration of the magistrate, on condition that what was necessary for life should be supplied for the rest of their days. The abbess did the same with her nuns: they left their order, handed everything over to the magistrate, took husbands, and became truly mothers, which before they had been called only in name. Among these was a noblewoman, later the mother of the excellent and most learned man Johann Konrad Koch, who even today feeds the Schaffhausen people with the bread of heavenly life. Erasmus, who had earlier attacked the doctrine of the Gospel, now defends the Gospel with great zeal. To him are joined colleagues, the most learned men Wolfgang Bidermann of Rottweil, Master Beat Gerin of Zurich, and Benedikt Burgauer of St Gall. Images, paintings and Papist ornaments, and the altars, were for a time left in place, since it seemed wiser to remove these first from men's hearts rather than from their eyes.

units.la: SANGALLENSIBUS veritatem cœlestem demonstrat Joannes Kesler VVittembergâ domum reversus, & VVolffgangus Ulmian, nuper monachus Curiensis. Eosdem in veritate ista mirè confirmant Leo Judæ Tigurinus, & Sebastian Hoffmeister Scaphusianus Ecclesiastes, qui illac transeuntes rogatu civium sunt concionati. Non ita multò post de voluntate Senatus per certos homines statuæ noctu sine turba sunt ablatæ. Quæ præterea in commodum pauperum, & Ecclesiæ decorem ordinata sunt, de iis legere licet librum Joannis Kesleri de ritibus & institutis Ecclesiæ Sangallensis.
units.tr: Johannes Kessler, who returned home from Wittenberg, and Wolfgang Ulmian, lately a monk of Chur, proclaim heavenly truth to the people of St Gall. Leo Jud of Zurich and Sebastian Hoffmeister, the Schaffhausen minister, who passed that way and at the request of the citizens preached, strongly confirm them in this truth. Not long afterwards, by the will of the Council, the statues were removed at night, by certain men, without a crowd. As for the other arrangements made for the benefit of the poor and the adornment of the Church, one may read about them in the book of Johannes Kessler, On the rites and institutions of the Church of St Gall.

units.la: In MONTE BELLICARDI Guilielmus Farellus vineam Domini plantat, Basileâ exactus. Fuit hic Farellus zeli in promovendo Evangelii vehementissimi. Erasmus in epistolis Phallicum nominat, & scribit, sæpe ab OecoOecolampadio, etiam literis, sæpe à Pellicano etiam fuisse obiurgatā illius vehementiam. Et ita est. Oecolampadius enim tertiâ Augusti literis exaratis ad Farellū, revocat illi in memoriam monita Basiliensia: deinde hortatur illum, ut Christum etiam vita exprimat, exemplo videlicet docendi. Rursum decimâ nonâ Augusti huius anni aliis literis ad moderationem hominem revocat, in quibus legantur ista: Evangelizatum non maledictum missus es: laudo Zelum, modò ne desideretur mansuetudo. Vinum & oleum in tempore suo infundendum. Evangelistam non tyrannicum legislatorem præstes.
units.tr: At Montbéliard, William Farel, expelled from Basel, plants the Lord's vineyard. This Farel was most vehement in his zeal for advancing the Gospel. Erasmus, in his letters, calls him "Phallicus," and writes that his vehemence was often rebuked by Oecolampadius, even in letters, and often by Pellicanus. And so it was. For on 3 August Oecolampadius, in a letter written to Farel, recalls to him the admonitions of Basel; then he urges him to express Christ also in his life, that is, by the example of his teaching. Again, on 19 August of this year, in another letter he calls the man back to moderation, in which these words are read: You were sent to evangelize, not to curse: I praise zeal, provided gentleness is not lacking. Wine and oil must be poured in at their proper time. Be an evangelist, not a tyrannical lawgiver.

units.la: WALDSHUTUM oppidum est Austriaci dominii ad Rhenum. In eo Balthasar Pacimontanus fructuosè hactenus Evangelium docuerat. Cives igitur aliqui Tigurinorum exemplum imitaturi cogitabant & ipsi de reformatione: quibus alii refragabantur. Ferdinandus Austrius civibus mandat, quieti sint, nihil innovent: ni pareant, dira minatur. Tigurini cives nonnulli suo in oppidum adventu animos Waldshutensium recreant. Sed statim domum revocantur, vel quòd Balthasar Anabaptistica deliria spargeret, quod scribit Zwinglius: vel quòd Senatus Tigurinus à Ferdinandicis Lucernę violatæ confœderationis hæreditariæ esset accusatus, quam causam Bullingerus adfert. Quàquam utrùq; fieri potuit.
units.tr: Waldshut is a town of the Austrian dominion on the Rhine. There Balthasar Pacimontanus had hitherto taught the Gospel with good fruit. Some citizens, intending to imitate the example of the Zurich people, were thinking of reform themselves, and others opposed them. Archduke Ferdinand of Austria orders the citizens to keep quiet and to innovate nothing; unless they obey, he threatens dire consequences. Some citizens of Zurich, by their coming to the town, revive the spirits of the people of Waldshut. But they were soon called home, either because Balthasar was spreading Anabaptist delusions, as Zwingli writes, or because the Zurich Council had been accused by Ferdinand's men at Lucerne of violating the hereditary alliance, which is the reason Bullinger gives. Yet either could have been the case.

units.la: Erasmus scribit ad Henricum Stromerum: Tigurinos omnes divos eiecisse è templis, VVals-hutenses etiam è vitreis fenestris privatarum ae-dium.
units.tr: Erasmus writes to Henry Stromer: "The Zurich people have cast out all the saints from the churches, and the people of Waldshut even from the glass windows of private houses."

units.la: CÆTERUM hoc anno UBIQUITAS in Gallia nata, BELLUM SACRAMENTARIUM in Germania ortum est.
units.tr: MOREOVER, in this year UBIQUITY was born in Gaul, and the SACRAMENTARIAN WAR arose in Germany.

units.la: Nativitas UBIQUITATIS ita habet. A Berengarii inde tempore usq; & ulterius multò ultra quingentos annos præsentia corporalis corporis Christi in cœna, tribus tanquàm columnis fundata est: 1. falsà interpretatione τούτου 2. transsubstantiatione per virtutem magicam verborum. 3. duplicitate corporis Christi, visibilis & invisibilis. Joannes Gerson Academiæ Parisiensis Cancellarius, intelligens, futilia hæc esse omnia, sub tempora Concilii Constantiensis realem communicationem naturarum primus omniū dogmaticè introduxit. Docuit enim Christū, quatenus creatura est, nō posse corpore suo uno & eodem tempore in plurib. & diuersis locis esse, à divina tamen natura, in unam personā cum ipso unitam humanā naturam accipere hanc prærogativā, & hanc ei communicari, ut in cœna saltem sua & in hac quidem tantùm & sola) simul esset in pluribus, omnib. nimirum cœnæ suæ locis. Quæ proprie non est παντοχρονία, sed πλυπληία. Hoc autem anno M. D. XXIV. Jacobus Faber ber Stapulensis, quam Gerson ex unione personali realem idiomatum communicationem in omnibus cœnæ locis sibi finxit, eam pari ratione & eâdem operâ in omnia mundi loca introduci posse iudicavit, & sic Ubiquitatem Parisiis in Sorbona primus asseruit, & accusante quodam Natali Beda postero anno M. D. XXV. à Sorbona propter hoc dogma Ubiquitatis, & realis idiomatū communicationis è Gallia relegatus exulavit apud Margaretha Navarrenam. Hæc est celebris illa Ubiquitas, quam è Gallia relegatam Lutherus in Ecclesias Germaniæ reduxit (in Sole etiam & in pane tabernæ pistoriæ corpus Christi esse docens) Brentius excoluit, Jacobus Smidelinus multis etiam invitis obtrusit, unde Apostoli Ubiquitatis cognomen meruit.
units.tr: The birth of Ubiquity goes like this. From the time of Berengar onward, and for much more than five hundred years afterwards, the bodily presence of Christ's body in the supper was founded on three pillars: (1) on a false interpretation of τούτου [touto]; (2) on transubstantiation through the magical power of the words; (3) on a twofold body of Christ, visible and invisible. Jean Gerson, Chancellor of the University of Paris, recognising that all these things were trifling, was the first of all to introduce dogmatically, around the time of the Council of Constance, the real communication of natures. For he taught that Christ, insofar as he is a creature, cannot be in several and different places at one and the same time with his body; yet from the divine nature, the human nature united with him in one person receives this prerogative, and it is communicated to it, so that in his supper, at least, and in that alone and only, he would be present in several places, namely in all the places of his supper. This is properly not omnipresence [παντοχρονία] but multilocality [πλυπληία]. In this year 1524, however, Jacques Lefèvre d'Étaples judged that what Gerson had invented, from the personal union, as a real communication of properties in all the places of the supper, could by the same reasoning and the same effort be introduced into all places of the world. Thus he was the first to assert Ubiquity at Paris in the Sorbonne. In the following year, 1525, he was accused by Noël Béda, and, because of this dogma of Ubiquity and the real communication of properties, was expelled from the Sorbonne and from France and went into exile with Margaret of Navarre. This is that famous Ubiquity which Luther, after its expulsion from France, brought back into the churches of Germany (teaching that the body of Christ is even in the sun and in the bread of the bakery shop); Brenz cultivated it, Jakob Schmidlin forced it upon many even against their will, and for this reason he earned the nickname "Apostle of Ubiquity."

units.la: SACRAMENTARIAM causam An- dreas Bodenstein, Sacramentarium bellum Martinus Lutherus primus commovit. ANDREAS BODENSTEINIUS, Carolostadius extra Helvetiam in superiore Germania & ditione Septemvirali Saxoniæ, cum Archidiaconus adhuc esset VVittembergæ, offendi se sermonibus quibusdam Lutheri de Eucharistia, ostendit, illis potissimū, quib. dicebatur Christus in pane sacro Cœnę esse tantus, quātus in cruce pependisset. Ac tum primū abalienari nonnihil animi inter ipsos cœperunt. P 2
units.tr: The Sacramentarian cause: Andreas Bodenstein, and Martin Luther who first stirred up the Sacramentarian war. Andreas Bodenstein, called Carlstadt, a man of upper Germany and of the Electoral Saxon lands, not of Switzerland, was still archdeacon at Wittenberg when he took offence at certain sermons of Luther on the Eucharist, especially those in which Christ was said to be in the sacred bread of the Supper as large as he hung on the cross. It was then for the first time that some estrangement of minds began between them.

units.la: Cum autem <bl>οἰκονομαχία</bl> ipsius à Luthero improbata esset, indignè ille id ferens, hoc 24. anno VVittebergam reliquit, ita ut simultatem sibi cum VVittebergensibus esse fateretur, & præ se tamen ferret studium de dubiis suis cum Luthero aliisq; differendi, seque, si scrupuli sibi eximerentur, cum iis denuo coniugendi. Recepit autem se Orlamundam, quod Thuringiæ oppidum est, per Ecclesiam loci illius legitimè vocatus ad Pastoratû, ubi Iconomachiâ suâ novas dedisse turbas iudicabatur. Revocatus ab Academia VVittebergam ad ordinariû munus obeundû in schola & Ecclesia, stitit se, promisitq; de reditu, si Orlamundani assentirentur. Rebus autem ad Salam Thuringiæ in peius ruentibus, decreto Electorio Lutherus primùm Jenam, deinde Orlamundam venit.
units.tr: Since his oikonomachia [οἰκονομαχία] was disapproved by Luther, Carlstadt took it badly and left Wittenberg in this year 1524. He admitted that there was a quarrel between him and the Wittenbergers, yet he professed a desire to discuss his doubts with Luther and others, and said that if his scruples were removed he would join them again. He withdrew to Orlamünde, a town in Thuringia, where he had been lawfully called to the ministry by the church of that place, and where his iconoclasm was judged to have caused new disturbances. Recalled from the university at Wittenberg to resume his ordinary duties in the school and the church, he presented himself and promised to return if the people of Orlamünde agreed. But when affairs at Saale in Thuringia grew worse, Luther, by the Elector's decree, first went to Jena and then to Orlamünde.

units.la: JENÆ xxii Augusti horâ septimâ matutinâ concionatur Lutherus contra fanaticû Spiritum Munceri. Eiusdem spiritûs ait esse οἰκονομάχας & Sacramentarios. Interest concioni Carolostadius: pûgi se arbitratur, quippe qui primus quædâ notasset & reprehendisset, quæ Lutherus de cœna sacra docuisset. A concione igitur Lutherum convenit in hospitio, cui insignè niger ursus; ibi post multos nõ gravissimos inter ipsos sermones habitos, Lutherus datâ arrhâ ad scribendû publicè contra se de sacra cœna Carolostadiû proprovocat, & belli sacramentarii, quod, pro dolor, adhuc durat, imprudenter initium facit. Narratio Germanica de cōgressu Lutheri & Carolostadii Tom. 2. Germanico operum Lutheri Jenensiū inserta est: quam etsi mendaciis mixtam cum veritate scribit Lutherus: tamen non negat se pactum fuisse cum Carolostadio: de cœna sacra disputare. Sed affirmat id etiam alibi. Quin imò gloriatur: se Prophetas illos, qui dudum mussitârint, aureo nummo ad pugnam elicuisse, cuius facti necdum se pœnitcat.
units.tr: At Jena, on 22 August, at seven in the morning, Luther preached against the fanatical spirit of Müntzer. He says that the oikonomachai [οἰκονομάχαι] and the Sacramentarians belong to the same spirit. Carlstadt attended the sermon; he thought himself struck, since he had been the first to note and criticise certain things Luther had taught about the Lord's Supper.
