units.la: M. Francisco Ænobarbo primo praeconi Evangelico Gorlicensiû successerunt ordine in Ecclesiae gubernatione: M. Nicolaus Zeidlerus, Wolffgangus Suftelius, M. Leonhartus N. Sprottaviensis. M. Joannes Petzsteinius, M. Othmarus Epplinus. M. Caspar Wirtwein. Samuel Janchius, Balthasar Theodorus, M. Elias Theodorus, Martinus Mollerus, Gregorius Richterus, vir literato orbi de editione Axiomatum Oeconomicorum, Politicorum, Ecclesiasticorum, notissimus.
units.tr: After Master Franciscus Ænobarbus, the first evangelical herald of Görlitz, the following men succeeded in order in the government of the church: Master Nicolaus Zeidler, Wolfgang Suftelius, Master Leonhard N. of Sprottau, Master Johann Petzstein, Master Othmar Epplin, Master Caspar Wirtwein, Samuel Janchius, Balthasar Theodorus, Master Elias Theodorus, Martin Moller, and Gregor Richter, a man well known to the learned world for his edition of the Axioms of Economics, Politics and Ecclesiastics.

units.la: RHETI in his temporum & certaminu de religione difficultatib. imitati vicinarum aliquot urbium in Helvetia exemplu, superioribus annis mandârat & ipsi Sacerdotib. suis, ut miso Thoma, Scoto, Aristotele, & omnibus hominum commentis ea tantummodo docerent populum, quae sacris literis essent consona. Hoc mandato animati, quos tyrannidis Pontificię metus hactenus cōtinuerat, Evangelium liberè profitentur, breviq; tempore ita crevit illorum numerus: ut hoc anno cum Joanne Comandro(Dorffman)Curiensi Pastore ad S.Martinū, recenserentur 41. Doctorum Evangelicorum in Rhetia. Non ferendum sibi hoc esse arbitrati sunt Abbas S. Lucii, & Decanus cum Capitulo Curiensi. In conventu igitur ante festum natalis Christi diem Curiae celebrato Ordines Rhetorum confoederatos adeunt, Joannem Comandrum, eiusdemq; in professione Evangelii socios haereseos graviter accusant: ut qui, Sacramenta convellant:
units.tr: In Rhaetia, in these times of difficulty and conflict over religion, imitating the example of some neighbouring cities in Switzerland, the authorities had in previous years ordered their own priests to set aside Thomas, Scotus, Aristotle and all human inventions, and to teach the people only what agreed with the sacred letters. Encouraged by this command, men whom fear of papal tyranny had until then restrained now openly profess the Gospel, and their number grew so quickly that this year forty-one evangelical teachers in Rhaetia were counted, including John Comander (Dorffman), pastor at St Martin's in Chur. The Abbot of St Luzi and the Dean with the Chapter of Chur judged this intolerable. So at an assembly held at Chur before Christmas, they approached the confederated Orders of the Rhaetians and sharply accused Johann Comander and his fellow professors of the Gospel of heresy, as men who overturn the sacraments:

units.la: Missam contemnant:
units.tr: despise the Mass:

units.la: Scripturam sanctam miserè discerpant:
units.tr: tear the holy Scripture to pieces wretchedly:

units.la: Ceremonias Ecclesiæ, ieiunia, confessionem auricularem, sacrificia, & id genus alia nullo loco habeant.
units.tr: hold the ceremonies of the Church, fasts, auricular confession, sacrifices and other things of that kind as nothing.

units.la: Atq; ut hæreticos istos functionib. suis moveant, enixè petunt. Ordines Joannem Comandatū ad se vocant, accusationis capita illi proponunt: ad ea ut respondeat, mandant. Comander respondet: se fratresq; suos mandato Ordinum de solo Dei verbo prædicando obsequutos, semperq; paratos fuisse, quibusvis volentib. rationem doctrinæ suæ reddere: stare se & nunc coram Ordinibus suo & quadraginta fratrum nomine, & per Deum, per iudicium supremum, per pacem deniq;, veritatem & concordiam rogare, Ordines accusationi fidem ut ne habeat, sed Christiano colloquio diem destinet, & de rei summâ parte utrâq; audita pronuncient. Placuit hoc Ordinib. confœderatis. Dies Dominica, quæ Epiphania proximè sequitur, disputationi dicta, de qua anno sequente agemus.
units.tr: And to remove these heretics from their office, they earnestly petitioned the Orders. The Orders summoned Johann Comander, set the heads of the accusation before him, and ordered him to answer them. Comander replied that he and his brothers had obeyed the Orders' command to preach only the Word of God, and had always been ready to give an account of their teaching to anyone who wished to hear it. He now stood before the Orders in his own name and that of forty brothers, and begged them, by God, by the last judgment, and finally by peace, truth and concord, not to give credence to the accusation, but to appoint a day for a Christian colloquy, and after hearing both sides on the substance of the matter, to pronounce judgment. The confederated Orders agreed to this. The Sunday immediately after the Epiphany was set for the disputation, of which we shall speak next year.

units.la: HANOVIÆ Comitatui syncerioris religionis lucem intulit PHILIPPUS Reinhardi VII. ex Catharina Schwartzenburgica filius: quem Carolus V. Imperator & superiori & hoc anno à pio reformandæ Ecclesiæ propósito per certos homines frustra est dehortatus. Primum Evangelii
units.tr: At Hanover, PHILIP, son of Reinhard VII by Catherine of Schwarzenburg, brought the light of the purer religion to the county. Emperor Charles V, both in the previous year and this year, tried in vain to dissuade him through certain men from his pious purpose of reforming the Church. The first herald of the Gospel

units.la: Annales Hanovici M. S. præconem aluit Hanovia M. Adolphum Arbogastum, Argentinâ à Capitone & Bucero sibi submissum: cui paulò post laborū socius adiunctus est Philippus Enneobolus Laudenburgo ab Illustri Comite Philippo Hannoviâ vocatus: qui M. Adolpho fidum sanè in Euangelii propagatione collegam, & adversus Evangelicę doctrinę tum ibidem adhuc subsistentes hostes animosum ἀντιλογίαν, quà concionando quà conscribendis etiā Theologicis tractatibus (ut Catechesis huius approbat) se præbuit: in eoq; maximè elaborvit, ut Pastores huiusce Comitatûs, & doctiores quoscunq; alios ad Evangelii agnitionem ac professionem pertraheret.
units.tr: (the Hanover Annals, manuscript) Hanover nourished as its first herald of the Gospel Master Adolph Arbogast, sent to him from Strasbourg by Capito and Bucer. Shortly afterwards Philip Enneobolus of Laudenburg was joined to him as fellow labourer; the illustrious Count Philip had called him to Hanover. He proved a thoroughly faithful colleague to Master Adolph in spreading the Gospel, and a spirited antilogia [ἀντιλογίαν] against the enemies of evangelical doctrine who still remained there, both in preaching and in writing theological treatises, as his Catechism shows. He laboured especially to draw the ministers of this county, and any other learned men, to acknowledge and profess the Gospel.

units.la: ALTENBURGICO in Comitatu antiquissimo Christophorus & Antonius Comites Altenburgici & Delmenhorstani lectione scriptorū Lutheri, & locorum communium Philippi Melāchthonis, cantilenis item Germanicorum Psalmorū à Luthero vulgatorū plurimùm oblectati, hoc anno initium secerunt emendationis Ecclesiarū in Phrisia Butiada, Pastoribus primis M. Edone Bolingo in Esensham: Edone Jolrico in Rodenkirchen: Joanne Hechlero in Twischenan, & Hermanno Crispino in Edewech Ammerlandię: repugnantibus conatui laudatissimo tum matre Comitum Dominâ Annâ, viduâ, tum fratribus natu maioribus Joanne & Georgio. CON-
units.tr: In the ancient county of Altenburg, Christopher and Anthony, Counts of Altenburg and Delmenhorst, greatly delighted by reading Luther's writings and Philip Melanchthon's Loci communes, and likewise by the German Psalm songs published by Luther, this year made a beginning of reforming the churches in Butjadingen in Friesland. The first pastors were Edo Bolingius at Esens, Edo Jolricus at Rodenkirchen, Johann Hechler at Twischen, and Hermann Crispinus at Edewecht in Ammerland. Opposing this most praiseworthy endeavour were their mother, the widowed Lady Anna, and the elder brothers Johann and Georg. CON-

units.la: CONRADUS Comes TECKLENBURGICUS & Lingensis, Dominus Redensis de consilio Philippi Hessorum Principis, affinis sui hoc ipso anno inter Westphaliae Comites primus Evangelium amplexus est, usus in reformatione Ecclesiarum operâ Joannis Pollii, poëtae tum celebris, & ab Eobano Hesso commendati.
units.tr: CONRAD, Count of Tecklenburg and Lingen, Lord of Rheda, on the advice of Philip, Landgrave of Hesse, his kinsman by marriage, this same year became the first of the Westphalian counts to embrace the Gospel. In reforming the churches he used the work of Johannes Pollio, then a celebrated poet, who was recommended by Eobanus Hessus.

units.la: In Domino Esensi regnabat Balthasar Nobilis Dominus in Esens & Witmūdae, qui licet puriori doctrinae esset addictus, propter hostes tamen, à quibus infestabatur, Ecclesias suas reformare non ausus est. Hoc vero anno M. Joannes Visbeckius Pastor in Burhave (qui ad Septennium studuerat Wittembergae) Richardus Hicko Pastor in Dunum, & Mammo Folckhardus Pastor in Ardorp, mutuis se cohortationibus ad aggrediendam reformationem incenderunt, quodque felicitér exorsi sunt, id Enno Comes Orientalis Frisiae Domini Balthasaris ditionem invadens, perque eam totam Ecclesias renovari curans, absolvit.
units.tr: In the lordship of Esens, Balthasar, a nobleman and lord of Esens and Witmund, was ruling. Although he was devoted to the purer doctrine, he did not dare to reform his churches because of the enemies who troubled him. This same year M. Johannes Visbeck, minister at Burhave (who had studied for seven years at Wittenberg), Richard Hicko, minister at Dunum, and Mammo Folckhard, minister at Ardorp, encouraged one another with mutual exhortations to undertake the reformation. What they had begun successfully was completed by Count Enno of East Friesland, who invaded Balthasar's territory and took care to renew the churches throughout it.

units.la: NORTHUSÆ Thuringorum Blasius Michaël consulem agebat & Pharmacopolam. Ad hunc mittebatur quicquid primis πολιγενειας Ecclesiae annis Lutherus scribebat. Cives in pharmacopolio frequentes convenire, libellos Lutheri legere, de iis inter se conferre, & agnitis erroribus Papatus emendātionem Ecclesiæ suæ optare. Non defuit optatis Magistratus, sed Laurentium Suffium, monasterii Augustiniani ibidem Priorem ad docendum Evangelium vocat, eiq; Ecclesiam Petrinam commendat.
units.tr: At Northusa in Thuringia, Blasius Michael was serving as consul and apothecary. To his shop was sent whatever Luther wrote in the first years of the regeneration [πολιγενεσίας] of the Church. Citizens gathered in large numbers at the apothecary's shop, read Luther's little books, discussed them among themselves, and, recognising the errors of the Papacy, wished for the reformation of their own church. The magistrate did not fail in these wishes, but summoned Laurentius Suffius, prior of the Augustinian monastery there, to teach the Gospel, and commended the church of St. Peter to him.

units.la: HAGANOÆ in Alsatia VVolffgangus Fabritius Capito Argentinâ evocatus confortat fratres in Evangelica doctrina, & Dominicâ Palmarum cœnam sacram secundum Christi institutionem civibus suis distribuit: (erat enim Haganoënsis) idem ipso die Paschati sacro in maxima hominum, rem novâ videre cupientium, frequentia, sine sale, sine oleo, sine aliis ceremoniis Papisticis, horâ 3. pomeridianâ baptizat VVendelini Rihelii filiolum Josiam, cui pater consultò hoc nomen indi voluit in memoriam beneficii divini: quòd, sicut regnante Josia liber legis inventus, & secundum illum sincerus Dei cultus restitutus est: ita nascente Josia filiolo suo liber Biblicus in Papatu quodammodo amissus, iterum repertus, & vera salutis doctrina Germaniæ restituta sit.
units.tr: At Hagenau in Alsace, Wolfgang Fabricius Capito, called from Strasbourg, strengthened the brothers in evangelical doctrine, and on Palm Sunday he distributed the Lord's Supper to his fellow citizens according to Christ's institution (for he was of Hagenau). On the same day, the holy day of Easter, in the greatest crowd of people eager to see a new thing, he baptised at three in the afternoon the little daughter of Wendelin Rihel, Josia, without salt, without oil, and without other Papist ceremonies. The father had deliberately wished her to be given this name in memory of the divine benefit: just as under King Josiah the book of the law was found and, according to it, the pure worship of God was restored, so with the birth of his little daughter Josia the Biblical book, which in some sense had been lost under the Papacy, was found again, and the true doctrine of salvation was restored to Germany.

units.la: Hæc igitur loca sunt, quæ religio orthodoxa hoc anno occupavit. Eadem religio in aliis locis, quæ proximis superioribus annis illustravit, incrementa minimè contënenda sumpsit.
units.tr: These, then, are the places which the orthodox religion occupied this year. In other places, which it had illuminated in the preceding years, the same religion, by no means, took on any increase.

units.la: ALBERTUS Marchio Brandeburgicus relicto ordine creatur primus Dux Prussiæ à Sigismundo Rege Poloniæ, & Ducatum illum hæredi-
units.tr: ALBERTUS, Margrave of Brandenburg, having left the Order, was created the first Duke of Prussia by Sigismund, King of Poland, and receives that duchy as a hered-

units.la: Ex Autographo Wendelini Rihelii descriptum.
units.tr: Copied from the autograph of Wendelin Rihel.

units.la: Funccius. hæreditarium accipit, qui antea ad fratres Ordinis Teutonici pertinebat: ita is, qui antea erat Magister Ordinis, iam salutatur Dux Prussiæ. Hic Albertus cum è Silesia in Borussiam reversus, & summâ omnium ordinū lætitiâ esset exceptus, convocatæ Nobilitati & civitatibus universis, in hoc pacis negotio à se toto triennio Acta, diligenter ac ordine perscripta, prælegi mandavit. Cui, finitâ recitatione, gratias solennes, nomine totius provinciæ, Georgius à Polentz, Episcopus Sambiensis egit: ac è vestigio Episcopæ seu dioecesis suæ universæ politicam administrationem, cum omni Nobilitate, oppidis, & terris sibi subditis, prolixâ oratione Principi resignat, quod Episcopo Ecclesiæ Evangelion, non politica imperia & regna huius mundi, sed ministerium docendi Evangelii, & necessaria vitæ alimenta, tantum tribueret. Princeps toto provincialium coetu teste vocato, quod se non petente aut sollicitante, Episcopus sponte ac liberrimo arbitrio, de Episcopā ipsi cederet, lætus eam accepit: altero Episcopo Erardo Pomesaniensi tacito astante, qui usque ad vitæ exitum gubernationem suam retinuit. Tam felices autem fuerunt vineæ Domini plantatores in Borussia, qui illuc à Luthero fuerant missi: ut intra triennium omne fere doctrinæ Papisticæ lolium extirpârint. Polonorum Regem audiamus testem:
units.tr: Funccius. itary possession, which previously belonged to the brothers of the Teutonic Order. Thus he who had previously been Master of the Order is now greeted as Duke of Prussia. When Albert returned from Silesia to Prussia and was received with the greatest joy of all the orders, he commanded that the Acts, which had been carefully and orderly recorded by him throughout the three years of this peace business, be read aloud to the assembled nobility and all the cities. When the reading was finished, George von Polentz, Bishop of Samland, gave solemn thanks in the name of the whole province, and at once, in a lengthy speech, resigned to the Prince the entire political administration of his bishopric or diocese, together with all the nobility, towns and lands subject to him, because the Church's bishop had granted to him not political empires and kingdoms of this world, but only the ministry of teaching the Gospel and the necessities of life. The Prince, with the whole assembly of the provincials called as witnesses, that the bishop of his own accord and by his most free choice, without any request or solicitation on his part, yielded the bishopric to him, received it gladly, with the other bishop, Erhard of Pomesania, standing by in silence, who kept his government until the end of his life. The vine-dressers of the Lord who had been sent there from Luther were so successful in Prussia that within three years they had almost entirely uprooted all the Papist tares of doctrine. Let us hear the King of Poland as witness:

units.la: Hic deest aliquid? Textus lineae ultimae in pagina plene legibilis.
units.tr: Is something missing here? The text of the last line on the page is fully legible.

units.la: Sigismundus primus Ioanni Dantisco, apud Romanum Pontificem Oratori.
units.tr: Sigismund I, to Johannes Dantiscus, envoy at the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: Cùm inducia cum Mugistro Prussia exspira-rent, ageretq; cùm Summus Pontifex tum Cæsarea Maiestas, Serenissimusq; Dominus Rex Hungaria, nepos noster apud nos de induciis prorogan-dis: ad quas subditi nostri nequaquam consentire voluerunt, iudicantes, eas bello fore nocibiliores; proindeq; nos ad prosequendam rem nostram armis instituere mus: venit ad nos id sentiens ipse Magister cum Illustribus Marchione Georgio, & Friderico Duce Lignicensi, transegitq; nobiscũ coram de tota controversia, præstito nobis debito suo, & datis illi per nos in feudum terris, quas prius ante libellum novissimum possedit. De reli-gione verò nihil inter nos est actum: tum quia interesse nostra non videbatur: tum quòd etiam Ordinis institutores non fuerimus: tum verò quòd ferè in tota ditione Ordinus prorsus de tota religione Catholica sit actum & deploratum. Proindeq; abusi sumus ea conditione depravati temporis in rem pacis, cum res aliter transigi nullo pacto potuit. Proinde si qui isthic hos actus nostros in re Prutenica suggillare vellent, habes quo innocen-tiam nostram tueri possis. Nam nos Ordinis curatores non sumus, sed hæreditarium ius no-strũ duntaxat semper exegimus. Religio Catholica nobis semper cordi fuit: pro qua nequaquam dubi-tamus vel sanguinē nostrũ profundere: tantũ abest, ut illi nostra opera vel consensu quicquam esset per hanc transactionem detractum. Anno 1525.
units.tr: When the truce with the Master of Prussia was expiring, and when both the Supreme Pontiff and the Imperial Majesty, and the Most Serene Lord, the King of Hungary, our nephew, were pressing us about prolonging the truce, which our subjects were by no means willing to agree to, judging that it would be more harmful than war, we therefore resolved to pursue our cause by arms. The Master himself, perceiving this, came to us with the illustrious Margrave George and Frederick, Duke of Liegnitz, and negotiated with us in person about the whole controversy, having rendered to us his due homage and having received from us, as a fief, the lands which he held before the recent pamphlet. About religion, however, nothing was settled between us, both because it did not seem to concern us, and because we were not the founders of the Order, and especially because almost throughout the whole dominion of the Order the entire Catholic religion had been wholly abandoned and given up. We were therefore compelled, in that corrupt age, to make a settlement for the sake of peace, since the matter could in no way be concluded otherwise. Therefore, if any there wish to censure these our acts in the Prussian affair, you have a means by which you can defend our innocence. For we are not guardians of the Order, but have always only claimed our hereditary right. The Catholic religion has always been dear to us, for which we have no doubt to shed even our blood; so far was it from being the case that anything was taken away from it by this agreement through our work or consent. In the year 1525.

units.la: Prutenico isto Evangelii successu Lutherus animosior factus, Albertum Cardinalem, & Archiepiscopum Moguntinum literis hortatur: ut exemplum hoc sequatur: uxorem ducat: de benedictione divina certissima quaeque sibi polliceatur: Deinde Georgio à Polentis Episcopo Sambiensi Deuteronomium à se explicatum dedicat: in qua dedicatione memorabilia haec eloquitur: Non te laudamus, cum dona Dei in te tollimus, sed insigne illud miraculum gratiae Dei extollimus, quam in te valere, regnare, & triumphare videmus & audimus cum gaudio. Ut quemadmodum pastor, sicut Amos loquitur, eruit ex ore lupi extremum auriculae aut duo crura, sic te unicum & solum inter omnes Episcopos orbis elegerit Dominus, & liberaverit ex ore Satanae, quod dilatavit sicut infernum, & devorat omnes. Nihil enim videmus in caeteris Episcopis (quamquam esse inter eos sperem aliquot Nicodemos) nisi quod subversis Caesare ac Regibus & Principibus fremunt & insaniunt contra resurgens vel potius oriens Evangelion, & denuo impleant illud Psalmi secundi: Adstiterunt Reges terrae, & Principes convenerunt in unum adversus Dominum & adversus Christum ejus. Quo provocant simul, ut & Deus in eis impleat quod sequitur: Habitator caeli ridebit, & Dominus subsannat eos. Tunc loquetur ad eos in ira sua & in furore suo conturbabit eos. Tibi vero ea singularis plane & mirabilis gratia donata est, ut non modo verbum suscipe-res & crederes, sed pro Episcopali autoritate etiam palam & publice confessus doceres, docerique per tuam dicecesin curares, liberaliter his, qui in verbo laborant, provisis, videntibus impijs, irascentibus ac dentibus suis frementibus, & tabescentibus frustra. Hac scilicet gratia Dei in te collata, quemadmodum Paulus cum Macedonibus facit ad Corinth. non fuit mihi silentio transeunda, sed omnibus modis evulganda, predicanda, cantanda, ad gloriam Dei, ad profectum Evangelij, ad incrementum fidei, ad solatium infirmorum, & eorum, qui apud nos varia patiuntur in variis locis, ad erectionem pusillorum, denique etiam ad terrorem & ignominiam hostium verbi, & idolorum istorum in loco Pontificum sedentium, qui preter tyrannidem nihil sciunt, neque possunt in misero populo prestare. Nec sum veritus, quod hac predicatione onerem te odio & invidia caeterorum Pontificum, Regum & Principum, aut etiam in periculum vitae trahàm, quandoquidem hodie nullum flagitium par est huic uni & summo sacrilegio, scilicet Evangelion Dei confiteri, ob quod jam multi sanguinem fuderunt constantissimè, inter quos imprimis lucent Henricus & Ioannes Brussella per sophistas Lovanienses exusti, & post eos Henricus noster Sutphanius Bremensis Evangelista, non uno igne, nec uno genere mortis per Diethmarianas bestias occisus. Quid nos maneat, Deus novit: si tamen digni fuerimus, ut socij illorum facti, & ipsi patiamur contumelias ob nomen Domini. Non, inquam, huic periculo te exponere sam veritus, certissimè persuasus, quod is, qui te honoravit verbo crucis, simul roborabit etiã spiritu crucis, triumphabit, in carne tua, non modò blasphemias nominis & odia & furores potentium in mundo, sed etiam vires & violentiam (si opus fuerit eas ferre) Satana cum toto suo regno; scimus enim, quod major est is, qui in nobis est, quàm is, qui in mundo est. Ad hac, ut gratia & donum hoc Dei cumulatius esset, addidit Dominus, & curavit benignitate suâ, ut Principem terra haberes Evangelio studiosissimum, heroëm illum inclytum Adelbertũ ex Marchionibus Brandeburgensibus, Magistrum magnum Prussia, cui donatum est eodem spiritu ut cogitet, quae Principe digna sunt, ut verbis Prophetae utar, ita fit ut utriusque vestrum praesidio Christianissimo populus Prussiae qui fortè nunquam Evangelion habuit, nisi opertum vel adulteratũ, nunc latè currens & fructificans audiat clarissimum & purissimum, inenarrabili beneficio Dei. Nam ego puto: Evangelion ad Germaniam usque ad hoc seculum nunquam pervenisse revelatum, & luce suâ coruscum: licet non dubitem, Dominum semper novisse suos ubique terrarum, etiam in medijs Sodomis & Gomorrhis servare. Et vide mirabilia: ad Prussiam pleno cursu plenisque velis currit Evangelion, quò non vocabatur, ubi nec quarebatur. batur, in Germania vero superiore & inferiore, quò ultra venit & accessit, omni furore & insaniâ blasphematur, repellitur, fugatur, ut in hoc impleri videas sortem illam egregiam Evangelij, de - qua Paulus dicit Roman. 10. Inventus sum à non quaerentibus, palàm apparui his, qui me non interrogabant. De Israel verò dicit: Tota die expandi manus meas ad populum incredulum, & dicentem mihi, qui ambulat vias non bonas.
units.tr: Encouraged by this success of the Gospel in Prussia, Luther, becoming bolder, exhorts by letter Albert, Cardinal and Archbishop of Mainz, to follow this example: to take a wife, and promises himself the most certain divine blessing. Then he dedicates to George von Polentz, Bishop of Samland, his exposition of Deuteronomy, in which dedication he speaks these memorable words: We do not praise you when we lift up the gifts of God in you, but we extol that remarkable miracle of the grace of God, which we see and hear with joy to prevail, reign and triumph in you. As the shepherd, as Amos says, rescues from the mouth of the lion the tip of an ear or two legs, so the Lord has chosen you alone among all the bishops of the world and has delivered you from the mouth of Satan, which has widened like hell and devours all. For we see nothing in the other bishops (though I hope there are some Nicodemuses among them) except that, with Caesar and the kings and princes overthrown, they rage and go mad against the Gospel rising again, or rather dawning, and they fulfil again that verse of the second Psalm: The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ. By this they simultaneously provoke God to fulfil in them what follows: He who dwells in heaven will laugh, and the Lord will mock them. Then he will speak to them in his wrath and trouble them in his fury. But to you has been given a singularly clear and wonderful grace, so that you not only received and believed the word, but also, with episcopal authority, openly and publicly confessed it, taught, and took care that it be taught throughout your diocese, generously providing for those who labour in the word, while the impious look on, angry, gnashing their teeth and wasting away in vain. This grace of God bestowed on you, just as Paul does with the Macedonians in Corinthians, was not to be passed over by me in silence, but was to be published in every way, preached and sung, to the glory of God, to the advancement of the Gospel, to the increase of faith, to the comfort of the weak and of those who among us suffer various things in various places, to the raising up of the little ones, and finally also to the terror and shame of the enemies of the Word and of those idols sitting in the place of the Pontiffs, who know nothing but tyranny and cannot provide anything for the wretched people. Nor have I feared that by this preaching I might burden you with the hatred and envy of the other Pontiffs, kings and princes, or even draw you into danger of life, since today no crime is equal to this one and supreme sacrilege, namely, to confess the Gospel of God, for which many have already shed their blood most steadfastly, among whom especially shine Henry and John Brussels, burned by the sophists of Louvain, and after them our Henry Sutphanius of Bremen, an evangelist, killed not by one fire nor by one kind of death by the beasts of Dithmarschen. What awaits us God knows, if indeed we shall be found worthy to become companions of them and ourselves suffer insults for the name of the Lord. I say that I have not feared to expose you to this danger, being most certainly persuaded that he who has honoured you with the word of the cross will at the same time strengthen you with the spirit of the cross, and will triumph in your flesh not only over the blasphemies against his name, the hatreds and furies of the powerful in the world, but also over the powers and violence of Satan with his whole kingdom (if it be necessary to bear them); for we know that greater is he who is in us than he who is in the world. Besides, that this grace and gift of God might be more abundant, the Lord added and took care, in his kindness, that you should have as prince of the land a most zealous supporter of the Gospel, that famous hero Albert of the Brandenburg margraves, Grand Master of Prussia, to whom it has been given by the same Spirit to think what is worthy of a prince, so that, to use the words of the Prophet, by the most Christian protection of you both the people of Prussia, who perhaps never had the Gospel except hidden or adulterated, may now hear it most clearly and most purely, spreading widely and bearing fruit, by the inexpressible benefit of God. For I think that the Gospel, revealed and shining with its light, had never reached Germany until this age, although I do not doubt that the Lord has always known his own everywhere on earth, and preserves them even in the midst of Sodoms and Gomorrahs. And see the wonders: the Gospel runs to Prussia with full course and full sails, to a place where it was not called, where it was not sought; but in Upper and Lower Germany, where it came and approached, it is blasphemed, repelled and put to flight with all fury and madness, so that in this you may see fulfilled that outstanding lot of the Gospel of which Paul speaks in Romans 10: I was found by those who did not seek me; I appeared openly to those who did not ask for me. But of Israel he says: All day long I have stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.

units.la: Hæc de Ducali Borussia. Regiæ Borussiæ urbs primaria Dantiscum Doctorem Bugenhagium Ecclesiæ VVittembergensis Pastorem vocat per legatum ad Ecclesiæ suæ instaurationem. Lutherus quid de hac vocatione senserit, epistola ipsius ad Georgium Spalatinum docet. Sic autem illa: Venit ad Principem hic D. Iohannes, Pastor unus Dantiscensis populi, postulaturus favorem Principis pro vocando illuc Pomerano nostro. Rogo itaq; ut illi adsis, sicut poteris. Quamvis enim eum virum hic manere velim, tamen in re tanta & causa verbi cedendum arbitror. Quis scit, quid Deus velit ibi per ipsum operari, ne forte tam insignem vocationem Dei non intelligamus, & impediamus: audies mira ex ipso, quae in Dantisco operatus est Christus. Ego sic vocatus non auderem reniti, sed irem statim.
units.tr: So much for Ducal Prussia. The chief city of Royal Prussia, Danzig, sent a messenger to summon Doctor Bugenhagen, pastor of the Church at Wittenberg, to restore its church. Luther's letter to George Spalatin shows what he thought of this call. It reads: Doctor John here, one of the pastors of the Danzig people, has come to the Prince to ask for his favour in calling our Pomeranian there. I ask you therefore to stand by him as far as you can. For although I would like this man to stay here, nevertheless in so great a matter and a cause of the Word I think we must yield. Who knows what God wishes to accomplish there through him? Let us not fail to recognise and hinder so remarkable a calling of God. You will hear wonderful things from him about what Christ has done in Danzig. If I were called in this way I would not dare to resist, but would go at once.

units.la: NORIMBERGÆ mense Martio die Cunigundæ in curia præsente Senatu & multis civibus colloquium inter Evangelicos Ecclesiæ ministros, quorum dux erat Andreas Osiander ander, Pastor ad S. Laurentium, & quatuor concionatores Papisticos in totidem monasteriis reliquos, institutum est: cuius hic exitus fuit, ut conciones & ceremoniæ monasteriorum deinceps intermittentur, & omnes sacerdotes, & Monachi cives fieri, & onera civium, instar cæterorum, subire cogerentur.
units.tr: At Nuremberg, in March, on the day of St Cunigunde, a colloquy was arranged in the town hall, in the presence of the Senate and many citizens, between the evangelical ministers of the Church, led by Andreas Osiander, pastor of St Lawrence, and four Papist preachers from the four monasteries. The outcome was that the sermons and ceremonies of the monasteries were thenceforth suspended, and all the priests and monks were compelled to become citizens and to bear civic burdens like the rest.

units.la: FRANCOFURTUM ad Mœnum ab Archiepisco Moguntino mittebatur Theodoricus quidam Ursellanus, qui sub larva Lutheranici concionatoris Papismum debebat defendere contra Ibachium, præconem Evangelii. Olfecit hoc Dionysius Melander Monachus Franciscanus, & hoc anno publicè ipsi, eiusq; successori Joanni Schallio contradixit. Melandro coniunxit se Joannes Bernhardi ab Algesheim, monachus Dominicanus. Utrerque Papatum fortiter impugnavit. Ortâ in urbe seditione paulò ante Pascha cives Missam & omnes abusus Pontificios tolli volunt. Senatus igitur Melandrum & Joannem ordinarios Evangelii Doctores renuntiat, & Pontificiis edicit: si patrocinio suo salvi esse velint, ut horum concionatorum contra missaticũ sacrificium doctrinam ex Dei verbo consutent. Quod cum illi non possent, multùm licet confirmatiâ Moguntino; templa S. Bartholomæi, Leonardi, & Mariæ Montis Evangelicis cessêre.
units.tr: From the Archbishop of Mainz, Theodoric of Ursel was sent to Frankfurt on the Main. He was to defend Papism under the mask of a Lutheran preacher against Ibach, the herald of the gospel. Dionysius Melander, a Franciscan friar, smelled this out, and this year he openly opposed both Ibach and his successor John Schall. John Bernhardi of Algesheim, a Dominican friar, joined Melander, and both attacked the papacy vigorously. Shortly before Easter, a riot broke out in the city, and the citizens wanted the Mass and all Papist abuses abolished. The Senate therefore appointed Melander and John as the regular teachers of the gospel, and told the Papists that if they wished to be safe under its protection, they should refute the teaching of these preachers against the sacrifice of the Mass from the Word of God. When they could not do this, the churches of St Bartholomew, St Leonard and Our Lady on the Hill yielded to the evangelicals, although the Archbishop of Mainz strongly backed them.

units.la: Uratislaviae nobilissimum templum ad D. Elisabetham à fermento Pontificio repurgatur, idq; ministerio Ambrosii Moibani. Fuit hic Ambrosius patriâ Uratislaviensis, qui cùm in omni disciplinarum genere esset exercitatus, Viennae artium Magister, VVittembergae Theologiae Doctor creatus est, carus Luthero, Melanchthoni, Camerario, aliis. Munus docendi Ecclesiam Elisabethanam subiit aetatis anno trigesimo primo. A Jacobo Episcopo Uratislaviensi, cui se stitit, haec audiit verba: Ito, & doceto Evangelium Domini nostri Iesu Christi in nomine patris, filij & spiritus sancti.
units.tr: At Breslau the noble church of St Elizabeth was purged of Papist leaven, through the ministry of Ambrosius Moibanus. This Ambrosius was a native of Breslau. He was trained in every branch of learning, was made Master of Arts at Vienna and Doctor of Theology at Wittenberg, and was dear to Luther, Melanchthon, Camerarius and others. He took up the office of teaching at St Elizabeth's in his thirty-first year. The bishop of Breslau, Jacob, before whom he presented himself, said these words to him: Go, and teach the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Hessus igitur & Moibamus primi erant Uratislaviensium Evangelistae, qui magnâ dexteritate & prudentiâ abusus Pontificios populo detegebant: ad obedientiam erga superiores subditos, ad vitae innocentiam singulos invitabant: idq; tanto cum fructu, ut sine ullo tumultu cultus imaginum, processiones, vigiliae, Anniversariae, Fraternitates, peregrinationes ad sanctos, leges de cibis vetitis, de monachis, monialibus, & id genus alia Papatus <bl>βδελύγματα</bl> uno quasi labefactata motu corruerent, & paulò post Evangelium in novem templis, quorum septem extra, duo intra urbis moenia sita, praedicaretur. Moibamus decimo quinto Maii, Hessus octavâ Septembris, uxorem duxit.
units.tr: Hess and Moibanus were therefore the first evangelists of Breslau. With great skill and prudence they exposed the abuses of the Papists to the people, and they urged each person to obedience toward superiors and to innocence of life. They did this with such success that, without any tumult, the worship of images, processions, vigils, anniversary masses, fraternities, pilgrimages to the saints, the laws about forbidden foods, about monks and nuns, and other such abominations [βδελύγματα] of the papacy fell as if shaken by a single movement. Soon afterwards the gospel was preached in nine churches, seven outside and two within the city walls. Moibanus married on 15 May, and Hess on 8 September.

units.la: Uratislaviensium exemplum urbes & oppida alia pleraq; in Silefia sequuta sunt. Multū juvit propagationem verę doctrinę in Silefia, prudentia & moderatio clarorum Episcoporū, Jacobi à Salꞔza, qui anno 1522. electus, & Balthasaris à Promnitz, qui Jacobo anno 1539. demortuo successit. Uterque enim à persecquutione Evangelicorum abhorruit. Etsi autem ex jure Canonico notum est, qualem vel in clericos suos, vel in laicos etiam in causis vel spiritualibus vel civilibus, habuerint potestatem Episcopus, Suffraganeus, Propositi, Decani, Archidiaconi, Scholastici, Cantores, &c. Silentio tamen hoc non est prætermittendum: reformatione Religionis factâ, euiusq; ἀνπνομία sive libertate concessâ, Ecclesiasticam jurisdictionem contra Augustanæ confessioni addictorum religionem, fidem, ritus & ceremonias suspensam, juraq; Episcopalia ad Principes territoriorū & Status tanquâ fiduciarios possessores translata esse ac deposita, adeo quidem, ut ipsi etiam clerici iis tanquam Magistratui ordinario subiecti sint, nec aliorum jurisdictione constringantur & obligentur. Quæ quidem Ecclesiasticæ potestatis iura, ut pro statu Ecclesiæ optimo administrent & gubernent, duobus ferè mediis utuntur; quæ ordinis sunt; per superintendentes, qui censuræ morum, & exercendæ disciplinæ præsunt, totiusque Ecclesiasticæ cutaxiæ eutaxiæ curā gerunt; quæ verò sunt legis diœcesanæ, & jurisdictionis in foro Ecclesiastico, per Consistoria exsequentes. Interim Episcopus, Abbates, & Prælati suam religionem, ceremonias, possessiones, vectigalia & jura libera fere hucusque retinent: neque quò minùs illis pacatè uti frui possint, ullâ ratione impediuntur, si paucas Ecclesiasticas Præfecturas, & quædam id genus alia bona sacra excipias, quæ Principes ac civitates nonnullæ sibi sumpserunt, eaque in ministerii, scholarum, egenorum, & similes pios atq; utiles usus converterunt.
units.tr: Many other towns and market-places in Silesia followed the example of Breslau. The spread of true doctrine in Silesia was greatly helped by the prudence and moderation of the distinguished bishops Jacob von Salza, elected in 1522, and Balthasar von Promnitz, who succeeded Jacob on his death in 1539. Both shrank from persecuting the evangelicals. Although it is known from canon law what power the bishop, suffragan, provosts, deans, archdeacons, scholastics, cantors and others had over their clergy, or over laymen, in both spiritual and civil matters, this must not pass in silence: once the reformation of religion was carried out and liberty [αὐτονομία] granted, ecclesiastical jurisdiction was suspended against the religion, faith, rites and ceremonies of those who adhered to the Augsburg Confession. The episcopal rights were transferred to and lodged with the princes of the territories and the estates, as trustees who held them. So much so that even the clergy themselves are subject to these as the ordinary magistrate, and are not bound or constrained by the jurisdiction of others. To administer and govern these rights of ecclesiastical power for the best condition of the Church, they use mainly two means. The first concerns good order: superintendents, who oversee the censure of morals and the exercise of discipline, and take care of the whole good order of the Church. The second concerns diocesan law and jurisdiction in the ecclesiastical court, which is carried out by consistories. Meanwhile the bishops, abbots and prelates have kept almost to this day their own religion, ceremonies, possessions, revenues and free rights. Nor are they hindered in any way from enjoying and using these peacefully, except for a few ecclesiastical offices and similar sacred goods which some princes and cities have taken for themselves and turned to the pious and useful purposes of the ministry, the schools, the poor and the like.

units.la: ARGENTINÆ Sigismundus Comes Hoënloius, Decanus Ecclesiæ collegiatæ Argentinensis edito scripto Germanico clerum suum graviter hortatur ad lectionem scripturarum, & vitam clericis dignam: profitetur, nihil sibi æquè in votis esse, ac hoc, ut Ecclesia illa celebris, totusq; Clerus reformetur, & verus Dei cultus restituatur.
units.tr: At Strasbourg, Sigismund, Count of Hohenlohe, dean of the collegiate church of Strasbourg, published a writing in German and earnestly urged his clergy to read the Scriptures and to live a life worthy of clergy. He declared that nothing was dearer to his wishes than that this famous church, and the whole clergy, should be reformed and the true worship of God restored.

units.la: TIGURI ut anno superiori Idola remota, ita hoc anno Missa fuit abrogata. Historiam ex Zwinglio ipso audire placet. Cum ad undecimam diem Aprilis coram senatu Diacoforum, is est senatorum ducentorum, de abolendis, Missa & panis ac vini adoratione, ageremus: & ibi Scriba quidam (qui albus an ater sit, non est huius instituti dicere) forte surrexisset, atque ad hunc modum quiritaretur; Equidem Patres tres conscripti, nō eo sum ordine aut loco, ut mihi coram vobis verba facere liceat, dummodò causa ageretur quantumvis magna, quae ad Rempublicam attineret: cùm autem hic animarum salutis cardo vertatur, ipsaq́ fides periclitetur, cujusq́ esse arbitror, ut in medium adducat quae sentiat? Ego igitur firmiter credens in isto pane verum corpus, ac verū sanguinem edi, testor, me in hac esse opinione, neq́ me patiar ab ea divelli, speroq́ de vobis, Patresq́ conscripti, quod nullo pacto sitis me ad Zwinglij opinionem adacturi. Et tu Zwingli, inquit, sophistarum versutis acerrimè obstitisti, nunc verò, ut plane dicam quod sentio, videris nos denuo sophistarum cavillis circumscribere. Multa denique alia, quae ad hanc rem facerent, quaestus esset, ut illi videbatur sciitè ac graviter. Cumq́ nos ad ea, quae responsione digna videbantur, puta, Tiguri nemine unquam ad fidem fuisse compulsum, neq́ ad ullam rem: neq́ sophisticum esse, si hanc vocem EST, per SIGNIFICAT quisquam exponat (hoc enim sophisticum esse dixerat) cùm inquam respondissemus ad ea, quae roboris aliquid habere videbantur: isteq́ jam ad haec arma se converteret: Ego sic credo, sic sanant verba: hoc est corpus meum: EST est verbum substantivum, ideo alius intellectus esse nequit, quàm quòd panis sit caro & similia, quae carnis cupidi objectant. Tum Henricus Engelhardus, olim Pontificij juris Doctor, nunc verò pauperis Christi discipulus, vir gravi judicio, auscultā, inquit, paulisper: ego abunde ostendam tibi ex sacris
units.tr: At Zurich, as the idols had been removed the year before, so this year the Mass was abolished. It is pleasant to hear the account from Zwingli himself. When on 11 April we were debating before the Senate of the Diacoforum, that is the Council of Two Hundred, the abolition of the Mass and the adoration of bread and wine, a certain scribe (whether he was white or black is no concern of this account) happened to stand up and complained in this way: Indeed, conscript Fathers, I do not hold a rank or place that allows me to speak before you, provided the matter under discussion is however great and concerns the Commonwealth. But since the hinge of the salvation of souls turns on this, and the faith itself is in danger, I think it is the duty of everyone to bring forward what he thinks. I therefore, firmly believing that in this bread the true body and the true blood are eaten, declare that I hold this opinion and will not allow myself to be torn from it. And I hope about you, conscript Fathers, that you will by no means drive me to the opinion of Zwingli. And you, Zwingli, he said, have most strongly resisted the cunning of the sophists; but now, to speak plainly what I think, you seem to be once again entangling us in the sophists' quibbles. Many other things, which would have helped the case, were said at length, as they seemed to him skilfully and gravely put. When we answered those points which seemed to deserve a reply, namely that at Zurich no one had ever been compelled to faith or to anything else, and that it is not a sophism if anyone explains this word IS as SIGNIFIES (for he had said this was a sophism), when, I say, we had answered what seemed to have some weight, he turned to these arms: I believe thus, thus the words heal: this is my body. IS is a substantive verb, so it cannot have any other sense than that the bread is flesh and the like, as those who love the flesh object. Then Henry Engelhard, once a doctor of Papal law, now a disciple of poor Christ, a man of grave judgement, said: Listen a little while. I will show you abundantly from the holy letters that the bread cannot be the body of Christ, because the bread is neither the natural, nor the glorified, nor the mystical body of Christ (the reasons set out above in the mention of Zwingli's booklet, which he entitled Subsidium de Eucharistia). After this debate with the scribe, the Senate decided that…

units.la: V literis, panem corpus Christi esse non posse: quia pa-nus neq; est corpus Christi naturale, neq; gloriosum, neq; mysticum (rationes supra expositæ in mentione libelli Zwinglii, quem subsidium de Eucharistia inscripsit.) Post conflictationem istā cum scriba habitam, statuit Senatus, ut à prandio Senatores quatuor cum Henrico Engelhardo, Leone, Megandro, Myconio, atq; nobiscum conveniant, quo res tanta graviter ventilaretur. Id vero ad hunc usum maximè fiebat, ut quibusdam obstrepentibus undique satisfieret. Deliberabatur aliquandiu variè, sed omnis deliberatio hunc exitum accepit, ut sequenti die duodecimo Aprilis ad Senatum universa causa iterum referretur. Cùm ergo duodecimâ Aprilis die ad Senatum redi-remus, atque ut Missa in universum aboleretur, ageremus, prodit denuo scriba iste, atque eandem cantilenam canit. Addit quidem sic docuisse, ut ista vox EST in præsentibus Christi verbis pro SIGNIFICAT posita sit, at agrè scripturæ testimoniis probavisse ad hunc modum accipi debere: Nam isti sermones: Semen est verbum Dei, Luc. 8. &, Ager est mundus, inimicus homo est Diabolus, &c. Matth. 13. ad hoc propositum nil faciût, Christus enim hic parabolicè loquutus sit, non etiam istic, cum dicit: Hoc est corpus meum. Cui breviter respondimus: Christum ista dixisse post finitam parabolam, quando tropicè quidem, sed tamen non amplius parabolicè loquebatur: differre enim tropum & parabolam: cumq; missâ contentione è Senatu nos recepissemus, sequutum est Senatus accredecretum totius Ecclesia nomine ad hunc fermē modum:
units.tr: ...from the sacred letters, that the bread cannot be the body of Christ: because bread is neither the natural, nor the glorified, nor the mystical body of Christ (the reasons set out above, in the mention of the little book by Zwingli which he titled a help on the Eucharist). After this contest with the scribe, the Senate decided that four senators, together with Henry Engelhard, Leo, Megander, Myconius, and ourselves, should meet after lunch, so that so great a matter might be thoroughly discussed. This was done chiefly so that satisfaction might be given to some who were making noise on every side. The matter was debated for some time in various ways, but every debate came to this outcome: that the whole case should be referred back to the Senate on the following day, 12 April. So when we returned to the Senate on 12 April, and were dealing with the abolition of the Mass as a whole, that scribe came forward again and sang the same tune. He added that he had taught that the word IS in Christ's present words is used in place of SIGNIFIES, but that he had poorly proved from the testimonies of Scripture that it must be understood in this way. For those sayings, "The seed is the word of God" (Luke 8) and "The field is the world, the enemy the devil," etc. (Matt. 13), do nothing for this point: for Christ spoke in parable there, but not here, when he says, "This is my body." To this we replied briefly: Christ said those things after the parable was finished, when he was speaking figuratively, but no longer in parable; for a trope and a parable differ. And when, with the dispute put aside, we had withdrawn from the Senate, the Senate's decree was issued in the name of the whole Church, to this effect:

units.la: Eucharistiâ, Deo volente, iuxta institutionem Christi, Apostolo- rumq; ritu posthac utiminor. In- firmis ac in fide adhuc rudioribus, fas esto hac vice tantūmodò ve- tere more uti. Missa in universum sic abolitâ, antiquata & ablegata esto, ut ne crastino quidem die repetatur.
units.tr: In the Eucharist, God willing, we shall from now on use the institution of Christ and the rite of the Apostles. For the weak and those still more untutored in faith, let it be permitted on this occasion only to use the old custom. Having thus abolished the Mass as a whole, let it be set aside, done away with and dismissed, so that it may not be repeated even on the following day.

units.la: Mox quod felix faustumq; sit, gratulata est tota Ecclesia, praeter paucos, nequid atrocius dicā, vel imbecilliores vel rudiores, qui in hanc lucem etiamnum adhuc dirigere nequibant. Restabat adhuc haud minimus conatus, quo scil. exempla proderemus, quae nulla cum parabola conjuncta forent. Coepimus ergo cogitare omnia, omnia revolvere attamen nihil aliud exemplorum occurrebat, quàm quod in commentario proditū est, aut quod occurrebat, erat illorū simile. Cū vero tredecima dies adpeteret (vera narro, adeoq; vera, ut celare volentem conscientia cogat effundere, quod Dominus imperiyt, non ignorans, quantis me cōtumelys, risibusq; exponā.) Cum inquā tredecimā Aprilis lux appeteret, visus sum mihi in somno multo cū tædio denuo contendere cum scriba, sicq; obmutuisse, ut q̃ verū scire, negāte linguā beneficiū suū ploqui nō possem: q̃me angor, ut solēt nōnūquam somnia fallaci ludere nocte (nihil enim alius quàm somnium narramus, quod ad nos attinet, tametsi leve non sit quod per somnium didicimus, gratia Deo, in cujus solius gloriam ista prodimus) vehementer turbare videbatur. Ibi ἀπὸ μηχανῆς visus est monitor adesse (ater an albus, nihil memini, somnium enim narro) qui diceret: Quin, ignave, respondes ei, quod Exodi 12. scribitur. Est enim Phase, hoc est, transitus Domini. Protinus ut hoc phasma visum est, expergefio, & è lecto exilio. Locum apud Septuaginta primum undiq; circumspicio, ac de eo coram tota concione pro virili differo: qui sermo ubi acceptus est, quemadmodum paulò post dicemus, omnibus sacrarum literarum candidatis, qui adhuc nonnihil propter parabola obstaculum harebant, omne nebulam discussit. Factum ģ est, ut tribus istis diebus, cœna Domini, Parasceves, & resurrectionis, tantum Pascha Christi celebratum sit, quantum ipse nūquam vidi, eorumģ numerus, qui ad allia ollasģ Aegyptias respectarent, opinione longè minor esset.
units.tr: Soon the whole Church, except a few (lest I say anything more harsh) who were weaker or more untutored and who still could not see the light, rejoiced at what was happy and fortunate. There remained still no small effort, namely to bring forward examples which were not connected with any parable. So we began to think, to go over everything, yet no other examples came to mind than those already published in the commentary, or any that came to mind were like them. But when the thirteenth day drew near (I tell true things, and so true that conscience compels one who wishes to hide them to pour out what the Lord has commanded, not unaware of how greatly I shall expose myself to insults and laughter), when, I say, the light of 13 April was approaching, I seemed to myself in sleep to be contending again with the scribe with great weariness, and to have fallen so silent that, though I knew the truth, my tongue, refusing, could not express its benefit; and this anguish, as dreams sometimes do in the deceptive night, seemed to disturb me greatly. (For I relate nothing but a dream, as far as concerns us, although what we learned through the dream is not slight, thanks be to God, to whose glory alone we publish these things.) Then, as a deus ex machina [ἀπὸ μηχανῆς], a monitor seemed to be present (whether dark or white, I do not remember, for I am relating a dream), who said: "Why, lazy one, do you not answer him with what is written in Exodus 12? For it is the Phase [Πάσχα], that is, the passing over of the Lord." As soon as this apparition was seen, I woke up and leapt out of bed. I first searched everywhere for the place in the Septuagint, and I spoke about it, as far as I could, before the whole congregation. When this discourse was received, as we shall say shortly, it dispelled all mist for all candidates of sacred letters who were still somewhat held back by the obstacle of the parable. As a result, in those three days, Maundy Thursday, Good Friday and Easter, Christ's Passover was celebrated to a degree I had never seen, and the number of those who looked back to the leeks and Egyptian pots was far smaller than expected.

units.la: Patroni oralis mäducationis corporis Christi, narratione istâ occasionem sibi oblatam esse putabant, Zwingliū & doctrinam ejus suggillandi. Jactatæ enim passim voces istæ: Zwvinglius in somnio primùm doctrinam suam didicit. Zwvinglius nescit, à quo spiritu doctrinam suam acceperit. Zwvinglio malus Damon doctrinam suam revelavit.
units.tr: The defenders of the oral eating of the body of Christ thought that this narrative offered them an occasion to disparage Zwinglius and his doctrine. For these phrases were bandied about everywhere: "Zwinglius first learned his doctrine in a dream." "Zwinglius does not know from what spirit he received his doctrine." "An evil demon revealed his doctrine to Zwinglius."

units.la: Quibus ab amicis Zwinglii responsum: injuriam fieri fratri suo, & contra historiae fidem ista in eum confingi. Nam ante hoc somnium edidisse Zwinglium epistolam ad Matthaeum Alberum: edidisse item libellum de vera & falsa religione, & in utroq; scripto suam de coena Domini sententiam exposuisse: Deinde nullius spiritus a Zwinglio mentione fieri, sed monitoris tantum, qui & homo esse potuerit, quemadmodum Ananias Paulo astiterit Act.9.12. Proverbium, albus an ater sit nescio, in hac ipsa narratione a Zwinglio de Scriba quoque fuisse usurpatum, & vim eius vel ex Erasmi adagiis notam esse: Praeterea tantum abesse, ut Zwinglius fassus sit, a malo Daemone sibi doctrinam de coena esse patefactam, ut contra palam profiteatur, Dominum sibi hoc impertiisse, quod in somnio didicit & se per conscientiam id celare non posse: Quod & inde evidens sit, quod monitor Zwinglii ipsi digitum intendit ad Dei verbum, eumq; in veritate ex scripturis confirmat, id quod spiritus malus nunquam facit: nec sequi, somnium divinum non esse, etsi nescierit, utrum monitor albus an ater fuerit, si quidem noctu albu ab atro nemo discreverit. Fuit etiam non nemo, qui istis Zwinglii adversariis in aurem insusurraret: meminissent quid Lutherus, pronuntiaturus, Romanu Episcopum esse Antichristum, de se scripserit: Mitto ecce acta mea acutius quàm speraverit Dominus legatus, edita, sed longè majora parturit mihi jam animus: NESCIO UNDE VENIANT ISTAE MEDITATIONES. Res ista necdum habet initium suum, meo judicio, tantum abest, ut finem sperare possint Romani Proceres. Mittam ad te nugas meas, ut videas, an rectè divinem: Antichristum illum verè, juxta Paulum in Romana curia regnare.
units.tr: To these, Zwingli's friends replied that an injury was being done to their brother, and that such things were invented against him contrary to the evidence of history. For before this dream, Zwingli had published a letter to Matthew Alber; he had also published a little book on the true and false religion, and in both writings he had set out his opinion on the Lord's Supper. Next, no spirit is mentioned by Zwingli, but only a monitor, who could also have been a man, just as Ananias stood by Paul (Acts 9:12). The proverb "I do not know whether he is white or black" was used by Zwingli in this very narrative about the scribe too, and its force is known even from the adages of Erasmus. Moreover, it is so far from the case that Zwingli confessed that his doctrine of the Supper was revealed to him by an evil demon, that on the contrary he openly professes that the Lord imparted this to him, which he learned in a dream, and that he could not in conscience conceal it. This is also evident from the fact that Zwingli's monitor pointed his finger at the word of God and confirms the truth from the Scriptures, which an evil spirit never does. Nor does it follow that the dream was not divine, even though he did not know whether the monitor was white or black, since indeed no one can distinguish white from black at night. There was also someone who whispered in the ear of these adversaries of Zwingli: they should remember what Luther wrote about himself, when he was about to declare the Roman bishop to be Antichrist: "Behold, I send you my writings, published more sharply than the lord legate hoped, but my mind is now bringing forth far greater things: I DO NOT KNOW WHENCE THESE MEDITATIONS COME. This matter has not yet begun, in my judgment, and the Roman magnates can hardly hope for its end. I shall send you my trifles, so that you may see whether I divine rightly: that Antichrist, truly, according to Paul, reigns in the Roman court."

units.la: Hoc eodem anno Tiguri lectio Biblica plurium linguarum in choro summæ ædis est inchoata, decimâ nonâ Junii. Zwinglius ab hoc voto exorsus est: Omnipotens, sempiterne, ac misericors Deus, cujus verbum lucerna est pedibus nostris, & lumen semitarum nostrarum, aperi & illumina mentes nostras: ut oracula tua pie & sancte intelligamus, & in illud, quod rectè intellexerimus, transformemur, quò majestati tua nulla ex parte displiceamus, per Iesum Christum, Dominum nostrum, Amen. Lectum deinde est a studioso quodam caput Biblicum, Latinè, quod idem mox Joannes Ceporinus Hebraicè, Zwinglius Græcè ex septuaginta interpretibus, postremò Pastor quidam Germanicè, legerunt & interpretati sunt. Quo facto, habitis iterum precibus, cætus est dimissus. Sed iste legendi & interpretandi Biblia ordo postea mutatus, & ratio lectionum Theologicarum ad consuetudinem aliarum Academiarum fuit conformata. Floruerunt autem Tiguri post Joannis Ceporini & Zwinglii obitum professores Theologi, Conradus Pellicanus, Theodorus Bibliander, Petrus Martyr, Josias Simlerus, Joannes Wolfius, Guilielmus Stuckius, Joannes Jacobus Frisius, Marcus Beumlerus. Hodie Scholae Tigurinae cathedram ornat vir eruditae doctrinae & plurium linguarum cognitionis laude clarissimus Caspar Waserus, qui pro amicitia nostra singulari, proque suo in Rempublicam Christianam studio, multum me in historiis Tigurinicis adjuvit.
units.tr: In this same year, at Zurich, a Biblical lecture on several languages was begun in the choir of the great church, on 19 June. Zwingli began with this prayer: "Almighty, eternal and merciful God, whose word is a lamp to our feet and a light to our paths, open and illumine our minds, that we may understand your oracles piously and holily, and be transformed into what we have rightly understood, so that in no way we may displease your majesty, through Jesus Christ, our Lord. Amen." Then a certain scholar read a chapter of the Bible in Latin; the same was then read and interpreted by John Ceporinus in Hebrew, by Zwingli in Greek from the Seventy, and finally by a certain minister in German. When this was done, after prayers had been offered again, the assembly was dismissed. But this order of reading and interpreting the Bible was later changed, and the method of theological lectures was conformed to the custom of the other academies. After the deaths of John Ceporinus and Zwingli, the theological teachers who flourished at Zurich were Conrad Pellicanus, Theodore Bibliander, Peter Martyr, Josias Simler, John Wolf, William Stuckius, John James Frisius, and Marcus Beumler. Today the chair of the Zurich school is adorned by Caspar Waser, a man most distinguished for the praise of learned teaching and for his knowledge of several languages, who, out of his singular friendship toward us and his zeal for the Christian commonwealth, has helped me greatly in my Zurich histories.

units.la: Tigurinorum exemplu imitati vicini Vitoduren-ses, abiecerunt & ipsi imagines, destruxerunt altaria, Missa, & quae illi affinia, abrogarunt.
units.tr: The Winterthurers, imitating the example of Zurich, also cast out their images, tore down the altars, and abolished the Mass and whatever was akin to it.

units.la: Forchemii, oppido Episcopi Bambergensis, Evangelizabat Joannes Crusius, qui paulo post captus & quinquaginta florenis multatus, Episcopatu eiectus est. Ceterum re me Theologiae studiosis non ingrata facturum existimo: si quibus ritibus, in administratione Baptismi & coenae Domini Ecclesiae nonnullae, sub initiu renati Evangelii usae sunt, paucis indicaro.
units.tr: At Forchheim, a town belonging to the Bishop of Bamberg, John Crusius preached the Gospel. Shortly afterwards he was arrested, fined fifty florins, and expelled from the bishopric. Moreover, I think I will do something not unwelcome to students of theology if I briefly indicate which rites some churches used at the beginning of the restored Gospel in the administration of Baptism and the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Nordlingensis Ecclesiae Pastores in libello quem inscripserunt: Renovatio Ecclesiae Nordlingensis de suo baptizandi ritu haec habent: Tingimus pueros, tingimus profectioris aetatis, non arcemus ab Ecclesia, qui pueros ad tingendum non offerunt, sed tantum manuum impositione & deprecatione Ecclesia Christo mediatori & servatori nostro commendant. Nullam aetatem praecepit baptismo Christus, sed neq; ulla vetuit. Baptizare jussit discipulos in nomine patris, filij & Spiritus S. Mat. ult. Asportari jussit infantes, increpans discipulos, qui prohiberent pronūtians horum esse regnum cælorū. Nunc autem nemo arbitror, arcebit à baptismo, qui regnum cœlestè donat, ut injurium sit, dogmate rem vitiare per se liberam. Et dum concilia tractamus, non ita repudianda esse arbitramur quæ Patres dicunt, ut etiam spiritum sanctum negemus. Placuit Carthaginensi Concilio baptismus infantium, liber, placet & nobis neminem cogimus, sed neminem etiā repellimus, in re nec præcepta, nec vetita. De oleo quo baptizandi unguntur, de sale, quo initiātur, de orationibus quibus adjurantur, librum facimus, ut vel ungantur, vel nō ungātur &c. Neq; protinus exclamamus, perdi animas unctione, eo quod Christus nō þceperit. Nō pditur ritib. anima, infidelitate pditur.
units.tr: The ministers of the church at Nördlingen, in a booklet they entitled Renovation of the Church of Nördlingen, say the following about their rite of baptizing: We baptize children, and we baptize those of riper age. We do not shut out from the Church those who do not offer their children for baptism, but they simply commend them to Christ our mediator and saviour by the laying on of hands and by prayer in the Church. Christ prescribed no age for baptism, but he forbade none. He commanded the disciples to baptize in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit (Matt. ult.). He ordered the infants to be brought to him, rebuking the disciples who forbade them and declaring that theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Now, I think no one will shut out from baptism the one who gives the heavenly kingdom, so that it would be wrong to spoil by a doctrine a matter that is free in itself. And while we are discussing the councils, we judge that what the Fathers say should not be rejected to such an extent that we deny the Holy Spirit as well. The Council of Carthage approved the baptism of infants, and it is free; we too approve it, we compel no one, but neither do we repel anyone, since in this matter there is neither command nor prohibition. Concerning the oil with which those to be baptized are anointed, the salt with which they are initiated, and the prayers with which they are exorcised, we make it a matter of free choice whether they are anointed or not, etc. Nor do we at once cry out that souls are lost through anointing because Christ did not command it. Souls are not lost through ceremonies; they are lost through unbelief.

units.la: Consimilem ferè ritū servavit Pacimō tánus Walshuti. Sic enim ille ad Oecolampadium hoc anno: Loco baptismatis ego curo cōvenire Ecclesiā, inducens infantulum, ac linguā vernaculā interpretor Evangeliū: Oblati sunt parvuli, &c. Matt. 19. Subinde impositio nomine orat tota Ecclesia flexis genibus pro parvulo, illum commendans in manus Christi, ut huic sit propitius, & oret pro eo. Si vero sunt parentes adhuc infirmi, qui volunt omnibus nervis baptizari prolem, hāc baptizo, in opere infirmus sum cū infirmiusculis ad tempus, dū erudiātur melius: sed in verbo nō cedo illis in minimo apiculo.
units.tr: The minister at Waldshut, Pacimontanus, kept a rite much like this. For he wrote to Oecolampadius this year as follows: Instead of baptism, I take care that the Church be gathered, bringing in the little infant, and I interpret the Gospel in the vernacular: "They brought young children" (Matt. 19.). Then, after the laying on of hands, the whole Church kneels and prays for the little child, commending him into the hands of Christ, that he may be gracious to him and may pray for him. But if the parents are still weak, and they wish with all their strength to have their offspring baptized, I baptize them. In practice I am weak with the weaker ones for a time, until they are better taught; but in the Word I yield to them not the smallest jot.

units.la: Oecolampadio supra modū placebat hicritus, ideoq; optabat, ut omnib. arrideret. Tum enim nondum illi occurrerant loci in scripturis, qui
units.tr: This rite pleased Oecolampadius beyond measure, and he therefore wished that it might be acceptable to everyone. For the passages of Scripture which compel the bringing forward of infant baptism had not yet occurred to him

units.la: Ibidem. qui cogant ad afferendum pædobaptismum. Sed nec video, inquit, quid prohibeat. Et durum fuerit infantibus salutis subsidia negari.
units.tr: Ibid. who compel the bringing forward of infant baptism. But I do not see, he says, what forbids it. And it would be harsh to deny infants the aids of salvation.

units.la: Consuetudinem communionis sacræ in Ecclesia Nordlingensi tum observatam Theobaldus Billicanus describit. Convenimus, ait, ad docendum, ad audiendum verbum Domini, atq; hic cognitionem cœlestium beneficiorum exercemus, ut sunt mortificatio veteris Adæ, vivificatio interioris hominis, communicatio spiritûs regenerantis & formantis nos, consolatio conscientiæ per Christum, spes futuræ vitæ cum Christo, charitas in fratres, in amicos, inimicos. Porrò & ad psallendum & ad Deo gratias agendum communiter confluimus, tum communicamus pane & vino Domini, non coacti, sed volentes, ferentes immensis laudibus & spiritualibus hymnis gloriam gratiæ Dei patris in Iesu Christo factam, qui remisso peccato, purgatos sacrificio Christi sui fecerit nos communiter haeredes regni cœlestis & cives suos. Ita memoriam Christi celebramus, & charitatem, ut cives regni Christi decet, fovemus, ut communicantes uno pane & uno poculo, corpore & sanguine Domini, confiteamur & cognoscamus nos regni cœlestis unanimes haeredes. Si qui non communicant in mensa, tamen bonis cœlestibus, iustitiâ Dei & charitate communicantes, non arcentur à consuetudine: quanquam malimus omnes in Domino fratres iuxta Christi verbum etiam in externa cœna accumbere.
units.tr: Theobald Billican describes the custom of sacred communion then observed in the church at Nördlingen. We meet, he says, to teach and to hear the Word of the Lord, and here we exercise the knowledge of heavenly benefits: the mortification of the old Adam, the quickening of the inner man, the communication of the Spirit who regenerates and forms us, the consolation of conscience through Christ, the hope of future life with Christ, and love towards brothers, friends, and enemies. Moreover, we gather together in common both to sing psalms and to give thanks to God. Then we share in the bread and wine of the Lord, not under compulsion but willingly, offering with immense praises and spiritual hymns the glory of the grace of God the Father in Jesus Christ, who, by forgiving sin and cleansing us by the sacrifice of his Christ, has made us jointly heirs of the heavenly kingdom and his citizens. Thus we celebrate the memory of Christ and cherish charity, as befits citizens of the kingdom of Christ, so that by sharing in one bread and one cup, the body and blood of the Lord, we confess and acknowledge that we are united heirs of the heavenly kingdom. If some do not communicate at the table, yet sharing in heavenly goods, the righteousness of God and charity, they are not excluded from our fellowship; although we would prefer that all, as brothers in the Lord, according to Christ's word, should also recline at the external supper.

units.la: ARGENTINÆ hoc anno Forma celebrandæ cœnæ Dominicæ excusa est, in qua inter alia & hæc leguntur: In dargebung des brods vnd des kelchs des Herren / spricht der Diener also: Gedenckt/ glaubet/ verkündiget/ daß Christus für euch gestorben ist: hoc est: In exhibitione panis & calicis Dominici, Minister verbi ita alloquitur sumentes: Mementote, credite, annuntiate, Christum pro vobis esse mortuum.
units.tr: At Strasbourg this year a form for celebrating the Lord's Supper was printed, in which, among other things, these words are read: In the giving of the bread and the cup of the Lord the minister speaks thus: Remember, believe, proclaim that Christ died for you. That is: In the giving of the bread and cup of the Lord, the minister of the Word addresses the communicants thus: Remember, believe, proclaim that Christ was dead for you.

units.la: TIGURINORUM ritus huiusmodi est: Finitâ concione mensa templo infertur, & mundâ mappâ sternitur. Huic imponitur canistrum pane infermentato plenum, catini & pocula lignea, quæ vino implentur. Accedit ad mensam Pastor Ecclesiæ cum Diaconis, & totum cœtum ad attentionem excitat. Mox alter ex Diaconis subjicit institutionem cœnæ Domini ex epistola ad Corinthios: alter verò recitat partem capitis sexti Joannis, ut ex verbis Domini omnes discant: quomodo Christi carnem edamus verè, & sanguinem eius verè bibamus. Mox recitato symbolo fidei, Pastor admonet, ut quisque seipsum examinet & exploret: ne indignè accedendo corporis & sanguinis Domini reus fiat. Postea omnes se in genua demittunt, & pastore præeunte, orationem Dominicam dicunt. Quâ absolutâ pastor panem infermentatum accipit in manus, & spectante fidelium cœtu alta voce, vocc, voce, magna religione recitat institutionem cœnæ Dominicæ: deinde panem ministris distribuit & poculū porrigit. Qui panem in catinis & vinum in cyathis circumferunt, & Ecclesiæ exhibent. Quisq; in manus sumit quod traditur à ministris, edit, & proximè assidenti offert partem eius quod accepit, similiter etiam poculū porrigit. Interim verò dū de pane Domini edunt & de poculo eius bibunt, unus ex Ecclesiæ ministris prælegit ex Evangelio Joannis dulcissima illa colloquia Domini, quę abiturus cum discipulis habuit, à pedum ablutione initium faciens. Si catini & poculum ad mensam redeūt, Ecclesia iterum in genua procumbit, & Deo gratias agit pro beneficio redemptionis Christi. In Ecclesiis autem agri Tigurini, minister omnia solus recitat, & ad mensam singuli accedunt. Hunc ritum multæ Ecclesiæ in Helvetia & Rhetia postea imitatæ sunt.
units.tr: The rite of the Zurich churches is of this kind. When the sermon is finished, the table is brought into the church and laid with a clean cloth. On it is set a basket full of unleavened bread, and wooden dishes and cups, which are filled with wine. The minister of the church comes to the table with the deacons and rouses the whole assembly to attention. Then one of the deacons reads the institution of the Lord's Supper from the letter to the Corinthians; another reads part of the sixth chapter of John, so that everyone may learn from the words of the Lord how we truly eat the flesh of Christ and truly drink his blood. Then, after the creed has been recited, the minister urges each to examine and test himself, lest by coming unworthily he become guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. Afterwards everyone kneels down, and with the minister leading, they say the Lord's Prayer. When this is finished, the minister takes the unleavened bread into his hands and, with the assembly of the faithful watching, recites the institution of the Lord's Supper in a loud voice, with great reverence. Then he distributes the bread to the ministers and hands round the cup. They carry the bread around in dishes and the wine in cups, and present them to the congregation. Each takes in his hand what is handed to him by the ministers, eats it, and offers a part of what he has received to the person sitting next to him; he likewise passes on the cup. Meanwhile, as they eat of the bread of the Lord and drink from his cup, one of the ministers of the church reads aloud from the Gospel of John those most sweet conversations of the Lord which he held with his disciples when about to depart, beginning with the washing of feet. When the dishes and the cup have returned to the table, the congregation again kneels and gives thanks to God for the benefit of Christ's redemption. In the churches of the Zurich countryside, however, the minister alone recites everything, and the individuals come up to the table. Many churches in Helvetia and Rhaetia afterwards imitated this rite.

units.la: WITTEMBERGÆ hoc anno exeunte demum lingua Teutonica celebrare Missam, & cœnam Domini administrare Dominica XX. post Trinitatis cœperunt. Cùm paulò ante Lutherus tanquā Orpheus Germaniæ verus, summā doctrinæ Christianæ, & partes Catechismi omnes, & præcipuorū Symboli articulorū ac Festorū historias, preces ad Deum, consolationes & gratiarū actiones, Germanicis carminibus seu odis numerosè & cōcinnè scrisententias rythmis inclusas verbis elegantibus, & congruente sententiis ac verbis harmoniâ seu vocis modulatione, eundem in animis motum & adfectum, quem sententiae ac verba requirunt, in animis canentium inprimente, edidisset, ut à vulgo etiam literarum rudi, facilius disci doctrinae Christianae summa, & preces, ac consolationes divinae, & fidelius memoriâ retineri ac propagari possent, ac in mentes & corda audientium, adiutae numeris ac harmoniis Musicis, altius penetrarent, & pios motus & adfectus verbis respondentes, in eis accenderent ac inflammarent.
units.tr: At Wittenberg, at the end of this year, they at last began to celebrate the Mass in the German tongue and to administer the Lord's Supper on the twentieth Sunday after Trinity. Shortly before this, Luther, like a true Orpheus of Germany, had published, in German songs or odes, with harmonious and elegant verse, the whole sum of Christian doctrine and all the parts of the Catechism, the histories of the chief articles of the Creed and of the festivals, prayers to God, consolations and thanksgivings, the sentences being enclosed in rhythms, and by a harmony of words and sentences and a modulation of the voice, impressing upon the minds of those who sang the same emotion and feeling which the sentences and words require. This was so that the sum of Christian doctrine and the prayers and divine consolations might be learned more easily even by the unlettered common people and retained and spread more faithfully in memory, and so that, aided by the rhythms and the musical harmonies, they might penetrate more deeply into the minds and hearts of hearers and kindle and inflame in them pious movements and feelings answering to the words.

units.la: Porrò quam Reges, Principes, Comites, Urbes, amplexae sunt hoc anno religionem puram, abolitis Papisticis, introductis Evangelicis ritibus: eius veritatem aliquot Martyres sanguine roborârunt.
units.tr: Furthermore, in this year, as kings, princes, counts, and cities embraced the pure religion, with the Papistical rites abolished and the Evangelical rites introduced, several martyrs confirmed its truth with their blood.

units.la: JACOBUS PAVANAS Bolonienfis superiori anno propter religionis sincerae prosessionem captus, metu mortis palinodiam cecinerat. Hoc vero anno resumptis novis viribus cùm fidem puram, præsertim de coena Domini, palàm doceret, ex voto suo vivus crematur Lutetiae summa cum animi alacritate, fidem faciens proverbio, Vir fugiens denuò pugnabit.
units.tr: James Pavanas of Bologna, who the previous year had been arrested for professing the sincere religion, had recanted through fear of death. But this year, having resumed his strength, he openly taught the pure faith, especially concerning the Lord's Supper, and so, in fulfilment of his vow, he was burned alive at Paris with great cheerfulness of spirit, bearing out the proverb: A man who flees will fight again.

units.la: VVOLFGANGUS Schuch Germanus in oppidum Lotharingiae à S. Hippolyto denominatum venit, Christum docet, Pastor Ecclesiæ declaratur: Quadragesimæ observationem, Imagines atque Idola, Missamque adeo ipsam abolet. Accusatur populus ad Ducem Lotharingiæ defectionis: Dux se urbem flammâ & ferro vastaturum minatur. VVolffgangus primùm epistolâ se purgat ad Ducem: deinde sua sponte se Nanceum confert fidei confessionem editurus, & cives S. Hippollyti periculo liberaturus. Sed statim in carcerem durum & graveolentem derruditur, post ad ignem damnatur: qua sententiâ audità orsus est psalmum centesimum vigesimum secundum: Lætatus sum in his quæ dicta sunt mihi, in domum Domini ibimus. In ipsis flammis psalmum quinquagesimum primum cecinit, obiitque die decimâ nonâ Augusti. Memorabile est: Judicem Ecclesiasticum huius Schuchii & eius asseclam, Abbatem clari loci paulò post subitaneâ morte exstinctos fuisse. Ipse Dux Antonius Lotharingus aulicis suis persuadere conabatur: satis esse ad salutem, scire Pater noster, & Ave Maria.
units.tr: Wolfgang Schuch, a German, came to the town in Lorraine named after St Hippolytus, taught Christ, and was appointed minister of the church there. He abolished the observance of Lent, images and idols, and the Mass itself. The people were accused to the Duke of Lorraine of rebellion, and the Duke threatened to lay the town waste with fire and sword. Wolfgang first cleared himself by a letter to the Duke. Then, of his own accord, he went to Nancy, intending to publish a confession of faith and to save the citizens of St Hippolytus from danger. But at once he was thrown into a harsh and foul-smelling prison, and afterwards condemned to the fire. When he heard the sentence, he began Psalm 122: I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord. In the flames themselves he sang Psalm 51, and he died on 19 August. It is remarkable that the ecclesiastical judge who had dealt with this Schuch, and his associate, the abbot of a famous place, were soon afterwards carried off by sudden death. Duke Antony of Lorraine himself tried to persuade his courtiers that it was enough for salvation to know the Lord's Prayer and the Ave Maria.

units.la: In Helvetia Suitenses sacrificulum quendam, quod ex Scripturis Papatum impugnasset, itemque nautam quendam Eberlinum Bolthium, quod de Baptismo & cœna sacra, paulò aliter ac Monachi in Papatu loquuntur. loquutus esset, combusserunt, utriq; Anabaptismi haeresi affictâ.
